Alamance County by the numbers

How is property tax set up for a house seller in Alamance County?

A single county department handles listing, valuation and collection of taxes on everything taxable. The department is at 124 W. Elm St. in Graham, open weekdays from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., and its phone line is (336) 228-1312.

The county was formed in 1849 from part of Orange County and covers about 434 square miles. Graham is the seat and Burlington is the largest community. The towns of Elon, Haw River, Green Level, Ossipee, Swepsonville and Alamance, plus parts of Mebane and Gibsonville, fall inside the county. Textile mills along the Haw River drove its early growth.

Four things shape a sale here: the January 1 listing date, the September 1 due date, the 2027 revaluation, and a delinquent tax check at recording. Each gets its own section below.

What is the Alamance County property tax calendar?

Land Records explains that each parcel is listed to whoever owned it on January 1, and that date fixes the tax year. Statements go out in July, and the county charges no interest on a payment made by January 5.

Alamance County tax calendar and relief deadlines
DateWhat happens
January 1Listing date; owner on this day is billed
January 1 to 31Filing window for present-use and exemption applications
June 1Deadline for elderly, disabled, circuit breaker and disabled veteran relief
JulyBills mailed
September 1Bills due
January 5Last day to pay with no interest
January 6Delinquent; 2% interest added, then 0.75% on the sixth of each later month

A purchase that closes after January 1 can still produce a bill in the previous owner's name, even though the deed is recorded and the county has updated its record. Getting the mailing address corrected before July is the surest way to receive the bill on time.

Payment options are by mail (counted by postmark), in an indoor or outdoor drop box (credited as of the drop date), or online with a convenience fee. Registered vehicles are billed separately by the state through Tag and Tax Together at registration renewal.

What is happening with the 2027 revaluation in Alamance County?

Alamance County is revaluing every parcel effective January 1, 2027, and notices of value are scheduled to be mailed February 15, 2027. The last revaluation took effect January 1, 2023. North Carolina requires reappraisal at least every eight years under G.S. 105-286, and the county has chosen a four-year cycle.

Vincent Valuations, which assisted with the 2023 work, is performing the 2027 appraisal. Staff spend roughly two years in the field checking property features, comparing sales, and noting improvements. The county says its goal is to reach, or come close to, 100% of market value at revaluation.

A bigger number on the notice need not produce a bigger bill. County staff say rates fall as values rise, and a revenue neutral rate would keep the typical owner near last year's payment. Parcels that gained more than the average pay more, while laggards pay less.

If you plan to sell in 2027, open the notice the day it arrives. Your appeal period runs from its date, and late filings are generally turned away. The revaluation hotline is the same number as the tax department, (336) 228-1312.

How do I appeal a property value in Alamance County?

County appraisers hear informal reviews first. If that does not settle things, the matter moves to the Board of Equalization and Review. Filing windows differ by property type.

  • Real property: during the annual listing period, with documentation such as sales, photos, repair estimates or an appraisal.
  • Business and individual personal property: thirty days from the notice of value.
  • Registered vehicles: thirty days after the due date shown on the combined tag and tax notice.

The state outlines what comes next. The local board starts deliberating about the first week of April and allots each side a fixed time. A losing owner can go to the Property Tax Commission in Raleigh, a trial-style body that follows evidence rules and puts the burden on the taxpayer.

The county lists three typical grounds: a value above likely sale price, wrong square footage or condition on the record, and nearby sales pointing lower. It supplies a comparable sales tool and a property record search to help you gather proof.

What tax relief programs can Alamance County homeowners use?

June 1 is the usual filing deadline, and income caps change yearly, so get current figures from the tax department. An online eligibility calculator on the county site covers four of the programs.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: a seniors-and-disabled benefit that shelters the larger of $25,000 or half the home's taxable value, subject to an income cap.
  • Circuit breaker deferral: postpones part of the tax on a permanent residence, scaled to income. Eligible owners are 65 or older, or disabled, with five years of ownership and residence behind them.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: shelters the first $45,000 of assessed value for an honorably discharged veteran with a total, permanent service-connected disability, or for a surviving spouse. Age and income do not matter.
  • Present-use value: taxes qualifying farm, horticulture and forestry land on its use, but taxes deferred for the previous three years can be recaptured if the land leaves the program.

An owner who sells while a deferral or present-use status is in place should ask about payoff or recapture amounts before agreeing to a closing date.

What does Alamance County check about taxes when a deed is recorded?

The Register of Deeds states that every deed recorded after May 2, 2011, except timber deeds and releases, must go before the county Tax Department for delinquent tax certification first. That step follows G.S. 161-31(b). A seller with back taxes should plan to clear them so the certification can be issued.

After recording, the change reaches the property record through a short chain. The Register of Deeds keeps the document and gives it a book and page number. Land Records staff review it, change the owner name and mailing address, and push the update to the online record and GIS map. A simple sale of an existing parcel moves faster than a split or a new subdivision. If you do not see the change after several weeks, call Land Records with the book and page number.

If an owner has died, the county follows the estate file at the Clerk of Superior Court or recorded documents. Bills stay due on schedule meanwhile, and staff ask for the estate file number, the parcel number or address, and a mailing address.

Which housing figures stand out in Alamance County?

The 2020 count was 171,415 residents, and the July 2025 estimate of 186,177 is 8.6% above the 2020 base. Houses carry a $241,500 median value for 2020 to 2024, owners live in 65.0% of homes, and the county has 70,062 households. Median gross rent was $1,064 and median household income was $65,651.

Builders took out 2,027 permits in 2025. Poverty stood at 13.8%, and workers averaged 25.9 minutes of travel to work.

Look up your own parcel in the county property record search before you pick an asking price.

More questions about Alamance County, NC Property Tax Guide

When are Alamance County property taxes due?

They are due September 1. Interest does not start until January 6, so a bill paid by January 5 carries none. After that, 2% is added, plus 0.75% on the sixth of each following month.

Whose name is on the bill after an early-year purchase?

A bill can still arrive under the prior owner's name, because the county lists parcels to the January 1 owner. Divide the cost at closing and fix the mailing address before July.

When will new values from the 2027 revaluation arrive?

Notices of value are scheduled to be mailed February 15, 2027, for the January 1, 2027 effective date. Your appeal deadline is tied to the date on that notice.

What is the deadline for tax relief programs in Alamance County?

June 1 for the elderly or disabled exclusion, the circuit breaker deferral and the disabled veteran exclusion. Present-use and exemption filings fall in the January listing window.

Who do I call at Alamance County Tax Administration?

Call (336) 228-1312 or visit 124 W. Elm St. in Graham, weekdays from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. The same number handles revaluation questions.

Which Avery County office handles property tax?

The Avery County Tax Administrator's office, at 200 Montezuma Street in Newland, keeps the property records, sets assessments and bills the taxes. It runs two divisions: assessment at 828-733-8214 and collections at 828-733-8228.

Mail for the assessor goes to PO Box 305, Newland, NC 28657, and collection mail goes to PO Box 355 in the same town. The office hours quoted on the county's revaluation page are 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. An online lookup covers real estate, sales and tax bills, and a separate viewer shows tax maps.

One caution printed on the tax office page: the records and maps exist for valuation, and the legal description of a parcel is whatever the recorded deed says. Buyers and sellers should read the recorded deed instead of trusting a map line.

What is the Avery County tax rate?

For tax years 2023 through 2025 the county page prints a county rate of 0.335, a fire rate of 0.065 and a total of 0.40. The rate page shows no unit, so ask the tax office how to apply it to a bill.

Towns that levy their own tax add a separate municipal rate. The county publishes them with a code for each town, and those 2025 rates are in the table.

Avery County city tax codes and rates for 2025, as printed by the county tax office
CodeTownRate
01Banner Elk0.46
02Beech Mountain0.65
03Crossnore0.30
04Elk Park0.30
06Newland0.56
07Seven Devils0.47
08Sugar Mountain0.28

The county rate and the fire rate apply to every parcel, and the town rate applies where a town levies one, so ask the tax office which codes your parcel carries. Ten fire districts cover the county: Banner Elk, Crossnore, Elk Park, Fall Creek, Green Valley, Linville, Newland, Frank, Beech Mountain and Seven Devils.

When did Avery County last revalue property?

Values now in force were set as of January 1, 2022, and notices went out in March of that year. Counties must reappraise real property at least once in eight years, and Avery describes the goal as tax value that matches what a willing buyer and seller would agree on.

Avery did the work with its own staff instead of hiring an outside appraisal firm, and it says it took advice from outside sources on the schedule of values and on commercial property. The county's revaluation guide includes a sales ratio table. For houses it lists 344 sales at a 91 percent ratio in 2018, 430 sales at 83 percent in 2019, 699 sales at 71 percent in 2020 and 675 sales at 60 percent in 2021. A ratio of 100 percent would mean tax value equals sale price,, so the 60 percent figure for 2021 houses shows how far values had drifted from sale prices before the 2022 reset.

The same guide says a lower value does not follow from owning a house for decades. The statute requires uniform appraisal, so a long-held home is valued like comparable homes that sold recently.

How can an Avery County owner appeal a value?

First use the informal review named on the value notice, which is not an appeal. Use it to correct facts on your record, learn how the number was built and compare similar parcels. If you remain unhappy, ask in writing for a formal hearing.

Avery staffs its appeal board with appointed taxpaying citizens rather than commissioners, and that board sits between the first Monday of April and the first Monday of May. For the 2026 tax year its first meeting was Monday, April 13, requests had to arrive by final adjournment on Monday, May 4 at 3:00 p.m., and the county asked for appeal forms by April 28 so hearings could be scheduled. Sessions begin at 9:00 a.m. in courthouse Conference Room 106.

  • Pick up the application at the assessor's office or download it from the county site.
  • Bring record cards and sale prices for similar parcels nearby.
  • The question before the board is whether the value is accurate and fair. Ability to pay is outside its scope.

A further appeal goes to the Property Tax Commission, by notice within 30 days of the board's mailed decision.

What tax relief can Avery County homeowners claim?

The county lists three state programs plus a farm program, and a single owner gets only one of the first three. Pick up forms from the tax department and return them to the assessor by June 1.

  • Age 65 or disability exclusion: shelters the larger of $25,000 or half the appraised value of a permanent home, with income capped at $38,800 for 2026.
  • Circuit breaker deferment: limits the bill to 4 percent of income when income is at or under $38,800 and to 5 percent when it is at or under $58,200 (2026 figures). The excess is deferred and carried as a lien, and you reapply annually.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: removes up to $45,000 of appraised value without an age or income test; an unmarried surviving spouse may also qualify.
  • Present use value: farmers with active income from land can ask the office for a list of criteria and an application.

Deferred taxes matter in a sale. When a circuit breaker owner transfers the property, the last three years of deferred taxes come due with interest on the transfer date.

What does the Avery County listing period require?

Owners list taxable property during January, and the county says the duty is solely on the taxpayer even if a form never arrives. For 2026 the county asked for returns by March 2.

Items to list include untagged motor vehicles and motor homes, multi-year tagged trailers, improvements to real estate, income-producing personal property, business equipment, single-wide mobile homes, furnished rental property, and airplanes, boats and motors. Listing time is also when relief applications are taken.

State law gives the commissioners power to extend the period by up to 30 days in a non-revaluation year, and an individual with good cause can file a written request for more time before the regular period ends, though no extension runs past April 15.

How do Avery County taxes work when you sell?

Bills fall due September 1 and carry no interest until January 6, when 2 percent applies; after February 1 three-quarters of a percent accrues per month. Because the lien attaches on the listing date, an unpaid bill stays with the parcel through a sale.

Census data shows how big the stakes are: median owner-occupied value is $265,800, 83.0 percent of homes are owner-occupied and the county has 14,597 housing units against 6,791 households. With so many seasonal homes, bills often go to a second address, so make sure the tax office has a current mailing address. Get the exact balance from collections and hand it to the closing attorney so the bill is paid out of the proceeds.

More questions about Avery County, NC Property Tax Guide

How do I reach the Avery County tax office?

Assessment is 828-733-8214 and collections is 828-733-8228. Visit 200 Montezuma Street in Newland; the revaluation page gives hours as 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

What was the Avery County tax rate for 2025?

The county page prints 0.335 for county tax and 0.065 for fire tax, which totals 0.40. Towns add their own rate, from 0.28 in Sugar Mountain to 0.65 in Beech Mountain.

When is the Avery County revaluation?

The latest took effect January 1, 2022. The eight-year statutory limit means another one is due within that span, and the tax office page is where the schedule will appear.

How do I appeal my Avery County property value?

Ask the tax office for an informal review first, then file the written hearing application before the appeal board adjourns. In 2026 adjournment was May 4 at 3:00 p.m.

Can I get a break on Avery County property tax if I am 65 or disabled?

Yes, when income stays within the 2026 limit of $38,800. The exclusion shelters the larger of $25,000 or half the value, and the assessor must receive the form by June 1.

Cash Home Buyers in North Carolina

  • Bertie County, NC Property Tax Guide: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is
  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Bertie County, NC Property Tax Guide sale

Selling in Bertie County? Get a Cash Offer

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Bertie County?

Who sends the tax bill and keeps the parcel maps in Bertie County?

Tax Collections and Tax Mapping works out of 106 Dundee Street in Windsor, one department for both jobs. The tax line, (252) 794-5310, takes bill and payment questions. The mapping line, (252) 794-5311, covers parcels, maps and ownership by street address.

The county website's Online Services menu links to a tax bill payment page and a real property search. The register of deeds indexes by name only, so a buyer or seller who starts with an address should start with the mapping line.

  • Bills and payments: (252) 794-5310
  • Parcels, maps and address lookups: (252) 794-5311
  • Recording and deed indexes: our Bertie County register of deeds page

What kind of county is Bertie, and how does that affect a sale?

Bertie covers 741 square miles of farm and timber land, and Windsor, established in 1766, has been the county seat since 1774. Eight towns are incorporated: Askewville, Aulander, Colerain, Kelford, Lewiston-Woodville, Powellsville, Roxobel and Windsor. The 2020 census counted 17,934 people countywide and 3,582 in Windsor.

Fertile uplands and lowlands share the county with large swamps called pocosins, and timber, livestock and broiler chickens anchor the economy. QuickFacts shows a shrinking population: 17,086 in mid-2025 against 17,933 in the April 2020 base.

Of 9,116 housing units, 72.7% sit in the Census's owner-occupied rate. The typical value for 2020 to 2024 was $98,500, compared with $332,700 for the country, and builders pulled 32 permits in 2025. At that price level a back-tax bill is a large slice of any sale, so clear the tax record before you list. The Census puts median household income at $48,750 and the poverty rate at 20.1%.

Land records here carry a notice required by state law: any tract within half a mile of a farm in a voluntary agricultural district is flagged, so a buyer researching title sees the farm next door.

When was Bertie County last revalued, and when is the next one?

Bertie's values date from January 1, 2020, and NCDOR's schedule puts the next reappraisal in 2028, inside the eight-year ceiling.

Between reappraisals a value moves mostly with building, demolition or rezoning. A house priced off 2020 schedules may land far from what a buyer will pay now. The tax department posts a locational sales report for each year from 2012 through 2025. Read the one for your area, and request your property record card, before you argue a value.

Neighboring counties are on different clocks, as the table below shows, so a Bertie seller comparing rates with a Hertford or Martin listing is looking at values from different years. Since the lien runs from the January 1 listing date, an inflated number costs money on every bill until 2028 arrives.

How does the Bertie County tax rate compare with nearby counties?

The Department of Revenue's 2024-25 schedule lists Bertie at $.9300 per $100, the top figure among the six counties below. The county board picks the rate each year, and a town levy rides on top inside town limits.

County tax rate per $100 and reappraisal years, 2024-25 (NC Department of Revenue, August 2024)
CountyRateLast reappraisalNext scheduled
Bertie.930020202028
Hertford.840020192027
Northampton.830020232031
Martin.810020172025
Washington.850020212029
Halifax.700020242028

The table is a 2024-25 snapshot, so take the live rate from your current bill.

What does late payment of a Bertie County tax bill cost?

The due date is September 1, and interest waits until January 6, when 2% attaches. After February 1, every month or fraction of a month adds three-fourths of a percent more. Mailed checks count as paid on the postmark date.

A bill that stays open can lead to a court action modeled on mortgage foreclosure, ending in a public auction where the high bidder may have to put down as much as 20%. Redemption stays open until the court confirms the sale, and it costs the full tax plus penalties, interest and costs. A house sale that closes in that window settles everything.

Bertie also sells county-owned parcels by the upset bid method under G.S. 160A-269. An offer comes with a 5% deposit, a notice runs in the newspaper, and anyone can top the offer within 10 days by 10% of the first $1,000 plus 5% of the rest. The board can reject any offer.

Which tax relief can a Bertie County homeowner claim?

Three state programs lower the tax on a primary home, and one application serves all three. An owner gets only one. Bertie's tax page also hosts a physician certificate form for disability claims a motor vehicle exemption form and a general exemption application.

Relief matters here because QuickFacts counts 26.9% of residents as 65 or older, so the elderly exclusion and the circuit breaker can reach a large share of owners. Each owner still has to meet the income test on the application.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: takes off $25,000 or 50% of appraised value, whichever is greater, for an owner who is 65 or older or who is totally and permanently disabled. NCDOR prints $38,800 as the 2026 income cap.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: takes off the first $45,000, with no age or income question. The veteran needs a permanent and total disability tied to service, and a surviving spouse who has not remarried can claim it too.
  • Circuit breaker: caps each year's tax at 4% of income, rising to 5% for incomes between the cap and 1.5 times it. Whatever exceeds the cap is deferred and stays as a lien.

Applications go to the county assessor. January is the usual window, and a late filing is still taken through June 1.

What does a Bertie County seller owe on the tax side at closing?

Back and current bills are paid from the seller's proceeds. A payoff letter from the tax office gives the closing attorney a firm number.

An owner in the circuit breaker program has one more charge, because a sale ends eligibility and the last three years of deferred tax come due with interest.

The seller also bears the state deed tax, $1.00 for every $500 of value or part of $500, and it is paid to the register before the deed is filed. Bertie's recording resolution adds a requirement: put a return name and address and the buyer's permanent mailing address on the first page of each instrument.

Inherited title, tenants and deferred repairs leave all of this unchanged. Lien payoffs look the same for a financed buyer as for a cash buyer, and selling as-is does not lift a lien before closing.

More questions about Bertie County, NC Property Tax Guide

Where is the Bertie County tax office?

It works out of the county office building at 106 Dundee Street in Windsor. Phone (252) 794-5310 for bills and (252) 794-5311 for maps and parcel lookups.

What county tax rate does Bertie charge?

NCDOR's schedule for 2024-25 lists .9300 per $100, the highest of the six counties in the table above. The rate for the current year is on your bill, and a town levy is added inside town limits.

When does Bertie County revalue next?

NCDOR shows 2028, eight years after the January 1, 2020 reappraisal. A county may go sooner, but none may go longer.

What is the cutoff to challenge a Bertie County value?

The deadline is the day the county board of equalization and review adjourns. If its notice was mailed with fewer than 15 days left, you get 15 days from the mailing. The board opens between the first Monday in April and the first Monday in May and mails rulings within a month. From there, a Property Tax Commission appeal is due 30 days after the ruling is mailed.

Can I buy a county-owned parcel in Bertie County?

Yes, through the upset bid method. You submit a written offer with a 5% deposit to the county manager's office at 106 Dundee Street, the commissioners act on it, and a newspaper notice opens a 10-day window for higher bids. A higher bid must add 10% of the first $1,000 and 5% of the rest, and the board may reject any offer.

How do you reach Bladen County Tax Administration?

Tax Administration sits at 201 E King Street in Elizabethtown, and walk-in hours run weekdays from 8:30 to 5:00. Letters go to PO Box 385, Elizabethtown, NC 28337. Phone 910-862-6730 or write to bctax@bladenco.org.

An online portal shows bills and takes payments, and an automated line at 1-877-369-0025 takes payments by phone. The county's property record search is a separate tool, and the FAQ points owners to bladen.ustaxdata.com for prior-year assessments.

The 2026 tax year brought a change: the county now collects for four towns, East Arcadia, Bladenboro, White Lake and Elizabethtown. Owners inside those towns should ask Tax Administration how the town portion appears on the bill.

What is Bladen County like, and what does that mean for a seller?

The county describes itself as a Coastal Plain county in southeastern North Carolina, about 879 square miles, which makes it the fourth largest in the state. The Cape Fear River bisects it, White Lake is commercially developed for visitors, and Jones and Singletary Lakes are state parks.

QuickFacts lists 30,007 people for July 2025. That is 1.3% above the 2020 base, yet far below the 35,190 of 2010. Home values are modest: the 2020 to 2024 median for owner-occupied homes is $135,100, versus $332,700 for the nation. Owners hold 69.2% of the housing stock by the Census rate, median gross rent is $773, and the county issued 97 building permits in 2025.

The county names food processing, manufacturing and assembly, textiles, chemicals and agribusiness as its industry base, with workforce training at Bladen Community College. Against a $135,100 median, even a small back-tax or title problem looms large.

Did Bladen County's 2026 revaluation change my 2026 tax bill?

No. The General Assembly postponed Bladen's new values by a year, so 2026 bills use the older 2025 values and the 2026 reappraisal values first apply for the 2027 tax year.

The county completed a reappraisal as of January 1, 2026, with a contracted appraisal firm, and mailed notices to all real property owners on March 9, 2026. The reappraisal before that dated from 2022. Then S.L. 2026-8 and S.L. 2026-47 imposed a one-year moratorium. The legislative staff summary lists Bladen among nine counties subject to it: Anson, Bladen, Buncombe, Chowan, Davidson, Guilford, Onslow, Pamlico and Pender.

A School of Government analysis of the first bill notes that counties must still list and appraise changes found during the reappraisal, such as an unrecorded building, but use the older schedule of values. It also says counties should send notice of the new values again in 2027. The 2027 value is the one that will drive your bill, so confirm where your parcel stands with Tax Administration at 910-862-6730 before you list.

How do appeals work after the Bladen reappraisal?

The county asked for appeals on its 2026 notices by April 10, 2026, a date now past. The two session laws separately give taxpayers in the affected counties the right to appeal 2026 values during calendar year 2026, and the School of Government reads that as running through December 31, 2026.

Bladen's FAQ rules out affordability as a basis. What counts is an assessment out of line with similar properties, or a factual mistake on the record card. Get the card first, then collect a private appraisal, comparable sales, a survey or photos of structural damage.

  • By mail to the revaluation team, PO Box 774, Elizabethtown, NC 28337
  • In the marked box in the lobby of the tax office on E King Street
  • In the drop box in the lot behind the county courthouse

Formal appeals go to the board of equalization and review, which opens in the window from the first Monday of April to the first Monday of May and, in a reappraisal year, wraps up by December 1. After the board mails its ruling, the owner has 30 days to take it to the Property Tax Commission.

How does Bladen County's tax rate compare with other 2026 reappraisal counties?

NCDOR's 2024-25 schedule prints Bladen at $.7850 per $100, and the county commissioners' association map book shows 0.7850 again for fiscal year 2026-27. Bladen is one of several counties that were scheduled to reappraise in 2026.

County rate per $100 and reappraisal years, 2024-25 (NC Department of Revenue, August 2024)
CountyRateLast reappraisalNext scheduled
Bladen.785020222026
Anson.777020182026
Pender.737520192026
Chowan.695020222026
Onslow.655020222026
Davidson.540020212026

Bladen's FAQ treats appraisal and tax rate as separate decisions: values come first, and the commissioners fix the rate in June from the budget. A higher value alone does not raise a bill.

When is Bladen County tax due and what relief can owners apply for?

Bladen bills use the state calendar. September 1 is the due date, January 5 is the last interest-free day, 2% attaches January 6, and three-fourths of a percent more accrues monthly from February 1. The statutory listing period for property runs through January 31.

Tax Administration posts two application deadlines:

  • June 1 is the cutoff for new elderly, disabled, disabled veteran and circuit breaker applications.
  • January 31 is the cutoff for new applications on everything else, including religious, charitable and present-use valuation.

For 2026, NCDOR prints a $38,800 income limit for the elderly or disabled exclusion and the circuit breaker, plus $58,200 as the higher circuit breaker ceiling. The disabled veteran exclusion takes $45,000 off appraised value with no age or income test. Only one of the three programs can apply to an owner, and the circuit breaker is renewed by a fresh application each year.

What does a seller need to know about taxes and deeds in Bladen County?

Before a deed is recorded in Bladen, taxes have to be accounted for. Either the filer completes a certification form, or a closing attorney prepares the deed and it states that delinquent taxes, if any, will be paid by the attorney to the county tax collector when closing proceeds are disbursed.

This route lets a house with back taxes close: the attorney pays the delinquent bills out of the sale money, and the deed then goes to the register. The seller also pays the $1.00 per $500 excise tax before recording.

A parcel that fails to sell at a county tax foreclosure auction becomes county property and stays on the market. Bladen keeps a public list of those parcels, updated November 2, 2026. State law gives the auction a deposit of up to 20% and a 10-day window for higher bids after the report of sale. Before confirmation, paying the taxes, penalties, interest and costs redeems the property.

More questions about Bladen County, NC Property Tax Guide

How do I call Bladen County Tax Administration?

Dial 910-862-6730. Visits are at 201 E King Street in Elizabethtown, weekdays 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

Why does my 2026 Bladen bill not reflect the new reappraisal?

The General Assembly postponed the reappraisal by a year for Bladen and eight other counties. Bills for 2026 use the 2025 values, and the new values start with the 2027 tax year.

Has the Bladen County appeal window closed?

The county's April 10, 2026 date is past, but the session laws allow appeals of 2026 values through calendar year 2026. A fresh notice for 2027 values should open the next round, so call the office to confirm your status.

When do Bladen homeowners apply for elderly, disabled or veteran tax relief?

New applications for those programs and the circuit breaker are due June 1 yearly. Other exemptions and deferments, such as present-use value, are due January 31.

Can a Bladen County house with unpaid taxes still be sold?

Yes. The closing attorney pays the delinquent taxes to the county tax collector from your proceeds, and the deed says so. The sale has to close before the court confirms any tax foreclosure sale.

Brunswick County by the numbers

How do you contact the Brunswick County Tax Office?

One office in the David R. Sandifer Administration Building, 30 Government Center Drive, Bolivia, NC 28422, does appraisal, assessment, ownership records and tax collection. Its main number is 910-253-2829. For relief programs, call 910-253-2811 on weekdays between 8:30 a.m. and 5 p.m.

From the tax office page on the county website you reach tax bills, property record cards, certifications, the foreclosure list and land records. A payment plan through the collections division is available for owners who cannot clear a bill in one payment; ask before the balance is late.

What do Brunswick County's housing numbers mean for a seller?

Brunswick County has grown fast. The Census Bureau estimates 174,702 people in July 2025, up 27.8% from 136,695 in the April 2020 base, on 850.08 square miles of land.

QuickFacts lists 116,023 housing units, with 84.6% owner-occupied by the Census rate. The 2020 to 2024 median value is $349,800, and the median gross rent is $1,351. People 65 and older make up 36.6% of residents. Builders took out 4,457 permits in 2025, and each new house or addition can change a parcel's value ahead of the next reappraisal.

The rate schedule names 19 towns and villages, among them Bolivia, Northwest, Leland, Navassa, Shallotte, Southport, Oak Island, Holden Beach, Ocean Isle Beach, Sunset Beach, Caswell Beach and Bald Head Island. The town where a parcel sits determines which town rate gets added to the county rate.

What is the Brunswick County property tax rate?

Brunswick levies 0.3420, which is 34.20 cents per $100 of value, and the county schedule shows that rate unchanged for 2024, 2025 and 2026. In 2022 the rate was 0.485, and it dropped to 0.342 in 2023, the year of the last countywide revaluation.

Brunswick County and selected town rates per $100 (county Tax Rates page)

Brunswick County0.3420.3420.342

Bald Head Island0.62770.65070.586

A separate Smithville Township rate of 0.04 and a few special districts, including two Bald Head Island zones, apply on top in their areas. The county adopts rates in late spring or early summer, so look at the page after each budget vote. The Department of Revenue's August 2024 schedule agrees with the county figure of .3420 and lists 2023 and 2027 as the last and next reappraisal years.

How will the 2027 Brunswick County revaluation and appeal process work?

Every parcel will carry its market value and condition as of January 1, 2027. A building that is unfinished on that date is appraised at its percentage of completion.

Notices of the new value are scheduled for February and March 2027. Check your notice against the record card for errors in the property data. Appeals then run in two stages:

  • Informal review: from January until the board of equalization and review convenes, the tax assessor can adjust a value when the facts support it.
  • Formal appeal: after the board convenes, it holds the authority, and owners or their representatives normally present their case in person.

An appeal received after the board convenes is handled as formal. One that arrives after adjournment is untimely and generally waits for the next year, and a successful appeal is not retroactive to earlier years. The board's first meeting falls from the first Monday in April to the first Monday in May under G.S. 105-322, and in a reappraisal year it must finish by December 1. The next step up, the Property Tax Commission, takes appeals filed within 30 days of the board's mailed decision.

What is the payment calendar for a Brunswick County tax bill?

September 1 is the due date. Interest holds off through January 5, or the next business day when January 5 lands on a weekend. The county mailed 2026 bills in mid-August, and they can be paid without interest through January 5, 2027.

Late bills then pick up 2% for the stretch from January 6 to February 1, and after that three-fourths of a percent accrues each month or fraction of one until the balance is cleared. A check mailed on time is judged by its postmark. Prepayment discounts are possible if the board adopts a schedule by May 1, so ask whether this year has one.

The county's claim for the tax runs from the January 1 listing date and can be enforced by suing in foreclosure.

What relief can a Brunswick County owner apply for?

The county's relief page lists four programs. First, the elderly or disabled exclusion: it removes $25,000 or half of appraised value, whichever is larger, from a permanent residence owned by someone 65 or older, or totally and permanently disabled, whose income is within the limit. NCDOR prints $38,800 for 2026.

  • Disabled veteran exclusion: the first $45,000 of appraised value comes off, with no age or income condition. A surviving spouse who has not remarried can claim it.
  • Homestead circuit breaker: the yearly tax is held to 4% of income, or 5% when income is over the limit but no more than 150% of it, and what exceeds the cap is deferred and liened.
  • Present-use value: qualifying farm, horticultural or forest land is assessed on its use value, not its market value.

The county's page says three years of deferred circuit breaker tax come due, with interest, if the owner dies, transfers the property or stops living there, so a sale brings that bill. Applications use the state form and go to the county tax office, ideally in January, although filings are accepted through June 1.

How do taxes affect a Brunswick County house sale?

Brunswick County requires, by resolution, that a deed be stamped by the tax office before the Register of Deeds will record it. The stamp shows that taxes, fees and assessments are paid.

To see what is owed, request a Tax Certification under G.S. 105-361. Owners, attorneys and other interested persons may ask. The report covers local tax liens, deferred taxes where they exist, fire fees and assessments the office has to collect, so request it early.

On top of that, the seller sends the register the deed tax, $1.00 for every $500 of consideration, before the deed is filed.

Properties with unpaid taxes can go to a county auction on the steps of the courthouse in Bolivia, rain or shine. Winning bidders pay a 5% deposit on the spot in cash, certified or cashier's check or money order, and the county provides no financing. A 10-day upset period follows, and each higher bid must beat the last by 5% or $750, whichever is more. The winner has a week after notice to pay the rest and receives a commissioner's deed. A homeowner can still sell and pay the taxes at closing while the process is pending.

More questions about Brunswick County, NC Property Tax Guide

Who do I call at the Brunswick County Tax Office?

Call 910-253-2829 for the Tax Office or 910-253-2811 for relief programs. The office is at 30 Government Center Drive in Bolivia.

What is the county tax rate in Brunswick County?

The county rate is 0.3420 for 2024, 2025 and 2026, with town or district rates added where they apply.

What date does the next Brunswick County revaluation take effect?

January 1, 2027, with notices scheduled between February and March 2027. The prior revaluation was effective January 1, 2023.

Does Brunswick County give a grace period on late tax bills?

Not after January 5. Interest begins the next day, and the collections division can arrange a payment plan if you call before the deadline.

Does Brunswick County make sellers get a tax stamp before recording?

Yes. By county resolution the tax office must stamp a deed before the Register of Deeds records it, which confirms taxes, fees and assessments are settled.

Buncombe County by the numbers

Which Buncombe County offices deal with my tax bill?

One department, Tax Assessment, covers the whole cycle from its building at 182 College Street in Asheville. The doors are open weekdays between 8 am and 5 pm. Listing, appraising and assessing belong to the assessor, and billing and collecting belong to the collector.

Each desk has its own number, so dial the one that matches your question.

  • Real estate values and appeal forms: 828-250-4940
  • Payments, balances and payment plans: 828-250-4910
  • Senior, disability and veteran relief: 828-250-4915
  • Business and personal property: 828-250-4930
  • Land records: 828-250-4970

You can also type an address into tax.buncombenc.gov to see the property record card, the bill and the appeal request. Anyone preparing to sell a Buncombe house should ask the collections desk for the balance on the parcel before choosing a closing date.

Why do 2026 Buncombe tax bills use 2021 values?

Because of a law the General Assembly passed in July 2026, the county must hold off on its new values until January 1, 2027. Bills for 2026 therefore rest on the schedule from the 2021 reappraisal, even though the county had finished a reappraisal as of January 1, 2026 and mailed owners their new numbers.

Two measures were involved: S.B. 889 (S.L. 2026-8), which delayed the schedule for a short list of counties that includes Buncombe, and S.B. 474 (S.L. 2026-47), which offered a way out through a revenue-neutral rate. The county said that rate would round to 40 cents. At a July 14, 2026 special meeting, commissioners picked the old values and a higher rate so the budget approved on June 2, 2026 would stand.

For most owners nothing moved. Unless you built or altered something, the value matches last year's, and last year's value already carried any Tropical Storm Helene adjustment. Mailed bills ran late, with most residential bills posted online first.

What rates appear on a 2026 Buncombe County bill?

The county levy is 61.54 cents on each $100 of value, and the districts below add their own. Your parcel's address decides which of them apply.

Rates the county adopted on July 14, 2026

Buncombe County61.54County news release of July 14, 2026
Unified Fire District17.38County news release of July 14, 2026
Asheville City Schools11.75County news release of July 14, 2026

Because the county assigns values for every town and district inside it, the delay reached those units too. The 40-cent option reached only the county's own rate. City and town rates come from their own governing boards, so read the lines on your bill.

What are the payment dates and options in Buncombe County?

A bill is normally due September 1, and the county lets owners pay through the following January 5 without a penalty. For the 2026 bills, that final penalty-free day is January 5, 2027.

After that, state law adds 2% interest from January 6 until February 1, then three quarters of one percent for each month or part of a month. A mailed payment counts as paid on its postmark date.

Owners who need more time can ask Tax Collections for a plan, either a Casual Payment Plan or a Preauthorized Debit Payment Plan. While you stay enrolled, the county does not use garnishments of wages or bank accounts. Call 828-250-4910 and ask for a collection specialist.

How can I contest my Buncombe County property value?

Two routes exist: an informal review by Property Assessment, or a formal hearing before the Board of Equalization and Review. The county's August 2026 guidance said an appeal of the value on the current bill could be filed through December 31, 2026.

To start online, enter your address at tax.buncombenc.gov, pick View Parcel, then Tax Appeal Request. A mailed form is available from 828-250-4940. Over 16,000 appeals came in on the 2026 reappraisal values, and the county is holding the unresolved ones for the 2027 reappraisal, so nobody has to refile unless a decision came back and they disagree.

  • Under G.S. 105-322 the board may lower, raise or confirm a value after hearing evidence.
  • Ask for the hearing before the board adjourns; a decision notice mailed late gives you 15 days from its mailing.
  • The board mails its ruling within a month of adjourning.
  • Beyond that, notify the Property Tax Commission in writing within 30 days of the mailed ruling.

Who gets relief on a Buncombe County bill?

The county runs the three programs that state law creates, and the application window is January 1 through June 1. A household can use only one program at a time.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: shields the larger of $25,000 or half of the home's appraised value, for owners aged 65 and up or totally and permanently disabled, with income at or below the cap. The cap printed for 2026 is $38,800.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: removes the first $45,000 of appraised value, with no age or income test.
  • Circuit breaker: holds tax to 4% of income, or 5% when income runs above the cap up to $58,200 for 2026. The excess is deferred and becomes a lien, due if the owner sells or leaves.

The county has also cautioned that online videos describe a federal senior property tax exemption that does not exist, and it asks older owners to use only its official applications. Separately, its General Assistance Program, described at buncombenc.gov/gap, offers short-term help with housing and utility costs.

What happens to unpaid Buncombe County tax when I sell?

The debt attaches to the parcel, so it gets settled from the proceeds at or before closing. State law makes the lien attach as of the date property is listed each year, and penalties, interest and costs ride along. The county may enforce it through a foreclosure suit filed where the land sits.

Call Tax Collections at 828-250-4910 for the figure before fixing a closing date. If you hold a circuit breaker deferral, expect that balance to come due on the sale. A buyer's attorney will also want proof that the account is paid before the deed goes to the register of deeds at 205 College Street.

Owners with an open appeal should keep the paperwork handy, since the outcome applies to the 2027 value that the next buyer will see.

What do the Census numbers tell me about Buncombe County homeowners?

Buncombe's July 2025 estimate was 277,417 people in 142,799 housing units spread across 656.50 square miles of land. The median owner-occupied home is $391,800, and 66.2% of homes are owned.

Median household income is $74,436. Owners with a mortgage pay a median $1,785 a month, owners without one pay $505, and renters pay a median $1,362 in gross rent. The Census Bureau shows 12.4% of residents in poverty and 23.2% aged 65 or older, an age group that includes many people eligible for state relief.

Source: Census QuickFacts for Buncombe County.

More questions about Buncombe County, NC Property Tax Guide

What rate does Buncombe County charge on 2026 bills?

The county levy is 61.54 cents per $100 of value on the 2021 schedule. Unified Fire District property adds 17.38 cents, and Asheville City Schools adds 11.75 cents.

When do Buncombe bills have to be paid?

September 1 is the usual due date, and no penalty applies through January 5 of the next year. Interest begins January 6.

Is it still possible to protest a Buncombe County value?

The county's August 2026 guidance allowed appeals of the current bill through December 31, 2026, filed at tax.buncombenc.gov or through 828-250-4940. Appeals already made on the 2026 values stay on hold for 2027.

Why is my 2026 Buncombe value unchanged?

A state law pushed the new reappraisal to 2027, so bills use the 2021 values. A change only shows up if you added or altered improvements.

Which Buncombe homeowners qualify for tax relief?

People 65 or older or totally and permanently disabled within the income cap, plus veterans with a permanent and total service-connected disability. Applications run January 1 through June 1, and the exemptions desk is at 828-250-4915.

Tax rate

Selling in Burke County?
We buy Burke County houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.

Burke County by the numbers

Where do I take a Burke County property tax question?

The Burke County Tax Office works out of the Burke Services Building, 110 North Green Street, Morganton, NC 28655, from 8 am until 5 pm each weekday. The phone is (828) 764-9430, letters go to PO Box 219, Morganton, NC 28680, and Collections takes email at collections@burkenc.org.

Three divisions split the work. Real Property appraises land and buildings and fields questions on values, revaluation and appeals. Personal and Business Property takes listings and forms for taxable equipment and business assets. Collections issues bills and accepts payment for the county plus the towns and fire districts the Burke office serves, which means one bill can carry several levies.

The office also publishes its deed certification form and a tax website at burkenctax.com. A seller should start with Collections, the division that certifies the amount owed on a parcel before a deed moves on to recording.

What rate does Burke County levy?

Burke's own levy is 55.5 cents per $100 of assessed value, and the budget for fiscal 2026-2027 kept it there. That budget, about $120.7 million, passed 5-0 and began July 1, 2026.

The county says its commissioners have cut the rate twice since 2023. Your bill may list more than the county line, because town and fire district charges go through the same office. Look at each rate line for the units covering your address.

A rate multiplies a value, and the values will shift once the 2027 revaluation project is done.

Is Burke County reappraising for 2027?

Burke County is carrying out a revaluation project for 2027. Commissioners called a public hearing for November 16, 2026, at 6:00 p.m. at the Burke Services Building, to hear comment on a proposed Schedule of Values and Present Use Schedule of Values. Copies were posted online and at the tax office.

State law (G.S. 105-286) sets an eight-year ceiling between reappraisals, each as of January 1. Larger counties, those with 75,000 residents or more, can be forced to reappraise early if their sales assessment ratio drops below .85 or climbs above 1.15. The review board gets until December 1 in a revaluation year, a longer runway than usual.

For questions about the schedules, call the Tax Department at (828) 764-9430. When your new notice comes, set it beside recent sales of comparable homes nearby before deciding whether to appeal.

Which dates shape a Burke County tax year?

Bills fall due on September 1, with face-amount payment allowed until January 6. This table collects the statutory dates an owner meets.

Calendar rules that govern each Burke County tax year
EventWhat the statute saysSource
Listing windowStarts on the first business day of January and ends January 31G.S. 105-307
Bill duePayable September 1 of the fiscal yearG.S. 105-360
Par paymentPayment received ahead of January 6G.S. 105-360
First interest step2% on balances from January 6 to February 1G.S. 105-360
Ongoing interest3/4 of 1% for every month or part, after February 1G.S. 105-360
Review board opensOpens no sooner than the first Monday in April and no later than the first Monday in MayG.S. 105-322
State-level appealNotice due within 30 days of the board's mailed decisionG.S. 105-290

Each summer the county mails listing forms for owners to update, sign and send back. Returning them within the January window avoids a late listing penalty.

How do I challenge a Burke County value?

Talk to the Tax Office first. Anything unresolved goes to the review board, which is the commissioners unless the county has formed a special panel. Your request must be in hand before the panel adjourns.

  • A written request or a personal appearance both count.
  • If the board's own notice was mailed less than 15 days before adjourning, the clock gives you 15 days from that mailing.
  • The ruling arrives by mail within 30 days after adjournment.
  • Past that sits the Property Tax Commission, which takes a written notice listing your grounds, with a copy to the assessor.

Hurricane Helene created a special case. The county offered reduced values for the 2025 listing date to owners who reported unrepaired structural damage, and gave them 30 days from receipt to appeal in writing. That relief lasted a single year, so ask the Tax Office where your parcel stands now.

What certification does Burke County require before a deed is recorded?

Burke uses a Delinquent Tax Certification form built on G.S. 161-31, which lets commissioners instruct the register of deeds to turn away a transfer deed until the collector certifies there are no delinquent taxes. The form was revised April 22, 2026.

You supply the parcel number, the seller and buyer names, the buyer's mailing address, the site address, the price and the acreage. The form also asks if a mobile home or personal property, such as vehicles, boats or farm equipment, goes with the sale, and whether land in Present Use Value will stay enrolled. Staff then complete a ten-year grid of deferred and due taxes.

Send it to the Office of the Tax Administrator, PO Box 219, Morganton, or to collections@burkenc.org. A closing attorney often files it, though asking Collections for a figure before you list can save days.

Can Burke County owners get a property tax break?

Yes. The state's three programs apply here, filed on Form AV-9 with the county assessor, and applications must be accepted through June 1. An owner may draw on one program only.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: removes whichever is greater, $25,000 or half the appraised value of a permanent residence, for an owner at least 65 or totally and permanently disabled whose prior-year income stays within the 2026 cap of $38,800.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: the first $45,000 of appraised value, with no age or income test.
  • Circuit breaker: tax limited to 4% of income, or 5% where income runs up to $58,200, once the owner has lived in the home five years.

Circuit breaker savings are deferred, and the tax deferred over the three prior years falls due on a transfer, an owner's death or a move out. Mention any such deferral to your closing attorney.

What does the Census say about Burke County housing?

Growth is slow. The mid-2025 estimate is 88,655 people, up just 1.2% from the 2020 base and below the 90,912 counted in 2010. The county has 41,669 housing units on 506.24 land square miles.

From 2020 through 2024, 74.5% of homes were owner-occupied, valued at a median $185,400. Household income hit a median $58,592, gross rent $884, and 14.0% of people were in poverty. Adults 65 and over make up 23.2% of residents. Building permits in 2025 numbered 588. Owners with a mortgage carry a median $1,220 in monthly costs, while owners without one report $389. Workers spend a mean 23.4 minutes getting to work, and 21.0% of adults 25 and older have a bachelor's degree or higher. The county's land area is 506.24 square miles at 173.0 people per square mile.

Source: Census QuickFacts for Burke County.

More questions about Burke County, NC Property Tax Guide

What is Burke County's rate per $100?

It is 55.5 cents, unchanged for 2026-2027, plus any town or fire district charges that reach your parcel.

Where can I pay a Burke County bill?

Go to 110 North Green Street in Morganton during weekday office hours, call (828) 764-9430, or email collections@burkenc.org.

When does interest start on Burke County bills?

Interest starts January 6, since payment before that date is at face amount. It is 2% through February 1 and 3/4 of 1% a month after.

Is Burke County revaluing property?

Yes, a 2027 revaluation is under way. A public hearing on the proposed values was set for November 16, 2026, and state law demands reappraisal at least every eighth year.

Do I need tax certification to sell in Burke County?

Yes, the county's Delinquent Tax Certification lets the collector confirm nothing delinquent remains before the deed goes on record. Request it at collections@burkenc.org or (828) 764-9430.

Cabarrus County by the numbers

How is a Cabarrus County house valued and billed each year?

Cabarrus County values every parcel at market value as of January 1, then sends one bill that combines the county rate with any city, town and fire district rates that apply to the address. The county's Revaluation FAQ says each property was valued at fair market value as of January 1, 2024, with no flat percentage change applied to prior assessments.

The tax office lists three building blocks for a parcel's value: the land, the building (type, age and physical characteristics) and extras such as garages, sheds, pools, fences and driveways. Improvements under construction are valued partially, based on percent complete on January 1, and those values feed the bill.

A county adopts its own reappraisal schedule within the limits of G.S. 105-286, which allows at most eight years between reappraisals. Cabarrus County cut that gap in half so values follow the market more closely.

Who do I contact about assessments and appeals in Cabarrus County?

The Tax Administration department handles assessment and appeals, and the Revaluation office answers value questions at 704-920-2126 or revalinfo@cabarruscounty.us. The office is at 65 Church Street S in Concord, NC 28025, open Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.

The Collections side bills and collects for every jurisdiction in the county, which the county's rate page counts as the county itself, seven cities or towns and 16 fire districts. The Equalization and Review Board hears appeals, and its members are appointed by the County Commissioners from residents who know the local real estate market.

  • Real estate values and property cards: the county's online real estate search, by name, address or parcel
  • Comparable sales: a map-based comparable sales tool on the Tax Revaluation page
  • Relief programs: homestead, disabled veteran and circuit breaker, plus present use value and wildlife conservation programs
  • Payment plans: the Collections office

How do I appeal a Cabarrus County property value?

Disagree in writing first, asking for an informal review; the Board of Equalization and Review hears you if the reply falls short. The county says nothing specific is required to start a review, but the more evidence you attach, the stronger the case. The appraiser for your area looks at what you send and responds with an Informal Review notice, which also explains how to go to the formal level.

You get 30 days from that response notice to continue the appeal. A board hearing request goes to Cabarrus County Tax Revaluation, PO Box 707, Concord, NC 28026-0707, or through the county's online system. It must reach the Office of the County Assessor within 30 days of the date on your Notice of Real Estate Assessed Value letter, or any time before the Board adjourns, which the county says usually happens in late April and is advertised in the local newspaper.

After you submit, you and the county appraiser get one more chance to review the case, and you complete an Application for Hearing form. The board hears evidence from both sides and mails a decision letter within 30 days of the hearing. Owners still unhappy after that can go to the NC Property Tax Commission, and under G.S. 105-290, written notice of that appeal, stating your grounds, must be filed within 30 days of the mailing date on the board's ruling.

One caution from the county itself: the size of the jump between two revaluations is not a valid reason for appeal. Compare your parcel to similar sales instead.

When are Cabarrus County property taxes due?

Bills are due September 1, and they are past due if not paid before the following January 5, according to the Collections page. Real estate, business and individual personal property bills are mailed annually and arrive toward the end of July. The county's FAQ narrows the mailing to late July or the first days of August.

Cabarrus County tax calendar from county Collections and Revaluation pages
WhenWhat happens
January 1Value date for each parcel; the bill goes to the owner on this date

State law sets interest at 2 percent for January 6 to February 1, then three-fourths of one percent a month after that (G.S. 105-360). The county notes that a delinquent bill faces collection actions or tax foreclosure. Collections will work out a payment plan, but the bill must still be paid in full by the delinquent date, and the taxpayer has to ask for the plan, ideally early in the year.

What are the Cabarrus County tax rates?

The county rate for 2026 is $0.576 per $100 of assessed value, and each city or town and fire district adds its own rate. The county's rate page works through an example for a Kannapolis address, adding the Kannapolis rate of $0.5595 to the county rate to reach a combined 2026 rate of $1.1355 per $100.

Rates are set during the budget process, with the Board of Commissioners and each municipality adopting theirs no later than June 30, and the final numbers are usually settled by June. Changes in assessed value may or may not change your bill, because the effect is unknown until the rates are adopted. If you want your own figure, use the county's real estate search for the assessed value and the rate page for each district that covers your parcel, then ask Collections to confirm.

Which tax breaks can a Cabarrus County homeowner apply for?

The Tax Revaluation page lists homestead, disabled veteran and circuit breaker relief, all filed with the county assessor. Under G.S. 105-277.1, a homeowner aged 65 or over, or one who is totally and permanently disabled, with income below the yearly cap, can shield $25,000 or half the appraised value of the residence, whichever is larger. The Department of Revenue's application sets that cap at $38,800 for 2026.

  • Disabled veterans: the first $45,000 of value is excluded, with no age or income test printed on the state form
  • Circuit breaker: after five years of owning and living in the home, the bill is capped at 4.0% of income under the cap or 5.0% between the cap and $58,200 (2026), and the excess is deferred as a lien
  • Form AV-9 goes to the assessor, who accepts it until June 1 before the tax year, and no owner may combine the three

Farm, forest and wildlife landowners should also ask about the present use value programs, which the county lists separately with applications.

Who pays the Cabarrus County bill when I sell?

Have this year's bill paid out of the sale proceeds. Under G.S. 105-355. The bill is issued in the owner's name as of January 1, so sellers who sold partway through the year are told to pass the bill on to the buyer.

The Cabarrus County market adds context. Census Bureau QuickFacts lists a median owner-occupied home value of $354,800 for 2020-2024, a population estimate of 249,725 for July 2025 and an owner-occupied rate of 71.2 percent. Values in the county's real estate search are set as of January 1, 2024, so compare yours with recent neighborhood sales before you list. Ask the closing attorney for a payoff of all taxes due, including fire district amounts, and ask Collections for the delinquent status of any prior year.

More questions about Cabarrus County, NC Property Tax Guide

When are Cabarrus County property taxes due?

September 1. The county says a bill is past due if not paid before the following January 5, and state law starts interest on January 6. Bills are mailed toward the end of July.

How often does Cabarrus County revalue real estate?

Every four years by local choice, although state law only requires every eight. The current values are as of January 1, 2024. The Revaluation office at 704-920-2126 can confirm the next cycle.

How do I appeal my Cabarrus County property value?

Submit a written request for an informal review, then appeal to the Board of Equalization and Review within 30 days of your value notice or before the board adjourns, usually in late April. The decision letter arrives within 30 days of the hearing.

Does Cabarrus County allow installments on a tax bill?

Yes. The Collections office works with taxpayers on payment plans, but you must request one and the bill still has to be paid in full by the delinquent date. Contacting them early in the year is preferred.

Who gets the bill if my Cabarrus County house sells before year end?

The bill still goes out in the name of the owner on January 1, so forward it to the buyer if you receive it after closing. Settle the current year's tax through closing so it does not turn into a lien problem for the new owner.

Caldwell County by the numbers

What should a Caldwell County seller know about the county first?

Caldwell County is a foothills county in the northwest of the state, formed in January 1841 from parts of Burke and Wilkes, with Lenoir as the county seat. The county's own history page places it about 69 miles northwest of Charlotte, with elevations running from 900 feet to 5,964 feet and the Yadkin, Johns and Catawba as its main rivers.

It has nine incorporated municipalities: Lenoir, Hudson, Granite Falls, Cedar Rock, Cajahs Mountain, Gamewell, Sawmills, and parts of Blowing Rock and Rhodhiss. The first modern furniture factories were organized here in 1889, and furniture work shows up repeatedly in local history. Which town a parcel falls in changes the bill, since each municipality adopts its own rate and a couple adopt none.

  • Population estimate for July 1, 2025: 81,105, against 80,652 in the 2020 Census
  • Housing units on July 1, 2025: 38,057, with 73.5% owner-occupied for 2020-2024
  • Middle owner-occupied home value in the 2020-2024 figures: $192,200
  • Median gross rent: $744; median household income: $56,425
  • Residents 65 and older: 22.8%; land area 471.89 square miles; 501 building permits in 2025

Where is the Caldwell County Tax Office and what does it handle?

Find the Tax Office at 905 West Avenue NW, Lenoir, NC 28645. Visits work on weekdays between 8 and 5; the office shuts on weekends and federal holidays. The mailing address is PO Box 2200, Lenoir, NC 28645, and the main number in the county directory is 828-757-1340. Listing questions can also go to 828-757-1320.

The office lists personal property and business property, bills and collects the tax, and runs revaluation. For a home sale, the pieces that matter are the real estate value, the delinquent status of each year's bill and any relief program the owner is enrolled in. A tax lien on real property in the county is advertised by the county once bills go unpaid, and the commissioners authorized advertising of 2024 liens at their February 2025 meeting.

What is the payment deadline for Caldwell County property tax, and when does interest begin?

Bills come due on September 1. Interest begins on January 6 of the next year at 2 percent and climbs by three-fourths of a percent every month until the bill is settled. The tax office's FAQ adds that it judges timeliness by the postmark from the U.S. Postal Service and refuses postage-meter dates.

Some practical details from the same FAQ:

  • Partial payments are accepted from the time the bill arrives until January 6
  • Online payment accepts American Express, Discover, Mastercard, Visa or a PayPal account, and PayPal's processing fees are not kept by the county
  • An escrow account does not stop the bill from being mailed to you, so contact your lender if you think it should pay
  • Personal property bills such as boats and unlicensed vehicles are mailed in July

The 2026 rate chart also lists a discount of 2.00 for July and 1.00 for August. G.S. 105-360 lets a county adopt a prepayment discount schedule approved by the Department of Revenue, so ask the tax office how the discount is applied before relying on it.

What rates did Caldwell County list for 2026?

The 2026 chart lists 0.4666 for the county, and a town or district adds its own line. Counties quote these figures per $100 of assessed value. Lenoir shows 0.4600, with a separate special downtown district at 0.1800, and fire and rescue districts add further lines for rural parcels.

The chart also prints a household solid waste fee of 22.75, and 17.75 for city households. Rural fire districts range widely on the chart, from 0.0430 for Bethlehem to 0.1415 for South Caldwell, so the district your house sits in changes the bill. Before estimating a bill, ask the tax office which fire and rescue districts include your parcel.

What happened with the 2025 revaluation in Caldwell County?

Caldwell County reappraised all real property for 2025, after the county's sales-assessment ratio fell below the 0.85 threshold that triggers a reappraisal under state law. The county's own earlier revaluation took effect January 1, 2021, and the tax office's Q and A says the goal of a reappraisal is equal, uniform values for every taxpayer.

At a February 2025 commissioners' meeting the tax administrator said county staff appraised all residential property, and a third party handled commercial and industrial property. Around 450 appeals had been received at that point. Residents spoke about large jumps in assessed value at that meeting, and one commissioner said the board would cut the rate as far as it could toward revenue neutral. That record shows why an owner who sells should check the assessed value on the bill before comparing it with an offer.

State law sets an eight-year outer limit under G.S. 105-286, yet a county of 75,000 residents or more must move up its reappraisal if the sales ratio slips under .85 or climbs over 1.15. Caldwell County's 2025 reappraisal followed that trigger, so owners should check their parcel's value on the bill.

How do I appeal a Caldwell County property value?

File for an informal review first, because the Board of Equalization and Review only picks up the case afterward. Under the county's revaluation Q and A, an owner who disagrees returns an Informal Review Form, and the best evidence is a recent fee appraisal backed by local sales or a comparison of similar homes by year built, size, construction and acreage. The county advises against paying for an independent appraisal unless you feel it is truly needed.

The Board of Equalization and Review is the formal appeals board, and appeals from it go to the NC Property Tax Commission. Under G.S. 105-322, the board convenes for the first time between early April and early May, and your hearing request has to reach it before adjournment. The commissioners' policy sets the Caldwell board at five members and four alternates, who must have lived in the county at least two years.

Personal property is separate: appeals of individual or business personal property values must be in writing to the Caldwell County Assessor's Office, PO Box 2200, Lenoir, NC 28645, within 30 days of the tax bill date. Business listings that miss the January 31 deadline without an approved extension carry a 10 percent penalty on the total tax.

What relief and special programs apply to Caldwell County homeowners?

Caldwell County follows the state's three programs, and the county tax site provides a relief brochure and an application. The elderly or disabled exclusion under G.S. 105-277.1 shelters the larger of $25,000 or 50 percent of a residence's appraised value, and the state's 2026 form sets the income cap at $38,800.

The disabled veteran exclusion takes the first $45,000 of appraised value, and the circuit breaker caps tax at 4.0 or 5.0 percent of income, with the 2026 upper threshold printed as $58,200. Form AV-9 is the application, filed with the county assessor, and June 1 before the tax year is the last day the county must accept it. Owners cannot stack the three programs.

If you list real estate improvements, the county says to report new buildings and additions during January with your cost and the percent complete on January 1, and to report demolished improvements as well.

Who owes the Caldwell County tax bill when a house is sold?

Caldwell County bills the January 1 owner; a seller who closed later should hand the bill to the buyer. The lien attaches as of January 1 under G.S. 105-355, the closing attorney should settle the current year and any open prior years.

Ask the Tax Office for a written payoff and check the town or fire district on the bill, since the combined charge varies by parcel. If the house was inherited or has back years unpaid, get the full list of open years before you accept an offer, since delinquent taxes are collected through foreclosure.

More questions about Caldwell County, NC Property Tax Guide

When are Caldwell County property taxes due?

September 1 of the tax year. Interest begins January 6 of the following year at 2 percent, then three-fourths of one percent a month until paid, and the county uses the U.S. Postal postmark, not a meter date.

Where do I pay or ask about my Caldwell County tax bill?

Visit 905 West Avenue NW in Lenoir on a weekday between 8 and 5, or call 828-757-1340. Online payment works by credit card or PayPal, and the processing fees go to PayPal rather than the county.

When did Caldwell County last revalue property?

The county reappraised real property for 2025, and before that the county's revaluation took effect on January 1, 2021. State law requires a reappraisal at least every eight years, and sooner when the sales ratio falls below .85.

How do I appeal a Caldwell County real estate value?

Return the informal review form with comparable sales or an appraisal. If the answer disappoints you, ask the Board of Equalization and Review for a hearing ahead of its adjournment. Appeals from the board go to the NC Property Tax Commission within 30 days of its mailed decision.

If I sold my Caldwell County house after January 1, who gets the bill?

Billing follows the January 1 owner, so send a copy to the buyer. The county says it tries to notify the new owner but asks sellers to help.

Who to contact in Carteret County
