The county's budget guide for the same year says the countywide rate stays at 64.86 cents and the fire tax at 4 cents. On a tax bill, the countywide fire levy shows up as ADVL followed by a number. Confirm the fire district on your parcel with the collector before you work out a payoff.

When are Davie County taxes due, and what does a late payment cost?

Davie bills go out after July 1 and fall due September 1, with payment accepted through January 5 (the next business day if that date is a Saturday, Sunday or holiday). An owner with no bill in hand by September 15 should call the collector.

  • A payment has to reach the collector or carry a postmark by the deadline; an envelope with no postmark counts on its delivery day, so the county urges mailing at least 5 business days early.
  • Real estate accounts past due pick up 2% for January and 3/4% for each month after that.
  • The office takes partial payments, and a mailed partial needs a stamped return envelope to get a receipt.
  • Card payments online carry a convenience fee, and you need the bill year, account number and bill number.

Between March 1 and June 30 the collector must advertise current-year delinquent real property liens in a newspaper, and the advertising cost is added to the taxpayer's balance. The county lists wage, bank account and rent garnishment, foreclosure and tax warrants among the collection tools. By statute the tax lien on a parcel arises on the listing date, January 1.

How does the 2025 revaluation affect a Davie County appeal?

The latest Davie revaluation carries a January 1, 2025 effective date, and new assessed values reached owners in February 2025. The previous one was in 2021, and the county says it has recently revalued every four years even though state law only requires one every eight.

County staff did the work in house. Appraisers grouped roughly 215 appraisal neighborhoods and compared recent sales, then applied a uniform schedule of values. The revaluation page puts the parcel count near 24,000 and says the schedule is used until a new one is needed or 8 years pass.

To contest a value, the county's steps are:

  • Fill out the appeal form completely, sign and date it, and return it within thirty days of receiving it.
  • Send it to the Revaluation Office at 123 South Main Street, Mocksville, NC 27028, email it with supporting documents, or use the online form on the Revaluation/Land Records page.
  • Give your basis for the appeal; some appeals get a site visit.
  • Expect a letter that says whether the value changed. It can go up, stay the same or go down.

The county's appeal page also lists sales that do not count as qualified comparisons: a conveyance of two or more parcels, transactions between relatives or related businesses, undivided or fractional interests, sales involving governments, utilities, lenders or relocation firms, and forced or auction sales. Pick comparable sales outside those categories. The county's tax administration page states that the appeal period for the 2026 cycle has ended. If the county board rules against you, the Property Tax Commission is the next stop, and the clock there is 30 days from the mailing of the board's notice.

What property tax relief can a Davie County owner claim?

Three programs created by state law apply in Davie, and an owner may draw on just one. The county's listing notice prints these terms:

  • Elderly and disabled exclusion: income at or under $39,900, taking off $25,000 or 50% of the value of the house and one acre.
  • Disabled veterans exclusion: no income cap, honorable discharge, a 100% service-related disability, and a $45,000 reduction on the home and one acre.
  • Circuit breaker: income of $59,850 or below, North Carolina residency, and five years of owning and living in the home.

The income ceilings change with the year, so ask the assessor which figures apply to the year you are filing. Owners already receiving an exclusion do not reapply, except that the state requires a new circuit breaker application every year. File Form AV-9 with the county assessor; the office has to take it up to June 1 ahead of the tax year.

Under the circuit breaker the tax above the cap is deferred and attaches as a lien. When the house is sold, up to three preceding years of deferred tax become payable, so a seller on this program should get that figure before listing.

The Davie listing window is the month of January. Forms need to arrive or be postmarked by January 31, and a late listing draws a 10% penalty. Owners also report new buildings and improvements, and list unregistered vehicles, mobile homes, boats and business assets.

What happens to Davie County property tax when a house sells?

The seller normally settles the year's tax at closing, and the county calls proration a courtesy between buyer and seller. The owner of record on January 1 carries the legal obligation, and the county says enforcement can follow the property to a later owner, so confirm the split with your attorney.

  • Get a payoff from the collector that covers each open year and any advertised delinquency.
  • The grantor buys the state deed stamp at the register of deeds, one dollar for every five hundred dollars of price, ahead of recording.
  • If you use the circuit breaker, expect the deferred amount to come due on transfer.
  • Any lien for unpaid tax has to be cleared through closing, whoever the buyer is.

More questions about Davie County, NC Property Tax Guide

Where do I pay Davie County property tax?

Pay the Davie County Tax Collector by mail, in person at the Administration Building, in the dropbox, or online with a card. The Tax Administration page says mailed payments can go to the lockbox, and there is a new teller window at the office. Online card payments carry a convenience fee.

Can I still appeal my Davie County value?

The county's tax administration page says the appeal period for the 2026 tax year has ended. Call 336-753-6140 to ask when the next window opens. The county's thirty-day clock on its appeal form starts when you receive the form.

What is the Davie County tax rate in Mocksville?

A Mocksville parcel is charged the county rate of $0.6486 per $100, the countywide fire rate of $0.04 and the town rate of $0.29 listed for 2026-27. Other towns and fire districts have their own figures in the table above.

Must I renew a Davie County elderly exclusion each year?

No, an owner already receiving an exclusion does not need to reapply, according to the county's listing notice. The circuit breaker is different because the state requires a new application each year.

Who covers the deed stamp on a Davie County sale?

The seller does. The register of deeds collects one dollar per five hundred dollars of price (a leftover fraction counts as another five hundred) at recording, and the proceeds are split between the county and the state.

Which Duplin County offices handle property tax?

The Duplin County Tax Department runs three offices: Assessing, Collections and Land Records. All of them work from the Hardison Building at 117 Beasley Street in Kenansville, Monday to Friday, 8 am to 5 pm.

A taxpayer can walk in with cash, check or a card, phone the office, or use the online portal; a fee applies to every card payment.

What is Duplin County like for a seller?

Duplin County lies in the Coastal Plain of southeastern North Carolina. Founded in 1750, it covers roughly 819 square miles. The county's financial report describes Kenansville as the seat, sitting near the middle of the county, with Wayne, Lenoir, Jones, Onslow, Pender and Sampson counties around it.

Other incorporated places named in that report are Beulaville, Calypso, Faison, Greenevers, Magnolia, Rose Hill, Teachey, Wallace and Warsaw. Interstate 40, US 117 and NC 24 cross the county, and Kenansville itself is crossed by NC 24, NC 11 and NC 50. The county's recent budget message calls Duplin a rural county dependent on agriculture and industry, without much retail or fast population growth.

Census QuickFacts supplies the housing picture:

  • 51,571 residents in the July 2025 estimate, after a drop from 58,505 in the 2010 census to 48,715 in 2020.
  • 24,235 housing units and 70.3% owner-occupancy.
  • A 2020-2024 median home value of $137,400 for owner-occupied units, against median gross rent of $865.
  • Median household income of $55,148, with 21.1% of residents in poverty.
  • Land area of 814.72 square miles and a 2020 density of 59.8 residents per square mile.

Before you list a Duplin house, request a payoff figure from the collector and ask the assessor if an exclusion is already on file.

What is the Duplin County property tax rate?

Duplin's recommended budget for fiscal year 2026-27 is built on a flat county rate of 58 cents per $100 of assessed value. The county manager's budget message reports the same 58-cent rate the year before, which was a 15.5-cent cut from the 73.5 cents budgeted for 2024-25 after the January 2025 revaluation.

  • The 2025 revaluation raised the tax base about 25%, and the county reached roughly 98 percent of market value.
  • The revenue-neutral rate that revaluation produced was $0.5667 per $100.
  • The tax office reports $6,143,053,057 in real and personal property value billed for 2026 and 42,374 nonexempt parcels as of January 2026.
  • Each fire district levies a rate of its own on top of the county figure. The recommended 2025-26 budget lists rates from 4.5 cents per $100 for the Calypso department to 10 cents for the Harrells department.

Ask the assessing office which fire district and which town a parcel sits in, because those decide the full rate.

When does Duplin County revalue property?

Duplin's current values date from a January 1, 2025 revaluation, and the county has penciled in January 1, 2030 for the next. State law only requires a reappraisal every eight years, but the Board of Commissioners voted in 2023 to go countywide every five years.

Between revaluations, the assessing office reviews building permits for new construction and additions, and it works with owners on questions about value. The county says the next reappraisal will be done by state-certified appraisers.

If you built, added on or demolished something since the last reappraisal, expect the appraisal staff to have picked it up from the building permit.

How do I appeal a Duplin County property value?

Start with the county's informal review form, which asks for the owner, appellant, parcel number, address and your opinion of value. You circle the basis of the appeal: appraisal, asking price, purchase price or comparable sales.

  • Attach photos or documents that back up your number; the form warns that missing evidence can delay the review.
  • Owners of commercial or income-producing property attach the three most current years of income and expense data.
  • Mail the form to Duplin County Revaluation, PO Box 968, Kenansville, NC 28349. The current form lists April 15 as the submission date.
  • Personal property appeals use a separate form that asks for a hearing before the Board of Equalization and Review.

Under state law the county board convenes for the first time no sooner than the first Monday of April and no later than the first Monday of May. After an adverse ruling, you get 30 days from the mailing date to send the Property Tax Commission a written notice that states your grounds, and the assessor gets a copy.

What happens when Duplin County tax goes unpaid?

Bills arrive due on September 1, and a payment made before January 6 stays interest-free. From January 6 the charge is 2% through the start of February, then 3/4% for every month or fraction after that.

The county's collection tools include:

  • Garnishment of wages.
  • Attachment of grower payments.
  • Attachment of bank accounts.
  • Attachment of state income tax refunds.
  • Foreclosure of the property.

The tax office runs mortgage-style foreclosures: delinquent accounts go to the county attorney, a sale date is set by the court, and the county puts a sign on the property and advertises in local newspapers. The sale takes place at the courthouse steps in Kenansville, opening with the county's bid, and the high bidder leaves a 20% deposit in cash or certified check the day of the sale. After the commissioner files a sale report, bidders have 10 days to raise the bid or file exceptions, and the owner can still redeem ahead of confirmation by paying taxes, penalties, interest and costs.

What property tax relief can a Duplin County owner claim?

The assessing office processes the senior, disability and veteran exclusions, along with present-use value applications for farmland. The county's forms list includes the application for property tax relief, a certification of disability and a certification for disabled veterans.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: whichever is larger, $25,000 or half the home's appraised value, for owners aged 65 and up or totally and permanently disabled whose income is under the cap ($38,800 for tax year 2026).
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: $45,000 off the home's appraised value, open to veterans of any age and income.
  • Circuit breaker: the bill is held to 4% of income (5% for incomes between the cap and 150% of it), and anything above is deferred.

Take the application to the county assessor, who must accept filings until June 1 ahead of the tax year. Duplin owners with a mobile home should know the collector will not issue a moving permit until the taxes are paid or shown not to be at risk.

What should I do about Duplin County taxes before selling?

Get a payoff from the collections office, confirm which fire district and town taxes apply, and settle the year's tax at closing with your attorney. The deed stamp is a separate charge the seller pays at the register of deeds.

If an inherited house carries back taxes, ask Collections whether the parcel has been sent to the county attorney for foreclosure, because that changes how much time you have.

More questions about Duplin County, NC Property Tax Guide

When does Duplin County revalue property next?

The next Duplin County revaluation is scheduled to take effect January 1, 2030. The most recent one took effect January 1, 2025, and the Board of Commissioners voted in 2023 to revalue every five years.

Where do I pay Duplin County property tax?

You pay at the Duplin County Tax Office, 117 Beasley Street in Kenansville, by phone at 910-296-2112, or online through the county's tax portal. Cash, check and card are accepted in person, and card payments carry a fee.

What is the Duplin County tax rate?

The county's recommended 2026-27 budget uses 58 cents per $100 of assessed value. Fire districts add their own rate, and towns whose taxes the county collects add theirs, so ask the assessing office for the full rate on your parcel.

How do I appeal my Duplin County assessment?

Send the informal real property review form to Duplin County Revaluation, PO Box 968, Kenansville, with supporting evidence. The form lists April 15 as the submission date, and commercial owners attach three years of income and expense figures.

What can Duplin County do about delinquent taxes?

The county can garnish wages, attach bank accounts, grower payments and state refunds, and foreclose. The foreclosure sale is held at the courthouse steps in Kenansville, with a 20% deposit due from the winning bidder.

Durham County by the numbers

Which Durham County office handles property tax?

Tax Administration occupies the third floor at 201 East Main Street, Durham, and answers at 919-560-0300. Appeals, bills and relief applications all begin there, and the Land Records team works from 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM.

Beyond the counter, the county runs an online Tax Help portal that lets owners file an appeal, message staff and watch the status of a case. Owners can view and pay a bill at pay.dconc.gov, mail a check to the Tax Collector at P.O. Box 580240, Charlotte, NC 28258-0240, pay at the counter, or pay by phone (a convenience fee applies). The e-check option adds a $3.25 processing fee.

Durham property owners inside the city pay both a county and a city tax, so keep both bills in view when you plan a sale.

What does the Durham County housing market look like?

Durham County is a university and research county, home to Duke University, North Carolina Central University and Durham Technical Community College. Research Triangle Park, which the county calls the country's largest research park with more than 380 companies and 55,000 workers, has roughly three quarters of its land in Durham County.

Other employers and districts the county names include the American Tobacco Campus, the 5,300-acre Treyburn Corporate Park in unincorporated northern Durham County, and the Hub RTP development at Davis Drive and I-40.

Census QuickFacts reports the following for Durham:

  • An estimated 347,240 residents in July 2025, 6.9% above the 2020 estimates base.
  • 164,222 housing units and 141,847 households for 2020-2024.
  • Owners occupy just 55.5% of homes, which leaves a large rental segment.
  • Owner-occupied homes have a median value of $389,400, and the median gross rent is $1,508.
  • Households earn a median $82,316, and builders pulled 4,772 permits in 2025.
  • The county has 286.53 square miles of land, at a 2020 density of 1,133.7 residents per square mile.

What are the Durham County and City of Durham tax rates?

The Board of County Commissioners approved a countywide rate of 57.92 cents per $100 of property value in the 2026-2027 budget ordinance. The City of Durham kept its rate at 43.71 cents per $100 for the same year, and the city says a home valued at $424,000 pays about $1,853 a year in city tax.

  • Durham County: 57.92 cents per $100 for 2026-27, according to the county's tax bill notice.
  • City of Durham: 43.71 cents per $100 for 2026-27, according to the city's budget announcement.
  • Owners of residential property in unincorporated Durham County get a solid waste decal with the mailed bill.

The 2025 reappraisal reshaped the rate history. Total taxable value in the county grew from $43 billion in 2019 to more than $70 billion. The county says its rate fell from 0.7987 to a revenue-neutral 0.5192, and the rate finally set for 2025-26 was 0.5542. The rate for 2026-27 is 57.92 cents.

When are Durham County property taxes due?

Durham bills come due September 1, and the county gives until January 5 to pay with no penalty. The 2026 bills were mailed August 10, 2026. Until January 5 an owner may also make partial payments on real property with no interest or added cost.

The county advises paying a bill as soon as it arrives or sending it to the escrow department if a lender pays it. Under the state schedule, January 6 begins a 2% charge, and each month or fraction after February 1 adds three-fourths of a percent.

The statutory lien on a Durham parcel dates from January 1, the listing date, and carries any penalties, interest and costs along with it. A sale later in the year does not remove it; only payment does.

How do I appeal a Durham County property value?

The county tells owners that its tax office can look only at appraised value, and that tax rates, affordability and services fall outside an appeal. If you believe the value is well above or below what the property would have sold for on January 1, 2025, you can appeal.

The cutoff for real property appeals in the 2025 cycle was 5:00 p.m. on June 17, 2026, when the Board of Equalization and Review stopped taking them, and that date has passed. The board can still allow a late application until December 31, and the county advises owners who miss a deadline to apply in future years. Appeals on personal property and vehicles generally run on a 30 day clock from the bill, or from a separate value notice if one was sent.

Evidence the county says helps:

  • An independent appraisal based on comparable sales near the reappraisal date.
  • The deed and related appraisal information.
  • A list of comparable sales from the same period.
  • Surveys, plat maps and photographs, especially of condition problems.

The path has three levels. An informal review with a staff appraiser typically takes 30 to 120 days, and any agreed value is only a recommendation. The Board of Equalization and Review, appointed by the commissioners, makes it final, and attendance is optional. Proof is the taxpayer's job. Beyond that, a petition to the NC Property Tax Commission must go in within 30 days of the board's mailed decision.

What property tax relief does Durham County offer?

The county publishes three state homestead programs plus one local program. The state programs share a June 1 filing date; the elderly and disabled exclusion takes a single application, while the circuit breaker is renewed every year.

Durham County homeowner tax relief programs as printed on the county Tax Relief page
ProgramWhat it doesMain requirement
Elderly/Disabled Homestead ExemptionRemoves $25,000 or half of assessed value, whichever is greater, for the home and up to 1 acreAge 65 or older, or totally and permanently disabled, with 2025 income of $38,800 or less
Circuit Breaker defermentLimits tax to 4% of income, or 5% in the higher tier; the excess is deferredSame age and disability rules, income up to $58,250, and five years of ownership and residence
Disabled Veteran ExclusionRemoves the first $45,000 of appraised valueTotal and permanent service-connected disability; open regardless of age or income
DSS Low Income Homeowner ReliefHelp toward the current bill through a three-tier income modelHousehold at or below 80% of area median income, five or more years in the home, apply through DSS

The county says applications for the DSS program open each September 1, and that it cannot be combined with the homestead exclusion. A circuit breaker owner who sells owes the deferred taxes for the most recent 3 years at the time of the transfer, with interest.

How do taxes work when a Durham County house sells?

Ask Tax Administration for a payoff figure ahead of closing so that the year's bill is settled at the table. A sale can also bring an appraiser to the property, and the county notes that a new structure built after 2025 is valued with the January 1, 2025 market rates.

  • Durham sellers buy the state deed stamp at the register of deeds, a dollar for each five hundred dollars of price, before recording.
  • The county's FAQ says assessed value stays tied to the January 1, 2025 market, so a newer sale price can differ from it.
  • Owners with a deferred circuit breaker balance should request the figure early.

An inherited or tenant-occupied house with a long tax history needs the same payoff request, and the county's relief team can say whether any exclusion should have been on the account.

More questions about Durham County, NC Property Tax Guide

What is the Durham County property tax rate?

The countywide rate approved for 2026-27 is 57.92 cents per $100 of property value. Owners inside the city also pay the City of Durham rate of 43.71 cents per $100.

When are Durham County property taxes due?

They fall due each September 1, with no penalty until after January 5. The 2026 bills went out by mail on August 10, 2026.

Can I still appeal my Durham County property value?

The June 17, 2026 deadline for the 2025 reappraisal cycle has passed. The Board of Equalization and Review has authority to allow a late application until December 31, and you can apply again in future years. Call 919-560-0300 to confirm what the board will accept.

How do I apply for Durham County tax relief?

Apply to the county assessor, by June 1, on Form AV-9 for the elderly or disabled exclusion or circuit breaker, adding the NCDVA-9 form for the disabled veteran exclusion. Call 919-560-0300 for help completing the form.

Who buys the deed stamp on a Durham County sale?

The seller does. The state rate is a dollar per five hundred dollars of price, paid to the register of deeds ahead of recording.

Edgecombe County by the numbers

Who values and who bills property in Edgecombe County?

The assessor and the collector split the job inside the county's Tax Administration department. The assessor appraises property and takes exemption, exclusion and deferment applications. The collector sends bills and chases unpaid ones. Anyone may inspect listing and valuation files from 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM.

  • Taxes paid or owed: the Tax Collector at (252) 641-7810.
  • Value and bill basis questions: the Tax Assessor at (252) 641-7855.
  • Mail for appeals: Edgecombe County Tax Assessor's Office, Attention: Tax Assessor, PO Box 10, Tarboro, NC 27886.

The collector's list of customers covers the county itself, 14 fire districts, one drainage district and eight towns: Conetoe, Leggett, Macclesfield, Pinetops, Princeville, Speed, Sharpsburg and Whitakers. Owners in other municipalities receive a separate bill from that town or city.

What does the Edgecombe County rate table show for each town?

The county's table lists 0.89 per $100 of value for Edgecombe County itself, with each municipality stacking its own rate on top. The sheet is headed 2025, so ask the collector which figures sit on the current bill.

Fourteen fire districts show their own rates too, from 0.07 for Lewis Fire up to 0.145 for Harrison Fire. A solid waste fee of $150.00 appears on the sheet, along with a reduced fee of $60.00. Because the county bills the fire districts and the eight small towns itself, a Pinetops address shows county and town levies together.

What is the January listing rule and the penalty for missing it?

Listing opens on the first business day of January and closes January 31, and the county charges a 10% penalty for each year a form comes in late. Forms for people who have listed before are mailed in late December.

Houses and land follow a permanent listing system, so owners report only when a building was added, altered or removed. A building permit does not count as that report. Mobile homes, campers, boats, untagged vehicles, business equipment and appliances in rentals do need listing.

Whoever owned the property on January 1 answers for the entire year, even after a spring sale. Commissioners may also stretch the listing season, and a person with good cause can ask in writing for a personal extension before the regular period ends.

When do Edgecombe County tax bills come due?

September 1 is the due date, and interest waits until January 6 under G.S. 105-360. It begins at 2% through the end of January, then adds three quarters of one percent for each later month or part of a month.

A county or town may adopt early payment discounts by resolution before May 1 of the due year, so ask the collector whether one is offered when you pay. Payments sent by mail are treated as received on the postmark date.

What steps lead to a lower real estate value in Edgecombe County?

First call the assessor at 252-641-7855 or send the informal review form. That review is open only when the value changed from last year's bill and you are seeing the new number for the first time, and a new owner faces the same test.

If the informal result disappoints you, or you did not qualify, you take a formal appeal to the Board of Equalization and Review, a panel the commissioners appoint from residents who know local real estate. The 2026 notice put the first meeting on Monday, April 6, 2026 at 6:00 PM in the Administration Building, 201 Saint Andrew Street, Tarboro, and set hearing requests to close at 5:00 PM on May 4, 2026. Those dates are behind us, so watch the Rocky Mount Telegram for the next notice.

  • The last revaluation took effect January 1, 2024, and its values stay until the next one.
  • Later swings in the market cannot be weighed in a review.
  • An owner who got word of a change after adjournment has until December 31.
  • Vehicle, business and personal property appeals are due 30 days from the bill date.
  • The next level is the state Property Tax Commission, reached by notice within 30 days of the board's mailed decision (G.S. 105-290).

Which relief programs does the assessor handle?

The assessor receives applications for exemptions, exclusions and deferments. State law offers three homestead paths: an exclusion for elderly or disabled owners, an exclusion for disabled veterans and a circuit breaker deferment. Form AV-9 goes to the county assessor, and the state accepts it through June 1 ahead of the tax year. The state's 2026 income limit is printed as $38,800.

Farm and forest owners have a separate path called Present Use Value, which taxes qualifying land at a use schedule and defers the difference. If the land drops out, the county rolls back the year of the change plus three earlier years.

How does Edgecombe County pursue unpaid property tax?

The collector's tools include foreclosure, sheriff executions, and garnishment of wages, bank accounts and rents. The county keeps a public Tax Foreclosure List that labels each parcel: complaint filed, settlement pending, private sale pending, upset bid period or a posted sale date.

Buyers at these sales leave a 5% deposit, take the property as is, and accept that sales are final, according to the county. Callers who want upset bid details contact the Clerk of Court at 252-824-3200 Ext. 2 with the file number. State law gives ten days after a sale report for an upset bid, and an owner can redeem before confirmation by paying taxes, penalties, interest and costs (G.S. 105-374). An owner whose parcel shows up on the list should phone the collector before the sale date.

What should a seller in Edgecombe County do about taxes before closing?

The collector prepares statements of taxes due for attorneys and real estate professionals, so ask for one before setting the closing date. The register of deeds fee schedule adds that deeds need a tax certification before recording unless the attorney preparer statement appears on the instrument.

Since January 1 ownership fixes responsibility for the whole year, have your closing attorney work out the proration. Use value land needs a new application within 60 days of transfer. Our Edgecombe County register of deeds page covers recording fees.

How does Edgecombe County look in Census data?

The Census Bureau's county profile adds some context.

  • 96.7 residents per square mile at the 2020 count, over 505.44 square miles of land.
  • Typical monthly owner costs of $1,252 with a mortgage and $511 without one.
  • 2.44 people per household across 19,652 households.
  • A 21.1% poverty rate and a middle household income of $51,265.
  • Population growth of 0.5% from April 2020 to July 2025.

More questions about Edgecombe County, NC Property Tax Guide

What does the Edgecombe County sheet list as the county rate?

It lists 0.89 per $100 of value on its 2025 sheet. Towns and fire districts add their own rates, and the sheet also shows a $150.00 solid waste fee.

What is the last day to list property in Edgecombe County?

January 31. Forms must reach the office or carry a postmark by that day, and a late form draws a 10% penalty per year. When the 31st falls on a weekend, the period runs to the next business day.

Where do I start if I think my Edgecombe County value is wrong?

Start with an informal review, by calling 252-641-7855 or sending the review form. If that fails, a formal hearing request goes to the Board of Equalization and Review before the day it adjourns.

Is Edgecombe County property revalued each year?

No. State law sets a revaluation at least every eight years, and the last one here took effect January 1, 2024. Between revaluations a house is relisted only when its buildings change.

How can I see whether an Edgecombe County parcel is facing tax foreclosure?

Open the county's Tax Foreclosure List, which shows each parcel's description, township, number, status and file number. For upset bid details, call the Clerk of Court at 252-824-3200 Ext. 2.

Forsyth County by the numbers

Which Forsyth County office sends the bill?

Forsyth County Tax Administration values real and personal property and collects the county's levy. The office sits in the Government Center at 201 North Chestnut Street, Winston-Salem, with counter service from 8 in the morning until 5 in the afternoon on weekdays and a main line of 336-703-2300.

Mailed payments go to Forsyth County Tax Collector, PO Box 82, Winston-Salem, NC 27102, and a drop box near the parking deck entrance takes payments around the clock. The county's FAQ lists in-person, mail, phone and online options. Credit cards add 2.25 percent with a $2.00 minimum, debit cards add $2.85 and an e-check adds $.20 up to $9,999.99.

As of July 1, 2025 the Census Bureau shows 401,718 residents and 184,703 housing units spread over 407.85 square miles of land. The rate sheet names ten places: Winston-Salem, High Point, Kernersville, King, Clemmons, Lewisville, Rural Hall, Walkertown, Tobaccoville and Bethania.

What is the property tax rate in Forsyth County?

The county rate adopted for fiscal year 2027 is 55.40 cents per $100 of assessed value, up 1.88 cents from the year before.

Commissioners approved a $600.7 million budget on June 4, 2026. The county's budget page says property tax supplies 61 percent of revenue, about $365.9 million, while projected growth in the tax base is only 1 percent. For a median home value of $269,700, the page prints a rise of $50.70 a year, or $4.23 a month, from the new rate. A town or fire district adds its own levy to the county's. The same page shows education as the largest use of funds at $193,464,655, or 32 percent, while sales tax is projected to slip from $110.8 million to $107.3 million, which is why the property tax carries so much weight.

Rows for Clemmons, Lewisville, Bethania and Tobaccoville carry additional fire district and local columns, so the total depends on the parcel's fire district. Winston-Salem also has a business improvement district with an extra levy.

What happens if a Forsyth County bill goes past January 5?

Bills are due September 1 and can be paid without penalty through January 5; after that, interest begins at 2 percent for January and rises by three-fourths of one percent each month.

The county's gap-bill FAQ explains that tax is delinquent when unpaid by the January 5 following the September 1 due date, and that wage garnishment and levy on personal property can begin immediately. The office can also intercept state income tax refunds and lottery winnings through debt setoff. A mailed payment counts on its USPS postmark date, and meter dates from private postage machines do not substitute.

Electronic payments count when the money reaches the collector, not when the owner clicks submit. The county warns that e-checks take several days and that a wrong account number gets the payment rejected, which can push an owner past due. Owners who have fallen behind can ask a revenue collector for a payment agreement, and current owners can begin a prepayment plan in January.

How did the 2025 reappraisal affect Forsyth County values?

Assessed values for real property were reset as of January 1, 2025, and the county describes the value as its estimate of the likely sale price on that date.

State law requires reappraisal at least every eight years, but the county says it has generally reappraised every four years since 1988 to lessen the swings. Notices went out in the first two weeks of February 2025. The county notes that one property can rise or fall independently of its neighbors, and that the change in a bill depends on the new value, personal property owned and the adopted rate. The rate is set separately, usually in May or June.

How can I contest my Forsyth County assessment?

An informal appeal to Tax Administration comes first, and a written request to the Board of Equalization and Review follows if the question stays open.

  • Formal window: January 1 through June 30 unless the county advertises another period, or 15 days after the latest value notice if that falls later.
  • Form: the board's appeal form prints from the parcel's detail page, or the office at 336-703-2300 can send one.
  • Personal property: a written appeal is due 30 days after the first notice or bill.
  • Next level: the North Carolina Property Tax Commission hears a board decision on a notice filed inside the 30 days set by G.S. 105-290, with the state courts above it.

Reappraisal appraisers are often out of the office, so call first and leave a number for a callback or book an appointment. Informal appeals can also be filed online through the county's eNotices portal.

Which relief programs does the Forsyth County office run?

The office takes applications for the three state programs, each due by June 1, and an owner may use only one.

  • Senior or disabled owners with income no higher than $38,800 for 2026 exclude at least $25,000 of value, or half of it when that is larger.
  • Disabled veterans exclude $45,000 on a residence, with Form AV-9 and VA certification of a permanent and total service-connected disability.
  • The circuit breaker limits tax to 4 percent of income, or 5 percent up to $58,200, and defers the difference.

An owner who already holds the senior exclusion reapplies only after moving to a new permanent residence, but the circuit breaker needs a fresh application every year. Disabled applicants attach a certificate from a North Carolina physician or a government agency. If the recipient dies, the person required to list the property tells the office.

How is tax handled when a Forsyth County house sells?

The bill goes to whoever owned the parcel on January 1, and the county's FAQ calls payment at closing the cleanest way to avoid trouble.

Proration between buyer and seller is a private agreement that the Tax Office does not calculate. If the current-year tax is not yet due, the office accepts a prepayment based on the prior year's bill. Session Law 2006-106 relieves a seller of liability for tax assessed on real property transferred before it goes past due, yet the collector can enforce against the parcel's owner on the past-due date.

Two other items can surface in a title search. Delinquent demolition assessments from Winston-Salem, Kernersville or the county can be billed by the tax office and, if unpaid, move a parcel toward foreclosure. Tax foreclosures are run by an outside attorney, with sales at noon at 175 N. Chestnut Street and upset bids of at least 5 percent more and no less than $750 (G.S. 45-21.27).

More questions about Forsyth County, NC Property Tax Guide

What rate applies to Forsyth County bills for fiscal year 2027?

The county rate is 55.40 cents per $100 of assessed value. Town and fire district levies are added, and the rate sheet prints 1.143 as the Winston-Salem total.

Where is the Forsyth County Tax Office?

At 201 North Chestnut Street in Winston-Salem, open on weekdays from 8 a.m. until 5 p.m., with a main line of 336-703-2300. Mail payments to PO Box 82, Winston-Salem, NC 27102.

When does a Forsyth County bill turn delinquent?

After January 5 following the September 1 due date. Interest of 2 percent applies for January, then three-fourths of one percent for each later month.

Can a tax foreclosure in Forsyth County be stopped?

Yes, by paying all taxes, interest and fees. Ask for the foreclosure liaison at 336-703-2300 to get the balance, since an outside attorney runs the case.

Must I renew the senior exclusion each year in Forsyth County?

No, unless the permanent residence changes. Tell the office if income climbs above $38,800 or the disability ends. The circuit breaker is the exception and needs a new application annually.

Who to contact in Franklin County

  • Franklin County Tax Collector

What we confirmed on official pages

  • Tax Collector's Office collects taxes under NC Machinery Act; mail: P.O. Box 503, Louisburg, NC 27549 (page opened; due date/interest text not extracted)

Franklin County by the numbers

Who runs property tax in Franklin County?

The county's Tax Office is split into the Assessor's Office, the Collections Department and GIS/Mapping, and its phone is 919-496-2172. When call volume is heavy, expect voicemail.

Each department has its own job and mailing box:

  • Assessor: lists and values real estate, personal property and registered motor vehicles. Value questions go to the Tax Assessor's Office, P.O. Box 504, Louisburg, NC 27549.
  • Collections: works under the Machinery Act and pursues current and delinquent accounts. Payments and certification requests go to the Tax Collector, P.O. Box 503, Louisburg, NC 27549.
  • GIS/Mapping: keeps the parcel layer for the county.

Growth is the local story. Census estimates put Franklin County at 82,037 residents in mid-2025, up from 68,625 at the 2020 base, across 491.80 square miles of land. Homeowners hold 78.6 percent of occupied housing, the median owner-occupied home is valued at $284,300, and builders pulled 735 permits last year. The average commute is 33.3 minutes.

What is the due date on a Franklin County bill?

A Franklin County bill is due on September 1, and the 2026 bills become delinquent on January 6, 2027.

Statements are produced in late July or early August. Money received before September 1 earns a discount, and prepaying ahead of the bill run is allowed. After the delinquency date the county moves to enforced collection, and G.S. 105-360 adds 2 percent from January 6 to February 1, then three-fourths of one percent for each month or part of one.

Cards are processed by a third party, BIS Online Services, for a non-refundable convenience fee, at 877-768-4775 by phone. A caller needs the tax year, bill number, local zip code and amount; the county office at 919-496-2172 can supply the figure. A past-due notice sometimes crosses with a payment in the mail, so pay ahead of the deadline and include interest if late.

Escrow customers can verify their lender's payment in the second week of September, as the next section explains, and anyone selling should ask the Collections Department for a current balance before setting a closing date.

Why does a Franklin County bill arrive when the lender escrows?

The county mails every bill to the owner of record, and lenders then pick out the ones they are responsible for from a county file.

To confirm the lender paid, search the county's collection site in the second week of September or call 919-496-2172 and choose option 2. The county suggests sending a copy of the bill to the mortgage company with the next house payment. A seller who has already closed should forward the bill to the new owner unless the seller means to pay it. The county treats side agreements among buyers, sellers and attorneys as outside its concern, but because the tax is a lien, a buyer wants each bill settled before closing.

What is the Franklin County tax certification step?

The Franklin County Register of Deeds has refused transfer deeds since April 1, 2015 unless the Tax Collector first certifies that the parcel carries no delinquent tax lien.

Collections provides this service free on weekdays during business hours, closed on county holidays, and a closing attorney or seller can stop by before recording. Mailed requests go to the Tax Collector, P.O. Box 503, Louisburg, NC 27549, with the words Attention: Tax Certification. Electronic filings pass through the certification step automatically.

An open bill can therefore hold up a sale. Settle it directly, or ask the closing agent to pay it from the proceeds so the certificate can be issued.

How do I dispute a Franklin County assessment?

The window for a real estate appeal opens after January 1 and closes when the county board of review adjourns, typically in May, though a value change notice restarts a 30-day clock.

Values rest on the January 1, 2024 revaluation. The county wants the appeal form returned, with all supporting papers, to Franklin County Revaluation, P.O. Box 504, Louisburg, NC 27549, before April. Staff review comes first. When that fails, a hearing before the board is scheduled and a decision is mailed. Anything filed after adjournment waits for the next tax year. A further step goes to the state Property Tax Commission within 30 days of the board's notice, and the owner carries the burden of showing a substantial overstatement.

How the Franklin County Tax Office sorts appeal reasons (source: county Value Appeals page)
Reason offeredCounty position
Bill is higher than before, or income is fixed in retirementNo legal basis
Prices fell or you paid less after January 1, 2024No legal basis under G.S. 105-287
Similar homes carry lower assessed valuesHas a legal basis
Highly similar sales before January 1, 2024 at far lower pricesHas a legal basis
Fire, wind or water damage still unrepaired on January 1Has a legal basis, with proof and photos
Septic permit denied, with a Health Department letterHas a legal basis

Is there relief for Franklin County homeowners on a fixed income?

North Carolina runs three programs and lets each owner pick one: a senior or disability exclusion, a veteran exclusion and the circuit breaker cap.

  • Senior or disabled owners with income at or below the 2026 ceiling of $38,800 shield at least $25,000 of value, or half the value if that is more.
  • Veterans with a qualifying disability exclude $45,000 of value whatever their age or income.
  • The circuit breaker is for owners of five years or more: tax is held to 4 percent of income, or 5 percent when income runs from $38,800 up to $58,200, and the excess is deferred.

Form AV-9 goes to the county assessor, not the state revenue department. The county's appeals page sends retirees to the Tax Assessor's Office for relief questions, since a fixed income does not lower the value itself. A sale triggers repayment of any circuit breaker deferral.

Do Franklin County fees and liens affect a sale?

Yes: a solid waste availability fee rides on bills for any dwelling or business with an electrical hookup, and the tax is a lien on the parcel.

According to the county, the fee funds trash collection and disposal at twelve convenience centers. It is charged for each electrical connection whether or not anyone lives there full time, so a vacant house with power still carries it. Commissioners set the amount each year in the budget ordinance, so ask the Tax Office for the figure on your parcel.

If a bill goes unpaid, G.S. 105-355 attaches the lien as of the listing date and G.S. 105-374 lets the county foreclose it in court through a courthouse-door sale and a 10-day window for increased bids. A bankruptcy filer still gets bills, though the collector cannot pursue delinquent tax during the case.

Owners who inherit a house with back taxes face the same lien as any seller. The tax collector can supply the open years, and G.S. 105-374 lets a redeeming person clear the debt before the court confirms a sale by paying taxes, penalties, interest and costs.

More questions about Franklin County, NC Property Tax Guide

On what date do 2026 Franklin County bills go delinquent?

January 6, 2027, as stated on the county's Collections page, after the September 1 due date.

Will Franklin County record my deed without a tax certification?

Not for a transfer of real property. The Tax Collector has to certify that no delinquent tax lien exists first, and that certification costs nothing during weekday office hours.

Where does a Franklin County value appeal go?

Mail the appeal form and supporting papers to P.O. Box 504, Louisburg, NC 27549. The window runs from January 1 to the board's adjournment, or 30 days from a value change notice.

Does a larger bill justify a lower Franklin County value?

No, the county lists a higher bill or fixed income as having no legal basis. Stronger proof is similar properties with lower values, pre-2024 sales or documented damage.

What number do I use to check or pay a Franklin County bill?

Call 919-496-2172 and choose option 2 to check payments. Card payments by phone go through BIS Online Services at 877-768-4775, with a convenience fee.

Gaston County by the numbers

Who runs property tax in Gaston County?

Gaston County splits the work between the Tax Office, which values property and takes appeals, and the Tax Collector, which bills and collects. Walk-ins go to 128 West Main Avenue, Gastonia, NC 28052, and mail goes to P.O. Box 1578, Gastonia, NC 28053. Weekday hours are 8:30 am to 5 pm.

The main number is 704-866-3158. Extension 1 reaches the Tax Collector's Office, which sits at 100 East Garrison Boulevard in Gastonia, and extension 2 reaches the Real Estate Appraisal Department. Questions about relief programs go to option 6, and exemptions for religious, charitable and similar property go to option 2. Under North Carolina law the assessor lists, appraises and assesses real estate for the county, and the collector uses the remedies in the Machinery Act to collect what is billed.

What are the 2026 property tax rates in Gaston County?

Your bill adds the county rate to the rate for the city or town you live in, or to a fire district rate if you live outside a municipality. The county's 2026 rate chart prints the figures below, and the chart notes that it was produced on June 25, 2026.

The chart also lists a Gastonia downtown service district at 0.2000 and flat city fees labeled as tags. Ask the Tax Office which tax district code your parcel carries before you estimate a bill. The chart shows the county rate at 0.8100 for 2022, 0.6100 for 2023 and 0.5990 from 2024 on.

When are Gaston County property taxes due?

Gaston bills come due September 1, with a grace period through January 5. Taxes become delinquent on January 6.

  • Interest of 2% starts on January 6.
  • Each month after that adds three-quarters of one percent until the balance is paid.
  • Delinquent accounts face levy, wage garnishment, attachment of rent or bank accounts, in rem foreclosure and mortgage style foreclosure.
  • Business personal property is listed during January.

How can I pay my Gaston County tax bill?

You can pay online with your Property Key or parcel ID, name or address, by phone at 980-303-2276, by mail or in person.

Mailed payments go to Gaston County Tax Collector, P.O. Box 1578, Gastonia, NC 28053. The county takes checks and money orders by mail and asks you not to mail cash. The 100 E Garrison Boulevard site has a drive-through for cash, check or money order, and a 2.2% fee applies to cards used inside. Drop boxes are at both tax office locations, 128 W Main Ave and 100 E Garrison Blvd. Credit card payments by web or phone carry a nominal fee and post within 48 hours. For prepayment plans call 704-866-3030 or 704-866-3037.

What is the appeal route for a Gaston County property value?

One form per parcel, signed by the owner or an attorney or attorney in fact, goes to the Tax Office. Gaston's board hears real estate cases in spring.

The board typically adjourns in the last week of April, and the county advertises exact dates in the Gaston Gazette in March. The 2025 board met from April 7 to April 25. A Notice of Value Change gives you whichever is later, adjournment or 30 days after the notice. Personal property can be appealed within 30 days of the bill. Five sworn members chosen by the commissioners sit on the board. A ruling comes within 30 days, with a letter that explains how to reach the state Property Tax Commission. Gaston presumes its value is right. Your evidence must show the value is well above market as of the last reappraisal date.

  • Bring appraisals, comparable sales, photos and, for rentals, income and expense statements.
  • Evidence has to relate to January 1 of the most recent reappraisal year.
  • An appeal cannot be based on inability to pay.

When is the next reappraisal in Gaston County?

The next countywide reappraisal is scheduled for 2027. Gaston has used a four-year cycle, with the last two reappraisals effective January 1, 2019 and January 1, 2023.

State law requires every county to reappraise at least once in eight years, so a four-year cycle is the county's choice. During a reappraisal year the county runs an informal review first. You can use the online form, schedule an appointment with an appraiser or return the form that comes with the reappraisal notice. A decision letter follows, and the value can rise, fall or stay the same. Disagreeing with the informal answer sends you on to the board. Sellers listing in 2027 should read the notice carefully, because a new value changes what a buyer expects the tax to be.

What property tax relief can a Gaston County homeowner get?

Three programs for homeowners apply to a permanent residence, and an owner can receive benefit from only one.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion (G.S. 105-277.1): removes $25,000 or half the assessed value, whichever is larger, from a home and up to an acre. Age 65 or a total and permanent disability, plus income under the yearly limit, is required.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion (G.S. 105-277.1C): up to $45,000 off assessed value for a permanently and totally disabled veteran or an unmarried surviving spouse, with no age or income test. Form NCDVA-9 goes with the application.
  • Circuit breaker (G.S. 105-277.1B): tax capped at 4% of income in the lower bracket and 5% in the next, after five years of owning and living in the home, with a fresh application every year.

Apply between January 1 and June 1. Later applications need approval from the Board of Equalization and Review. The county prints its own income thresholds, and they adjust yearly, so ask the Tax Office on option 6 for the current limit. Present use value for farm and forest land needs 10 acres of agriculture, 5 of horticulture or 20 of forestry, and applications are due in January.

What happens to my tax relief and unpaid tax when I sell in Gaston County?

A sale ends your personal relief and can start a bill for deferred tax. If a residence is sold or the owner dies between January 1 and July 1, the elderly or disabled exclusion is removed for that year, and after July 1 it stays for the current year and drops off the next January 1.

Selling ends circuit breaker status, and three years of deferred tax then become payable with interest. Farm and forest land that leaves present use value is billed the difference for the current and three prior years, and a buyer has 60 days to file for continued use. Because unpaid tax is a lien, a title company will want the bill cleared at closing. Our Gaston County Register of Deeds guide shows where the deed is filed once the tax is settled.

More questions about Gaston County, NC Property Tax Guide

What is the Gaston County property tax rate for 2026?

The county rate printed on the 2026 chart is 0.5990, and you add your city or fire district rate, such as 0.4700 for Gastonia or 0.1150 for most fire districts. Ask the Tax Office which district your parcel is in.

When do Gaston County property taxes become delinquent?

They become delinquent on January 6. Bills are due September 1, and 2% interest starts January 6 followed by three-quarters of one percent monthly.

Where do I file a challenge to my Gaston County assessment?

Filing must wrap up before the board adjourns, which the county says is usually the last week of April. A Notice of Value Change gives you the later of adjournment or 30 days.

Can I pay Gaston County property tax by phone?

Yes. Call 980-303-2276 and have your property key number from the top right corner of the tax bill. A nominal card fee applies.

When is the next Gaston County reappraisal?

The county's next countywide reappraisal is scheduled for 2027, after reappraisals effective January 1, 2019 and January 1, 2023.

Granville County by the numbers

Which Granville County office deals with my tax bill?

Granville County Tax Administration, reachable at 919-693-4181, is the single contact for valuation, relief programs and billing questions. The county's FAQ routes almost everything there.

A contracted appraiser fills the assessor's role for informal real estate appeals. The next level up, the Board of Equalization and Review, is staffed by the commissioners themselves. Granville has five municipalities (Butner, Creedmoor, Oxford, Stem and Stovall), and the county bill carries each town's levy next to its own.

Owners who live outside every municipal boundary, along with owners inside Stovall, owe a fire district tax as well. The county says that revenue is restricted to fire protection.

What rate will I pay on a Granville County parcel?

The county rate is 0.631 per $100 of value on the county's rate page, and a town or fire district rate gets added to it depending on where the parcel sits. Inside a town you add the town rate. In the countryside, or in Stovall, you add the fire district rate.

Rates per $100 as printed by Granville County (https://granvillecounty.org/303/Tax-Rates-within-Granville-County)
JurisdictionRate per $100
County rate0.631
Fire service district0.06
City of Oxford0.57

City of Creedmoor0.58
Town of Stovall0.355
Town of Stem0.35

The county's own method is value multiplied by the combined rate and divided by 100. To confirm which districts touch a specific address, call the tax office, because the district boundaries decide which rows count.

What are the payment dates and the early discount?

Granville knocks 1.5% off a current-year bill paid between July 1 and August 15. After that the bill is due September 1, and interest begins to accrue once January 5 passes.

  • July 1 to August 15: early payment discount of 1.5%.
  • September 1: standard due date under G.S. 105-360.
  • January 5: final day at face amount.
  • After that: 2% through February 1, then three-fourths of one percent per month or fraction.

The county's payment page lists online, mail, counter, bank bill pay and phone options. It also offers e-billing through its card vendor, with alerts whenever a balance, an owner or a due date changes. A mailed check is judged by its postmark, so do not wait for the last day.

When is the next Granville County revaluation?

The next countywide revaluation is set for 2030. Assessed real estate values reflect market conditions on January 1, 2024, and stay in place until then.

Granville finished a reappraisal in 2018 and then ran on the state's eight-year schedule. In 2020 the Department of Revenue told the county that tax values and sale prices were pulling apart and urged a shorter cycle, so the commissioners moved to six years. The county's FAQ says average home sale prices in the county are up 27% since 2021.

Frozen valuation dates cut two ways. A later market swing, up or down, cannot be used to argue for a different value. A factual mistake on the parcel record, such as wrong acreage, a missing demolition or a building listed that is not there, can be argued at any time during the appeal window.

In a revaluation year the sequence runs: notices in January or February, informal appeals February through April, board hearings starting in April, board adjournment in June and a new rate on July 1.

How can a Granville County owner contest a value?

An owner moves through three stages in order: informal review by the assessor, a hearing before the commissioners sitting as the equalization board, and finally the state Property Tax Commission.

  • Send in the county's Assessor's Appeal Form early. The appraiser writes back, and accepting the answer ends the matter.
  • If you do not accept it, phone 919-693-4181 and ask for a board hearing. Dates begin near the end of April and run into early June, per the county FAQ.
  • Last, give the Property Tax Commission written notice within 30 days of the date the board mailed you its decision (G.S. 105-290).

In years without a revaluation, appeals open January 1 and the cutoff is the day the board adjourns, never later than early June. Only an owner whose value was changed with notice sent after adjournment gets extra time.

Personal property is a different track. An owner has 30 days from the first notice to contest, a conference follows, and a written request to the board must come within 30 days after the final answer. Vehicles are covered on a separate county page. A review may leave the number alone, lower it or raise it.

Which relief programs could lower a Granville County bill?

The state runs three, and the tax office at 919-693-4181 can say which one fits. An owner gets only one of them.

  • G.S. 105-277.1, for seniors and disabled owners: the larger of $25,000 or half of a home's appraised value drops off the tax roll. NCDOR's 2026 sheet shows a $38,800 income limit.
  • G.S. 105-277.1C, for disabled veterans: $45,000 of value drops off, whatever the owner's age or income.
  • G.S. 105-277.1B, the circuit breaker: the bill is limited to 4.0% or 5.0% of income, and the difference is deferred as a lien.

Applications use Form AV-9 and go to the county assessor, who must take them through June 1. A circuit breaker home that sells triggers repayment of deferred tax for the last three fiscal years, so mention the program to your closing agent.

What happens to a Granville County tax balance when a house sells?

The balance is a lien on the parcel and attaches as of the January 1 listing date (G.S. 105-355), together with penalties, interest and costs.

Ask Granville County Tax Administration, in writing, for the amount due on the current bill and any deferred amount tied to a relief program, then give those figures to whoever runs the closing.

A balance left alone can end in a court-ordered sale at the courthouse door (G.S. 105-374), though an owner may redeem before confirmation. Paying it off stops that. The new deed is recorded in Oxford, and the seller pays the state excise tax of $1.00 per $500, or fractional part, before the clerk files it.

How populous and how owner-heavy is Granville County?

Census QuickFacts puts the county at 61,421 people in 2025, living on roughly 532 square miles of land, which is about 115 for each square mile.

  • Owner-occupancy: 77.1% of occupied homes (2020 to 2024).
  • Middle value of an owner's home: $247,700.
  • Middle household income: $71,111.
  • Middle gross rent: $1,008.
  • Residents 65 or older: 20.0%.
  • Typical commute to work: 30.8 minutes.

The county also counts 25,685 housing units and 22,474 households, with a typical household of 2.52 people. A one-in-five senior population makes the age-based exclusion worth asking about. These are countywide midpoints, and a specific parcel can sit well away from them.

More questions about Granville County, NC Property Tax Guide

What is Granville County's county tax rate?

The county's rate page prints 0.631 per $100 of value. Your town or the fire district adds its own rate, and the same page lists each one.

Does paying early save money in Granville County?

Yes. The county takes 1.5% off current-year bills paid from July 1 through August 15. The regular due date is September 1.

By when must a Granville County value be challenged?

In a year without revaluation the deadline is the day the Board of Equalization and Review adjourns, no later than early June. Begin with the assessor's form.

Who can claim the $25,000 or half-value exclusion?

A homeowner age 65 or older, or totally and permanently disabled, who occupies the home and keeps income under the limit, which NCDOR prints as $38,800 for 2026. Apply on Form AV-9.

Where is a Granville County deed recorded?

At the Register of Deeds in the courthouse at 101 Main Street, Oxford, phone 919-693-6314. The seller pays the excise tax to that office before recording.

What we confirmed on official pages

  • Taxes due at par on or before January 5, after which interest begins; 0.5% discount if paid by August 31 (per FAQ)
  • Board of Equalization and Review appeal: on or before May 15 each year for the current tax year (per Guilford FAQ)

Guilford County by the numbers

Which Guilford County offices value property and take payment?

Guilford County's Tax Department sets values and mails bills, and walk-in help comes from two buildings: 400 W. Market St. in Greensboro and 325 E. Russell Ave. in High Point. Both are staffed on weekdays, 8 a.m. until 5 p.m.

Guilford dates to 1771 and has a courthouse in each of its two big cities. According to the state encyclopedia, county government relocated to Greensboro in 1808. Census Bureau estimates credit the county with 562,234 people in mid-2025 on 645.92 square miles of land, so a listing might be a High Point bungalow or acreage near Summerfield.

Payment channels the department lists:

  • The Pay It portal, online or at (336) 203-7795, adds a 1.85% electronic fee and a $2 transaction fee.
  • Mailed checks are made payable to Guilford County Tax Department and sent to a Charlotte lockbox address, P.O. Box 70939, zip 28272-0939.
  • Counter payments accept cash, checks and cards, and card payers add 2.35% plus $2. Gift cards cannot be used.

How did the 2026 reappraisal and moratorium affect Guilford bills?

Bills for 2026 carried 2025 values, so the reappraisal numbers debut on the 2027 bill. Senate Bill 889 put a one-year hold on the reappraisal that began January 1, 2026, and the county confirms that Guilford is covered.

State revenue officials told Guilford in April 2023 to reappraise because most parcels were selling above their assessed values. Staff appraisers did the work themselves, and owners received notices in February 2026. The county lists 2032 as the following reappraisal year.

An owner who had already appealed the 2026 value keeps that appeal alive, according to the county, and it carries to the next bill. Commissioners set the fiscal year 2026-27 rate at 78.95 cents per $100, which is 5.9 cents higher than before. The rate went up in 2026 while the new values arrive in 2027, so the two changes land in different years.

When do Guilford County tax bills come due, and when does interest begin?

State law makes September 1 the day a bill is payable, and a payment on or before January 5 owes no interest. Guilford's FAQ agrees with the January 5 cutoff and expects bills in the first half of July.

A prepayment discount rewards early payers. The FAQ prints 0.5% for payment by August 31, while the county's moratorium notice said payers who beat Monday, August 31, 2026 would still get 1%. Ask the Tax Department which figure fits your bill.

After the cutoff, interest starts at 2% for month one and 0.75% per month beyond that. The county says collection steps begin immediately: garnishment of wages and bank accounts, levies on personal property, attachment of state refunds and lottery prizes, and eventually foreclosure. The department adds that it never runs tax lien sales.

Mailed payments are timed by postmark. Without a Postal Service postmark, the day the office receives the envelope counts, and the taxpayer must prove it was on time.

How does a Guilford County owner dispute an assessment?

Put the appeal in writing and send it to the Board of Equalization and Review any time from January 1 to May 15. The 5 p.m. cutoff moves to the following working day when May 15 lands on a weekend or holiday. The county accepts online filings, and the paper form is available from 336-641-4814.

Under the moratorium law, the board's page keeps 2026 appeals open through December 31, 2026 and lets 2027 appeals run to May 17, 2027. The online portal reopens January 1, 2027, and taxreval@guilfordcountync.gov can mail a form earlier.

A county appraiser looks at the file and offers a recommendation. Accepting it closes the matter. Rejecting it earns a hearing date before the five-member board, where the county value starts out presumed correct and the owner must bring proof. Guilford lists useful proof:

  • Closed sales of similar homes near the reappraisal date, an appraisal from the year before, or a contractor quote that attaches a dollar figure to a defect.
  • Wrong square footage on the property record card, and outside influences like a flood zone.

The board will not act on the size of an increase or on hardship paying, and it excludes forced sales from its comparables. Further review sits with the state Property Tax Commission, which takes a notice filed within 30 days after the board mails its ruling.

Which Guilford County relief programs reduce what a homeowner owes?

Guilford administers three programs, and an owner can collect from only one. June 1 is the filing deadline. A late packet goes to the review board if the Tax Department has it a full week ahead of the board's final December session.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: shelters $25,000 or 50% of the home's value from tax, whichever is greater. The owner must be 65, or totally and permanently disabled, on January 1, and the county's page puts the gross income ceiling at $38,800. It needs one application.
  • Circuit breaker: caps the yearly bill at 4% of income, or 5% when income falls between $38,800 and $58,200. Five years of owning and living in the home are required, and the owner reapplies annually.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: shelters the first $45,000 of value with no age or income test. It serves a veteran whose service-connected disability is total and permanent, and that veteran's unmarried surviving spouse.

Sellers should look hardest at the circuit breaker. Tax above the cap is postponed and stays on the parcel as a lien. Once the home changes hands, three years of postponed tax come due with interest. The exclusions carry no repayment. Applications can be mailed to PO Box 3138 in Greensboro (27402) or handed in at either tax office. The relief help lines are 336-641-3320 and 336-641-7911.

What are the main Guilford County property tax figures at a glance?

Guilford County property tax dates and figures
ItemWhat the official page printsWhere it comes from
County rate, fiscal year 2026-2778.95 cents per $100County budget announcement, June 25, 2026
Appeal windowJanuary 1 to May 15, 5 p.m.Board of Equalization and Review page
Relief application deadlineJune 1Property Tax Relief Programs page
Early-payment discount0.5% if paid by August 31Tax Department FAQ
Next reappraisal2032Property Tax Moratorium Information Hub

What should a Guilford seller do about a tax balance?

Pay it off no later than closing. The state attaches the lien to a parcel as of its January 1 listing date, with interest and penalties riding along, so a buyer's title search will turn it up.

If a lender escrows your taxes, the servicer requests the bill from the county, and the department says a notice reaches you around mid to late July. The notice leaves the legal duty with you, so confirm the amount was paid. Without escrow, pay directly before interest starts.

Taxes left unpaid can lead to a court foreclosure modeled on a mortgage foreclosure. It culminates in a sale at the courthouse door, followed by ten days in which a higher bid may be filed once the commissioner reports. Selling first keeps the price with you. The Tax Department's bill search will show what is owed, and our register of deeds guide explains how the deed records afterward.

Items worth checking before listing a Guilford house:

  • A circuit breaker deferral that comes due on transfer.
  • A parcel record that no longer matches the house after an addition. An online Property Verification form fixes this, and the county says the record card updates in about 48 hours.
  • Vehicle gap bills, which arrive separately from the real estate bill.

What does the Census say about housing in Guilford County?

The Census Bureau counts 246,403 housing units in Guilford, and 59.9% of occupied homes are owner-occupied. The middle owned home is worth $259,900 in the 2020 to 2024 figures. Owners with a mortgage pay a median $1,536 a month and those without pay $515, while renters pay a median $1,163.

The median household income is $68,642 in 2024 dollars. Builders drew 2,876 permits in Guilford during 2025, and seniors make up 18.0% of the population, the group the relief programs target.

More questions about Guilford County, NC Property Tax Guide

Were Guilford's 2026 tax bills based on the new reappraisal?

No, they used 2025 values because Senate Bill 889 paused the reappraisal for a year. The new values apply to the 2027 bill, appeals filed against them are still processed, and the county lists 2032 as the next reappraisal.

When must a Guilford property owner file a value appeal?

In an ordinary year the cutoff is 5 p.m. on May 15, and the appeal has to be in hand or postmarked by then. The moratorium law extended 2026 appeals to December 31, 2026 and set May 17, 2027 for 2027 appeals, per the board's page.

Can seniors or veterans pay less property tax in Guilford County?

Yes. Owners who are 65 or older, or totally disabled, and under the income cap can shelter $25,000 or half the home's value, whichever is larger. Qualifying disabled veterans can shelter $45,000. File with the Tax Department by June 1.

What becomes due if a circuit breaker owner sells?

Three years of deferred tax, plus interest, come due on the transfer date, because a sale ends eligibility. Ask the Tax Department for a payoff figure before closing.

How can I pay the Guilford County tax bill?

Choose the Pay It portal online or by phone, a mailed check, or a visit to the Greensboro or High Point office. Cards add a fee, and gift cards are refused.
