What we could not confirm

  • Recording hours, e-recording

Halifax County by the numbers

Which office values property and collects tax in Halifax County?

A single department, Tax Administration, does the work that many counties split between an assessor and a collector. Staff appraise houses and business equipment, send the bill, take the payment, review relief and exemption requests, and keep the ownership records, tax maps and GIS layers.

The office sits at 357 Ferrell Lane in the town of Halifax (zip 27839), with P.O. Box 68 as the mailing address. Call 252-583-2121. The counter runs half past eight to five, Monday to Friday. The county's pay page has a link for paying property tax online.

Halifax sits on the fall line of the Roanoke River, where the Coastal Plain meets the Piedmont. Edgecombe County gave up the land for it in 1758, and the town of Halifax became the seat. Other communities the state encyclopedia names are Roanoke Rapids, Weldon, Littleton, Enfield, Scotland Neck and Hobgood. Census data estimates 46,534 residents for July 2025 over 723.74 square miles of land. The 2020 density was about 67 people for each square mile.

Why must Halifax County taxes be settled before a deed can record?

A county rule dated January 1, 2016 tells the Register of Deeds to refuse any deed that moves title to real property until the Tax Collector certifies the described parcel carries no lien for delinquent property tax or any other tax the collector enforces.

For a seller, that is a gate in front of closing. Staff need time to research the parcel, so the deed has to reach the collector's office by 4:30 p.m., and not before 8:30 a.m. Ask your closing attorney to confirm the certification is finished before recording is scheduled.

The county also handles town taxes through a tax agency fund. Request a payoff figure well ahead of closing and ask whether a municipal balance shows on the parcel.

What property tax rates apply in Halifax County?

The ordinance for the year beginning July 1, 2026 levies $0.70 on every $100 of property listed as of January 1, 2026. Five cents of it is reserved to repay the installment contract dated May 26, 2016 that financed the school replacing Manning Elementary.

More layers may sit on top, depending on location. The same ordinance covers school supplements, fire districts and town collections for Enfield, Halifax, Hobgood, Littleton, Roanoke Rapids, Scotland Neck and Weldon.

Halifax County levies in the fiscal year 2026-27 budget ordinance
LevyRate per $100 as printed
County general levy$0.70
Part of the levy for school debt$0.05
School supplement, Weldon-Halifax Administrative Unit$0.20
School supplement, Halifax County Schools Administrative Unit$0.10
Special fire districts$0.0401 (Tillery) to $0.0905 (Davie)

Source: Halifax County fiscal year 2026-27 budget ordinance. The county's valuation estimate is $4,975,269,130, with a 98.2% collection rate. Separate rates apply in eleven fire districts: Arcola, Darlington, Davie, Enfield, Halifax, Hobgood, Littleton, Rheasville, Scotland Neck, Tillery and Weldon. A call to the tax office will tell you your district and whether a town rate applies.

What is the payment calendar for Halifax County property tax?

Under state law the bill is payable September 1, and a payment made through January 5 carries no interest. Interest then runs at 2% for the rest of January and at three-fourths of a percent for each month or part month afterward.

Listing happens in January and closes January 31, though commissioners can add 30 days in an ordinary year or 60 in a revaluation year. A prepayment discount exists only when the governing board adopts a schedule ahead of the due date, so ask Tax Administration whether Halifax offers one. The postmark governs mailed checks.

The county budget moves $100,000 into a revaluation fund for 2026-27. Reappraisal of real property is required at least every eight years, and counties with 75,000 or more residents must move up the date if sales ratios stray outside .85 to 1.15. Halifax has fewer people than that. The tax office can tell you the year your current values took effect.

How does a Halifax County owner contest a valuation?

Start with the county's equalization board, formally the Board of Equalization and Review. Commissioners fill that role unless a separate board has been created, and the board starts meeting in April or early May. The request for a hearing must reach it before it adjourns.

In years without a revaluation the board finishes in a few weeks and stops by July 1. In a revaluation year it can work until December 1. A decision follows within a month of adjournment. The next level is the state Property Tax Commission, where a written notice stating your grounds is due thirty days after the board's mailing, with a copy for the assessor.

Boards respond to evidence tied to the revaluation date, such as sales of similar homes, an independent appraisal or repair quotes. Tax Administration can give you that date for Halifax.

Which relief programs can a Halifax County homeowner claim?

Three state programs exist, and each owner may use just one. Form AV-9 goes to the county assessor rather than to state revenue officials. January is the intended window, yet the assessor must accept applications through June 1 before the tax year begins.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: excludes $25,000 or 50% of the home's appraised value, whichever is more. The owner is a North Carolina resident who, as of January 1, is at least 65 or totally and permanently disabled and whose income falls below the limit that the state form prints as $38,800 for 2026.
  • Circuit breaker: holds the bill to 4% of income, or 5% for income between the limit and $58,200. The owner needs five years of owning and living in the home. Postponed tax stays as a lien and falls due when the home transfers.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: excludes $45,000 of value, and no age or income test applies. Form NCDVA-9 is completed first with a Veterans Service Officer and then filed with the assessor.

Census figures show seniors at 25.2% of Halifax's population, and 16.3% of people under 65 report a disability. Guilford County shows 18.0% and 8.8%. The programs are aimed at exactly these groups.

What follows if Halifax County property tax is left unpaid?

Unpaid tax becomes a lien from the January 1 listing date. To collect, the county files a foreclosure suit locally, and notice goes to the record owner, the spouse and other lienholders.

Halifax advertises each scheduled tax foreclosure on its website. Its published sale rules say:

  • Bidding happens in the courthouse's lower lobby in the town of Halifax.
  • Every bid stays open to upset for 10 days.
  • Property sells as is, and neither the county nor the commissioner warrants title or condition.
  • Bidders should consider a title examination, and skipping one does not release a bid.

Before confirmation, an owner can redeem by paying the tax bill together with penalties, interest and court costs. Any money left after the taxes is held by the court for those entitled to it. Selling beforehand leaves the equity in your hands. Call the county Legal Department at 252-583-3612 about a scheduled sale.

How does Halifax County's housing market look in the Census data?

The Census Bureau counts 25,078 homes and apartments in July 2025. Owners occupy 62.9% of the occupied ones, the survey's middle value for an owned home is $106,200 (2020 through 2024), and the middle rent is $813.

The middle household earns $45,590 in 2024 dollars, and the poverty rate is 18.8%. Permit activity was light, with just 75 permits for new building in 2025, and the population estimate is 4.3% below the April 2020 base. Recording after a sale is covered in our Halifax County register of deeds guide.

More questions about Halifax County, NC Property Tax Guide

Where do I find Halifax County Tax Administration?

At 357 Ferrell Lane in Halifax, with P.O. Box 68 for mail and 252-583-2121 for calls. One department handles both valuation and collection, and service runs half past eight to five on weekdays.

Which tax rate does Halifax County charge?

The 2026-27 ordinance sets $0.70 per $100 for the county. Two school administrative units add $0.20 or $0.10, and fire districts and towns add rates that vary by parcel location.

Must a seller clear delinquent taxes before a Halifax County closing?

Yes. A county rule in force since January 1, 2016 bars the register from taking a deed until the Tax Collector certifies the parcel has no delinquent tax lien. Pay any balance first so the certification can issue.

Is it possible to challenge a Halifax County assessment?

Yes. Request a hearing from the county's equalization board before it adjourns in spring. If the board's decision disappoints you, the Property Tax Commission accepts an appeal filed thirty days after the mailing at the latest.

What is a Halifax County tax foreclosure sale like?

It is a public auction in the courthouse lobby. Each bid stays open to a higher offer for 10 days, the house sells as is with no title warranty, and the county posts each notice on its website.

Harnett County by the numbers

Where do I go with a Harnett County property tax question?

The Harnett County Tax Department, based in Lillington, lists, appraises and bills every parcel in the county, and its Collection Division takes the payments. For a value, call the Real Property Division at 910-814-6920. For a bill or a payment, call 910-893-7520 or write to taxinfo@harnett.org.

Collections are at 305 W. Cornelius Harnett Blvd, Suite 101, Lillington, NC 27546. The register of deeds uses the same street address at Suite 200, which is handy when a sale needs both a payoff figure and a recorded deed.

Real property is listed automatically every year, so owners do not receive an annual listing form. The county does ask owners to report new structures and additions, and its appraisers work from building permits issued by the county or a municipal permit office.

Which dates drive a Harnett County tax bill?

The Harnett payment clock starts September 1 and stays penalty-free through January 5. On January 6 the balance picks up 2%, then 3/4% for every further month, as in G.S. 105-360.

The 2026 bills went into the mail on August 28, 2026, and January 5, 2027 is the final day before delinquency. Owners can pay in equal monthly amounts or in any amount they choose while the bill is open, and each payment is applied to the bill with an updated statement mailed back.

Harnett County tax calendar as printed by the county
ItemWhat the county page says
Bills dueSeptember 1

Interest2% on January 6, then 3/4% each month
PrepaymentsAccepted February through August
Early-pay discountNone offered on ad valorem tax
Advertisement of liensIn or after March each year

Source: Harnett County Collection Division.

What are the payment options and fees in Harnett County?

Bills can be settled through the online portal, the phone line at 1-866-580-9996, the mail, or the counter, and only the counter takes cash. Checks, certified checks and money orders work at the counter or through the mail.

  • Personal debit cards carry a $3.80 convenience fee per transaction.
  • Credit cards are charged 2.50% of the balance.
  • Business credit or debit cards on high-rewards programs carry 3.25%.
  • E-checks carry $2.00 per transaction.

The processor keeps those fees. A bounced check voids the payment, and the bill is charged the larger of 10% of the check or $25.00. The office makes no payment arrangements once a bill is delinquent, so installment payers should begin before January 6.

How does Harnett County value a house?

The Real Property Division sets fair market value for the county's 73,000-plus parcels with a CAMA system. Inputs include site visits, zoning and soil classes, deeds, market sales and aerial photos.

The last reappraisal took effect January 1, 2022. On the revenue department's recommendation, the commissioners then moved the county to a four-year cycle, which put the next reappraisal at January 1, 2026. State law sets the outer limit at eight years under G.S. 105-286.

A structure is valued by its percent complete on January 1. A garage finished in March therefore adds nothing to that year's bill. That timing matters for a seller who has just built or renovated, because the value on the bill may lag the real condition of the house.

Can I dispute my Harnett County assessment?

Start by asking the Real Property Division how it handles value reviews after the 2026 reappraisal, and go to the county's review board if that conversation leaves a gap. Commissioners usually sit as that board, and G.S. 105-322 sets its opening session between the first Monday of April and the first Monday of May.

  • Request a hearing, by letter or by appearing, before the board adjourns.
  • A written decision follows within a month of adjournment.
  • A further appeal goes to the Property Tax Commission, with notice due thirty days after that decision is mailed.

Bring comparable sales close to the house, contractor estimates and dated photos. A value tied to January 1 of the reappraisal year is easier to contest with evidence from that date.

Which relief programs apply to Harnett County homeowners?

Harnett County points owners to an exemptions page and to a present-use value program for farm and forest land. Three state programs for a permanent residence run through the assessor on Form AV-9, and an owner may draw on just one of them.

  • An elderly or disabled owner can exclude the larger of $25,000 or half the assessed worth of the home, if 2025 income stayed under $38,800.
  • A disabled veteran's home gets a flat $45,000 cut in taxable value, with no age or income test.
  • The circuit breaker holds tax to 4.0% of income, or 5.0% for incomes between $38,800 and $58,200, and defers the remainder as a lien.

File during the January listing period; late forms are still taken until June 1. The deferral ends at transfer, and the deferred taxes for the three prior fiscal years are then payable, so a seller using it should expect that balance at closing.

What follows when a Harnett County bill goes unpaid?

Liens on unpaid real estate tax are advertised each spring. The 2025 list ran in The Daily Record on May 12, 2026, under the name of the owner on January 6, with an advertising fee added to the bill.

Harnett mostly uses the mortgage-style foreclosure method, a civil action ending in a courthouse-steps auction by a court-appointed commissioner. The county page calls for a 10% deposit at the sale, then a 10-day upset bid window, and each upset bid must top the last by 5% or $750, whichever is greater. The owner can redeem before confirmation by paying all taxes, fees and costs.

The county adds that the state issues no tax lien certificates, so an outsider who pays someone else's delinquent bill gets no title. Foreclosure usually comes after the office has tried bank attachments, wage garnishment, rent attachment and a sheriff's levy.

What changes for tax when a Harnett County house is sold?

Whoever owns the parcel at closing settles its tax, and the payoff is taken out of sale money at the closing table. Get a written balance from the Collection Division, with interest and any advertising fee included, before closing is scheduled.

The register of deeds collects a separate deed tax before recording, and the seller carries it. A house with delinquent tax, a foreclosure filing or a deferred balance can still sell, provided the lender and tax office are paid in the right order.

County numbers help set expectations for pricing and timing:

  • The 2025 population estimate is 150,137 residents, 12.4% above the 2020 base.
  • Housing units: 59,085, with 71.0% owner-occupied.
  • Typical owner-occupied house value for 2020-2024: $246,200.
  • Median household income: $71,287, with a 32.8-minute average commute.
  • Permits issued during 2025: 2,205 (Census QuickFacts).

More questions about Harnett County, NC Property Tax Guide

Does Harnett County reward early payment?

No. The county page states that Harnett County offers no discount on ad valorem property tax. Owners can make prepayments from February through August, which spreads the cost but earns no reduction.

Final day to pay a Harnett bill without a penalty?

January 5, following the September 1 due date. For the 2026 bills that is January 5, 2027, and interest begins the next morning.

Is a sale possible while Harnett taxes are unpaid?

Yes. The title agent remits the tax, interest and any advertising fee out of the seller's funds, so request an up-to-date payoff figure from the Collection Division first. A filed foreclosure case adds court costs and attorney fees to that figure.

Does Harnett County reappraise property every year?

No. The county moved to a four-year cycle after its January 1, 2022 reappraisal, and its next scheduled reappraisal is January 1, 2026. Between reappraisals, values change when a property changes, such as new construction or an addition.

Where do I pay or ask about a Harnett County tax bill?

Use the online portal, the phone line at 1-866-580-9996, the mail, or the counter at 305 W. Cornelius Harnett Blvd, Suite 101, Lillington. Questions about a bill go to 910-893-7520 or taxinfo@harnett.org.

Haywood County by the numbers

Whom do I call at Haywood County about a bill?

Two offices inside the Historic Haywood Courthouse in Waynesville share the job. The Tax Assessor's Office sets values from Suite 220, and Tax Collections sends bills and takes money from Suite 224, both at 215 N. Main Street.

Call 828-452-6643 for Collections, including questions about partial payments and the amount needed to clear a parcel before a sale. The reappraisal questions line at the assessor is 828-452-6734.

A Haywood bill can include more than a county rate. The county collects for 22 fire districts, 10 road maintenance districts and one sanitation district, and owners of improved property, including manufactured homes and campers, pay a landfill fee on top.

Haywood covers 553.56 square miles of land and counted about 63,369 residents in its July 2025 estimate, a 2.1% gain since 2020. Commutes average 23.8 minutes. The Census Bureau also reports 4,981 veterans for 2020-2024, a group the state's veteran exclusion is meant to help.

What is the Haywood County tax calendar?

Haywood mails bills in late August or early September. Payment is expected in September, and nothing accrues through January 5. Once that day passes, a 2% charge applies, then 3/4% more each time a new month begins, until the account is cleared.

Haywood County tax dates from the county's own pages
DateWhat happens
January 1Who owns a parcel is determined for the tax year
Late August to early SeptemberBills mailed to owners
SeptemberTaxes due
January 5Last day without interest
After January 52% charge, then 3/4% monthly
MarchUnpaid real estate taxes advertised with a fee added

Sources: Haywood County Office of Tax Collections FAQ and Tax Collections.

Anyone unable to clear a bill by January 5 can ask Collections about a fixed monthly payment. The statewide interest rule sits in G.S. 105-360.

Where and how do Haywood County owners pay?

Choices include the website, the phone line at 1-877-729-8290, the mail, a dropbox outside the Historic Courthouse, and cash at the Collections counter. A processor, not the county, collects 3% on cards (online or by phone) and 2% on e-checks.

  • The dropbox takes checks and money orders only. Never leave cash in it.
  • Mail goes to the address on the bill. The county changed its lockbox to PO Box 96270, Charlotte, and a returned payment can be resent to the Waynesville office in its original envelope, keeping the first postmark.
  • Lenders and escrow companies do not receive bills from the county, so owners whose mortgage servicer pays the tax should forward their copy.

Why was the Haywood County revaluation moved to 2027?

After Hurricane Helene, Haywood County pushed its reappraisal back two years, from 2025 to January 1, 2027, and checked with the state that the delay was permitted. The announcement is dated November 5, 2024.

In the meantime, most parcels kept their 2025 values unless something changed, such as an addition, an update, new construction or flooding. The 2027 numbers will track the market as it stands then, which could move a Waynesville or Maggie Valley assessment a long way.

Commissioners took comments on the proposed schedule of values, standards and rules for 2027 at a hearing on October 19, 2026, and the schedules are on view in the second-floor assessor's office. State law requires reappraisal at least every eighth year, as set out in G.S. 105-286.

What if my Haywood County house was storm-damaged or overvalued?

Fill out the county's Damage Report Form and send it to the assessor in person, by post, or to personalproperty@haywoodcountync.gov. A seller with a flooded house should do this so the assessment matches what the house is now.

Disputes over real property value are heard by Haywood's review board, which has five appointed members and one alternate on one-year terms. The assessor schedules its meetings as the need arises.

  • Ask to be heard before adjournment, as G.S. 105-322 requires.
  • Expect the written result within a month of adjournment.
  • A Property Tax Commission appeal must be filed within thirty days of the board's mailed notice.

Does Haywood County offer homestead-type relief?

Yes, through three state programs that apply to a permanent residence. With 28.2% of residents 65 or over, the age-based ones matter here. Form AV-9 goes to the assessor, and an owner qualifies for only one program.

  • Owners aged 65 or older, or disabled, can shelter half the value or $25,000 if that is larger, if income is at or under $38,800 for 2026.
  • A veteran with a permanent and total service-connected disability shelters $45,000 of value.
  • The circuit breaker limits tax to a share of income (4.0% or 5.0%) after five years of living in the home, and defers the rest.

Forms are due in the January listing period but are taken through June 1. A deferral ends on transfer, so it shows up as a closing item for a seller.

How do the Census numbers shape a Haywood County sale?

These Census Bureau figures put numbers on the household base behind a Haywood County listing.

  • 27,123 households for 2020-2024, at 2.29 persons each.
  • Roughly nine in ten residents (89.6%) had stayed put for the prior year.
  • A $1,067 median gross rent, against $1,447 monthly for mortgaged owners.
  • Degree holders: 29.5% of those 25 and up.
  • Density of 112.2 residents per square mile at the 2020 count.

Add the 28.2% share of residents 65 or over and the picture is a long-tenured owner base.

What happens to unpaid Haywood County property tax, and what about a sale?

Foreclosure can start any day after January 5 of the collection year, though the county says it forecloses only when an owner does not respond or breaks a payment arrangement. Before that, the collector can attach bank accounts, garnish wages or rents, or levy on personal property.

The county uses two routes. In an in-rem foreclosure under G.S. 105-375, the Tax Department and County Attorney handle everything, and in a mortgage-style case under G.S. 105-374 an outside attorney does. Sales are public auctions in front of the Haywood County Justice Center, as is and without warranty, with a 20% deposit and a balance due at the end of the 10-day period and confirmation. Upset bids must exceed the last bid by 5%, at least $750, and are filed with the Clerk of Superior Court.

Selling does not erase the year's bill. Ownership is fixed on January 1, a mid-year transfer leaves the seller liable, and the payoff is therefore settled at closing. County data to keep in mind: 36,637 housing units, 74.9% owner-occupied, a median owner-occupied value of $279,200, median household income of $61,912 and 514 building permits in 2025 (Census QuickFacts).

More questions about Haywood County, NC Property Tax Guide

When does interest start on Haywood County property tax?

After January 5. The county adds 2% then, and a further three-quarters of one percent on the first day of every month until the bill is paid.

Does Haywood County sell tax lien certificates?

No. The county's foreclosure page says North Carolina does not sell tax liens or tax certificates over the counter, and paying someone else's delinquent bill does not transfer ownership.

When is the Haywood County revaluation?

January 1, 2027. The county moved it from 2025 after Hurricane Helene, and 2025 values stayed the same for most properties unless something about the property changed.

I sold my Haywood County house, so why did I get the tax bill?

Because ownership of real property is set as of January 1 of the tax year, and a transfer during the year does not remove the seller's liability. Settle the year's tax at closing.

Where do I send storm damage reports in Haywood County?

To the Tax Assessor's Office at 215 N. Main Street, Suite 220, Waynesville, NC 28786, or by email to personalproperty@haywoodcountync.gov, using the Damage Report Form.

Henderson County by the numbers

Who runs property tax in Henderson County?

Property tax in this county runs on two desks. An Assessor sets values here, and a Tax Collector bills and collects. The collector's counter is Suite 66, ground floor, at 200 North Grove Street, Hendersonville, NC 28792, open weekdays from 8:30 to 5:00.

For an appraisal or appeal, dial 828-697-4667. For payments, dial 828-697-5595. Rates are not the Assessor's call: commissioners and the governing bodies of Hendersonville, Fletcher, Saluda, Mills River, Flat Rock and Laurel Park each set one to fit their budgets.

One collector bills for the county, thirteen fire districts, Hendersonville, Laurel Park and the Henderson County portion of Saluda. The Assessor's page counts 22 tax districts, including the general county district, and rates vary with the services each district provides.

How does Henderson County value property?

Everything taxable is valued at 100% of market value under the uniform standards in G.S. 105-283. The workload covers about 71,500 parcels, some 4,500 businesses with personal property, over 10,000 manufactured homes and more than 100,000 registered vehicles that are billed monthly.

Henderson County reappraises every four years rather than waiting for the eight-year state limit in G.S. 105-286. The last reappraisal was in 2023, and the next takes effect January 1, 2027. Buildings still under construction on January 1 are valued by their percent complete, and a farm or forest tract in the Present-Use Value Program is assessed below market.

The county's reappraisal page estimates that property tax covers 50% of total operating spending in fiscal year 2027.

What is the Henderson County 2027 reappraisal schedule?

The county's published schedule runs from the Schedule of Values hearing in fall 2026 through tax bills in August 2027. Notices of assessed value are expected to go out around February 1, 2027, so owners will see new numbers before the appeal window closes.

Henderson County 2027 reappraisal schedule

April 14, 2027county review board convenes

By June 30, 2027Commissioners set the 2027-2028 tax rate

Source: Henderson County Reappraisal Schedule. The county also lists information sessions for community groups from September 1, 2026 through January 31, 2027.

What steps does a Henderson County appeal follow?

An informal written appeal to the Assessor comes first, on the county's standard form. A formal appeal goes to the county review board only when that fails to settle the value, and it must be received before the board adjourns.

  • Once a formal appeal is in, an appraiser meets the owner to discuss value and verify the information supplied.
  • If they still disagree, each side presents at a public hearing.
  • The board mails its decision inside 30 days of that hearing.
  • The next step is the state Property Tax Commission, where notice is due 30 days from the board's letter and most cases are heard in Raleigh.

The statewide framework is G.S. 105-322. A seller's best exhibits are recent sales of similar homes nearby, any appraisal tied to a sale contract, and repair quotes for defects a mass appraisal cannot see.

Which payment methods does Henderson County accept?

Owners can mail a check, visit the counter, pay online or use the automated phone line. The counter takes cash, check, money order and cards. A drop box in the south parking lot is emptied daily, and it is no place for cash.

  • Card and e-check users pay a convenience fee that goes to the payment vendor.
  • Prepayments taken January through July appear as a credit once the bill is issued.
  • Owners who expect to be late are asked to call before delinquency, and most are offered a plan.
  • Mail checks to Henderson County Tax Collector, 200 N Grove St, Ste 66, Hendersonville, NC 28792.

The state calendar, due September 1 with par payment until January 6 and interest after that, is in G.S. 105-360.

What relief programs are open to Henderson County homeowners?

Residents 65 or over make up 29.1% of the county, so the age-based programs reach many owners. The tax pages list the elderly or permanently disabled exclusion, the disabled veterans exclusion, present-use value and the circuit-breaker deferral, all handled by the Assessor.

  • Elderly or disabled: $25,000 or half the value of the permanent residence, whichever is greater, if 2026 income is within $38,800.
  • Disabled veteran: $45,000 off appraised value, no age or income cap.
  • Circuit breaker: tax held to 4.0% of income, or 5.0% above the $38,800 mark up to $58,200, with the excess deferred.

Only one of the three can be used by a given owner. Apply on Form AV-9, which the county accepts through June 1 before the tax year. A circuit-breaker deferral is payable when the home transfers.

Which Census figures matter for Henderson County owners?

Census Bureau data frame the household base behind a Henderson County sale.

  • Land area of 372.95 square miles, with 311.8 residents per square mile counted in 2020.
  • 51,067 households for 2020-2024, averaging 2.29 persons.
  • Population estimate of 122,375 on July 1, 2025, a 5.2% rise from the 2020 base.
  • A $1,187 median gross rent and 7,811 veterans.
  • Degree attainment: 36.5% of those 25 and up hold a four-year degree or more.
  • 2022 retail sales of $2,287,875 thousand, plus $1,199,447 thousand in health care and social services receipts.

Commutes average 22.5 minutes, and nearly nine in ten residents (89.7%) were in the same home a year before the survey.

What follows unpaid Henderson County tax, and how does it touch a sale?

The Tax Collector may foreclose on real property with delinquent taxes, and sales are held on the courthouse steps at 200 North Grove Street. The county lists each parcel with an estimated opening bid that does not include interest and expenses accruing daily. Upset bid amounts are available from the Clerk of Court at 828-694-4100, and sale questions go to 828-698-3090.

The sale posted on the county page was May 27, 2026 at 10:00 a.m. and listed 15 parcels with estimated opening bids from $739.08 up to $14,077.24.

A seller with a balance can clear it at closing instead. Get the payoff from the Tax Collector, and expect the deed excise tax of $1.00 per $500 to be paid separately by the seller. On pricing, Census figures show owner-occupied homes with a median value of $351,400, 75.0% owner occupancy, household income at a $68,187 median and 1,093 permits issued in 2025 (Census QuickFacts).

More questions about Henderson County, NC Property Tax Guide

When is the Henderson County reappraisal effective?

January 1, 2027. The county's last reappraisal was in 2023 and it follows a four-year cycle, so values reset to market as of that date.

By when must a 2027 Henderson County value be contested?

The county schedule shows the Board of Equalization and Review adjourning and closing the 2027 appeal period on May 14, 2027. Informal appeals to the Assessor run from January 1 to April 13, 2027.

Can I pay Henderson County property tax in installments?

Yes. The Tax Collector encourages monthly installments, accepts prepayments from January through July, and usually offers a payment plan if you call before the bill is delinquent.

Where are Henderson County tax foreclosure sales held?

On the courthouse steps at 200 North Grove Street, Hendersonville. The Tax Collector's page lists each parcel and an estimated opening bid, and the Clerk of Court gives current upset bid amounts.

Who sets the Henderson County tax rate?

The Board of Commissioners sets the county rate, and each municipality sets its own. The Assessor only determines value, so an appeal changes the value and not the rate.

Which Winton offices value and bill property in Hertford County?

Two neighboring offices on Justice Drive in Winton split the work, and both stay open on weekdays until five in the afternoon.

Hertford County tax offices as listed on county web pages
OfficeAddressPhone

The assessor's stated mission is to find, identify and appraise every taxable parcel and personal property account. The collector bills for the county and also for the towns of Ahoskie, Harrellsville, Cofield, Como, Murfreesboro and Winton, plus two drainage districts, three fire districts and solid waste fees. So one parcel's bill may carry several lines.

What is the Hertford County payment calendar?

Bills fall due on September 1. A 2 percent charge starts on January 6, and a further 3/4 of 1 percent builds for every month after that.

The postal postmark decides whether a mailed payment is late; a meter date does not count. Partial payments are welcome from the day the bill arrives until January 6. An escrow account does not stop the bill from coming to you, because the lender is told electronically and chooses which bills to pay. Call your lender if you expect it to pay.

  • Options: online, at the Winton counter, or on the toll-free line at 1-888-520-8728.
  • An online card payment adds 2.5 percent, a fee set by the processor and not kept by the county.
  • Cards are also taken at the counter.
  • A bounced check draws the G.S. 105-357(2) charge: $25.00 or 10 percent of the check, whichever is more, capped at $1,000.

What does the 2027 Hertford County revaluation change?

New real estate values take effect January 1, 2027. The last revaluation in the county was in 2019, and the state requires reappraisal at least every eight years.

Appraisers divide the county into market areas, which the county also calls neighborhoods, review recent sales in each one, and apply a uniform schedule of values so similar houses are judged by the same standard. The county hired an outside appraisal firm from North Carolina and Virginia for the 2027 cycle. Field measuring began in July 2025 to fix listing errors and capture changes since the last cycle. Owners get a notice of assessed value shortly after the effective date, and appeal instructions will appear on that notice. The old value can be compared using the parcel's 2018 tax card, which the tax office can pull.

The county says the aim is fairness among owners, and values will not all move together. Rates come from the commissioners and the town boards, typically in June. A bill is the tax value times the rate, so request the rate sheet from the tax office when you plan a sale.

What can I do if my Hertford County value looks too high?

Use the instructions printed on your notice of assessed value. The county says it will also post appeal forms on the Assessor's page as the revaluation date approaches.

A formal appeal is heard by the county's equalization and review board, normally the commissioners sitting in that role. In a revaluation year it wraps up by December 1, and a request to be heard has to arrive before it adjourns. The assessor can give you the adjournment date. Read G.S. 105-322.

Which tax relief programs apply in Hertford County?

North Carolina lets an owner draw on only one of its three relief programs. All are filed with the county assessor on Form AV-9. The elderly or disabled exclusion, the disabled veteran exclusion and the circuit breaker are described in G.S. 105-277.1, 105-277.1C and 105-277.1B, and the revenue department's printed 2026 income limit is $38,800.

Call the Tax Assessor at 252-358-7810 to learn which program fits and whether a filing already exists for your parcel. The state form says filings are accepted through June 1 before the tax year, and a new application is needed every year for the circuit breaker. A sale can end a deferral, so raise it before listing. Form details: NCDOR Form AV-9.

What if taxes are unpaid when a Hertford County house sells?

The tax follows the property. A lien for real property taxes attaches on the date the property must be listed, and penalties, interest and costs attach with it under G.S. 105-355. The county's FAQ adds that each year's listing names the owner on January 1, so a seller who conveys later can still receive the bill.

Practical steps for a seller:

  • Request a payoff total from the collector covering this year and any earlier years.
  • Have the closing attorney settle taxes out of proceeds, which is the wording the Register of Deeds expects on deeds.
  • Pass any bill that shows up after the sale to the new owner.

Left unpaid, a bill can lead to wage garnishment, bank attachment, attachment of state income tax refunds, levy and foreclosure. The collector's office also offers a three-month payment plan on delinquent taxes. Foreclosure auctions are held at the courthouse door, buyers pay in full with cash or certified funds, and the local newspaper carries the advertisement.

What vehicles, county-owned land and auctions does the collector handle?

The Tax Collector's pages cover more than house bills. Motor vehicles are billed within 90 days of tag renewal, owners get one month to pay before interest starts, and after four months a block goes on the tag. The county cannot prorate or reduce a vehicle bill without the FS20 receipt from NCDMV, which must reach the office within one year of surrender. The license plate agency in Ahoskie is at 907 E. Memorial Drive.

The office also lists county-owned property open for bids and foreclosed parcels with their auction dates, and it ties foreclosure sales to an outside attorney who schedules them. Properties that fail to sell at auction are sold by the county. No advance registration is needed for an auction; you or a representative simply appear at the courthouse door.

Who owns homes in Hertford County?

The county counts 8,285 households of about 2.20 people each. Owners hold 67.4 percent of the homes. The middle-priced owned home is worth $119,200. Owners with a mortgage spend a median $1,285 a month, against $523 for those without. Poverty touches 22.9 percent of residents, and 27.1 percent have passed 65. These figures come from Census QuickFacts.

The county took shape in 1759 from parts of Bertie, Northampton and Chowan counties, and farming still anchors its economy. Parcels range from town lots in Ahoskie, Murfreesboro and Winton to cropland and timber, which is why the fire district and solid waste lines on a bill vary from one parcel to the next. Bring the collector's total to the closing table so nothing is left owing.

More questions about Hertford County, NC Property Tax Guide

How can I pay my Hertford County tax bill?

Pay online, in person at 115 Justice Drive, Suite 5, or by calling 1-888-520-8728. Online card payments add a 2.5 percent fee, and partial payments are accepted until January 6.

Which office sends the Hertford County tax bill?

The Tax Collector bills for the county, six towns, fire and drainage districts, and solid waste fees. Call 252-358-7815 with questions.

When does the next Hertford County revaluation take effect?

January 1, 2027. The last one was in 2019, and owners receive notices of their new assessed values shortly after that date, with appeal instructions on the notice.

I sold my house but still got the Hertford County bill. Why?

Whoever owned the parcel on January 1 is the name on the bill, so one can still arrive after you sell. Send a copy to the new owner, as the county asks.

Can I pay Hertford County taxes over time?

Yes for delinquent accounts: the collector offers a three-month plan. Call 252-358-7815 to ask about it.

The Hoke County Tax Office has two departments, and both are at 227 N. Main Street in Raeford. The Assessor lists, appraises and assesses all taxable property, and Collections bills and collects tax on real estate, personal property and delinquent motor vehicles.

The post office box is 1557 in Raeford, ZIP 28376, and the phone line is 910-875-8751. The appraisal office keeps weekday office hours. Hoke County was founded in 1911, and Raeford, incorporated in 1901, became the county seat. The county sits between Fayetteville and Cumberland County to the east and Pinehurst and Moore County to the west, and part of Fort Bragg lies on county land.

What rates and fees appear on a Hoke County tax bill?

A bill is built from the county rate, any city rate, a fire district rate and a solid waste fee. The county's tax rates page explains that rates apply to each $100 of value, and that city properties do not get the fire district tax or the solid waste fee.

Fire district rates differ by district, so request from the Tax Office the sheet that lists the district for your parcel, and confirm the current Raeford rate if the house is inside city limits.

When did Hoke County last revalue property, and what is next?

The last countywide revaluation took effect January 1, 2022. Notices went to all Hoke County taxpayers on February 3, 2022, and the next revaluation is set for January 1, 2030, with work starting two years before.

The county cites G.S. 105-286, which requires reappraisal at least every eight years. Between cycles your assessed value on real property stays tied to the January 1, 2022 market level unless you add improvements or the parcel changes. Ask the assessor how a sale price compares with the 2022 value on your parcel.

In the county's words, an appraisal sets each owner's share of the taxes that support schools, roads, parks, public health, libraries, police and fire protection. The amount you pay depends on your property value and the rates adopted each year by elected county and city or town officials.

What is the route for contesting a Hoke County assessment?

The Notice of Appeal of Assessment goes to the Tax Assessor ahead of the equalization board's adjournment. The county advertises that date in the local paper and online, and the assessor's office can confirm it.

  • One form per parcel, signed by the owner or a representative (an attorney, or an attorney in fact holding a power of attorney when the owner is not a corporation).
  • Evidence can be an appraisal, sales of similar properties, income and expense statements or replacement cost, and copies go in with the form.
  • The owner must show the value substantially exceeds true market value on the January 1, 2022 valuation date.
  • The board sets a hearing date and tells you; you can attend or send counsel.

The county's procedures mention informal appeals, and an appraisal already submitted informally need not be sent in again. The next stop after the county board is the Property Tax Commission, with a written notice due 30 days after the mailing of the decision. Statute: G.S. 105-290.

What is the Hoke County payment timeline?

September 1 is the due date. Under G.S. 105-360, paying before January 6 costs face value; from then until February 1 a charge of 2 percent applies, followed by three quarters of a percent per month.

The county lets residents pay online, and the Collections office answers billing questions. The USPS postmark date counts for mail, so keep the envelope. State law lets a county adopt prepayment discounts; ask whether Hoke has one.

Under G.S. 105-355, unpaid tax attaches to the parcel as a lien from the listing date, and the county can enforce it by foreclosure filed where the land lies. A sale is a public auction at the courthouse door, and a person who redeems before confirmation pays the tax plus penalties, interest and costs. See G.S. 105-374.

Which relief programs can Hoke County owners use?

North Carolina offers an elderly or disabled exclusion, a disabled veteran exclusion and a circuit breaker deferral, and an owner may take only one. The county assessor takes the Form AV-9 filing. Veterans are a large group here, with 6,926 counted by the Census Bureau.

The 2026 thresholds printed by the revenue department are $38,800 for the base income limit and $58,200 for the circuit breaker's upper tier. The state accepts filings through June 1 before the tax year. A transfer of the property triggers the deferred tax under the circuit breaker, so mention it to your attorney before you list. See NCDOR Form AV-9.

How is the Hoke County housing market shaped?

Hoke has grown from 52,082 people at the 2020 count to an estimate of 56,939 in July 2025. The county counts 22,440 housing units and issued 558 building permits during 2025.

Owners occupy 73.0 percent of homes. The midpoint owned home is valued at $219,300, with owner costs of $1,472 monthly where a mortgage exists. Rent runs $1,089, household income is $64,912, and the average trip to work takes 28.8 minutes. Children under 18 are 26.7 percent of residents and seniors 13.1 percent.

The county's economic development page ties the growth to the neighboring military post and describes a past built on cotton, then poultry. Butterball is credited with 600 jobs, and the North Carolina Fall Festival is described as drawing more than 30,000 visitors. Industrial sites with dual rail service connect to two national railroads through the Aberdeen and Rockfish line, the same line whose extension led to the incorporation of Raeford in 1901. Source: Census QuickFacts.

How should a Hoke County seller handle the tax bill?

Request a payoff from Collections that covers this year and earlier years. Because the lien dates from the listing date, an unpaid current-year bill must be cleared at closing.

  • Have the closing attorney pay taxes from proceeds.
  • Look for a fire district tax and a solid waste fee on the bill if the house sits outside Raeford.
  • Confirm any exclusion filing is current before the sale.
  • Keep your 2022 value notice handy for buyers who ask.

More questions about Hoke County, NC Property Tax Guide

Where is the Hoke County Tax Office?

Both the Assessor and Collections are at 227 N. Main Street in Raeford. The post office box is 1557 in Raeford, ZIP 28376, and the phone line is 910-875-8751.

When is the next Hoke County revaluation?

It is scheduled for January 1, 2030. The last one took effect January 1, 2022, with notices mailed February 3, 2022, and work begins two years before the effective date.

What is the Hoke County property tax rate?

The county's tax rates page prints a county rate of .73 per $100 in its examples, a Raeford rate of .48 and a North Raeford fire district rate of .10. A solid waste fee can apply outside city limits, so request the current rate sheet.

What do I file to contest a Hoke County value?

File a Notice of Appeal of Assessment for each parcel with the Tax Assessor before the equalization board adjourns, with evidence such as appraisals or comparable sales. The adjournment date is advertised in the newspaper and on the county website.

Does Hoke County have a fire district tax?

Yes. The county tax rates page lists a fire district rate that is charged on top of the county rate, based on the district where the property sits. City properties do not receive it.

Iredell County by the numbers

Which Iredell County office deals with property tax?

Iredell County Tax Administration runs the whole property tax system from its building at 135 E. Water Street in Statesville, and it is split into an assessor division, a tax collector division and a land records mapping division. The county board of commissioners set the policy, but you deal with the staff for almost everything.

The county Tax Administration page gives weekday hours that begin at 8 a.m. and end at 5 p.m. Call 704-878-3017 for the assessor and 704-878-3020 for the collector. The mailing address is PO Box 1027, Statesville, NC 28687.

  • Assessor division: listing, values, exemptions and appeals.
  • Tax collector division: bills, payments, delinquent accounts and closing payoffs.
  • Land records mapping: parcel maps and the online GIS used to find an owner of record.

Sellers tend to call the collector for a bill and the assessor when a value looks off.

What is the Iredell County property tax rate?

For the 2026 tax year the county levies 0.50 on every $100 of assessed value, unchanged from 2025 and 2024 on the county's chart. The budget the commissioners approved for 2026-2027 holds it there.

Your bill adds a municipal rate if you live inside a town, plus any fire or special district. The table pulls the 2026 column from the county tax rates page, each figure stated per $100 of value.

Source: Iredell County Tax Administration rate chart. Downtown districts in Statesville (.10) and Mooresville (.14) add to the bill for properties inside them.

The county also bills a flat solid waste fee of $64 per household, mobile home or apartment for 2026, and half of that for an owner with the elderly or disabled exclusion. Davidson adds a $20 privilege charge on vehicles, and Mooresville has its own solid waste fee.

When does an Iredell County tax bill come due?

Statements are mailed in August with a September 1 due date, and the collector gives owners until January 5 before any charge applies. A 2 percent charge lands on January 6, followed by 0.75 percent at the start of every later month.

North Carolina law sets the same framework for every county. The listing period runs the month of January, and the statute on due dates and interest explains the January 6 trigger. A town or county may also adopt a prepayment discount, so ask the collector whether one applies to the unit you are in.

Iredell also advertises unpaid real estate taxes in the newspaper during March and adds an advertising fee to the bill. The collector lists these tools for a delinquent account:

  • Attachment of bank accounts
  • Debt set-off against state income tax refunds
  • Garnishment of wages or rents
  • Levy on rents or other money owed to you
  • Seizure of a vehicle or other personal property
  • Foreclosure

Motor vehicle tax is separate. It rides on the state tag renewal notice and is paid to the Division of Motor Vehicles, not the county office.

How does reappraisal work in Iredell County?

Iredell County reappraises every four years, which is twice as often as the state minimum of eight. The last effective date was January 1, 2023, and the county rate table says the next revaluation takes effect January 1, 2027.

The county has published an adopted schedule of values for 2027 on its assessor pages, and the commissioners have discussed preparation for the countywide reappraisal at recent meetings. State law at G.S. 105-286 sets the outside limit, and a county can choose a shorter cycle.

Appraisers group the county into neighborhoods, review recent sales in each one and adjust values to market. They screen out sales that do not reflect market value, such as transfers between relatives, gifts and trades. A sale made under pressure can also pull a price down, which is one reason the county does not rely on every closing it sees.

For a seller, a reappraisal year matters because the value on the notice becomes the base for tax bills until the next reappraisal. If you plan to list a home around a revaluation date, pull the new appraisal card from the county taxweb site before you choose an asking price.

What is the appeal route for an Iredell County value?

Iredell County sets up a ladder with three rungs, and you climb it one step at a time. The county's appeals page prints the whole sequence.

  1. Informal review: send the appeal form and your documents to the assessor at PO Box 1027, Statesville, NC 28687, or use the online portal. The deadline is 30 days counted from the notice date, and an appraiser answers with a fresh notice that can lower, raise or keep the value.
  2. Review board: put the request in writing, naming the property and the grounds, signed by the owner or an attorney. The county's board page says to mail it and not to count on electronic filing, so confirm the method with the assessor's office at 704-878-3017. Under G.S. 105-322 the board holds its opening session in the spring window the statute sets.
  3. State commission: if the board's written decision still disagrees with you, a Property Tax Commission appeal must be filed in 30 days.

A friend or tax consultant who is not an owner or lawyer must attach a power of attorney, or the request may be rejected. At the hearing the county's appraisal starts out presumed correct, so the owner carries the proof. The county wants sales contracts, MLS data or private appraisals dated 2022, plus photos of damage and surveys.

  • Accepted reasons: the value is out of line with market on the reappraisal date, similar properties are assessed differently, or the record card has errors.
  • Rejected reasons: a big increase, inability to pay, weak county services, high taxes, or a market shift after the effective date.

Which state relief programs reach Iredell County homeowners?

Three state programs reduce the bill for a permanent residence, and a household may use only one. The assessor takes the application on the state's AV-9 form.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: for owners at least 65, or with a lasting total disability, whose 2026 income stays under $38,800. It excludes $25,000 or half the appraised value, whichever is greater.
  • Veteran exclusion: removes $45,000 of value for a permanent, total, service-connected disability, whatever the owner's age or income.
  • Circuit breaker: caps tax at 4 percent of income, or 5 percent for incomes up to $58,200, once the owner has spent five years in the home.

The state AV-9 notice shows the filing window stretching through June 1 ahead of the tax year. Circuit breaker savings are deferred and secured by a lien, so selling the house or moving out triggers repayment of the prior three years. Anyone in that program should obtain a payoff from the assessor before listing. Iredell also halves its solid waste fee for owners who hold the elderly exemption.

Farm and forest owners can apply for present-use value, and builders can claim inventory relief, both through the same division.

How does a sale in Iredell County change who owes the tax?

A house that sells after January 1 leaves the seller on the hook for that year's bill, because ownership is fixed on that date. Dividing it with the buyer is a private arrangement worked out at closing.

The collector says a transfer does not release the seller, that the bill for the transfer year still goes to the seller, and that any proration is a contract matter. Questions about how it was divided go to your realtor or closing attorney. If you want no loose ends, you can request that the payment be made to the collector at closing, and the office will take a prepayment based on the previous year's rate if the current bill is not out yet.

Unpaid back taxes are the sharper risk. A tax lien attaches to the parcel as of the listing date under G.S. 105-355, so the buyer's lawyer will want the account paid up. The county advertises the owner of record as of the delinquency date, which is another reason to get a payoff figure before a contract is signed.

How large and how expensive is Iredell County?

Census QuickFacts estimates Iredell County's population at 211,798 for mid-2025, a 13.5 percent jump over the 2020 count base. Its land area is 574.41 square miles, and it holds about 93,711 housing units.

  • Owners live in 71.9 percent of occupied homes (2020-2024)
  • Typical home value among owners: $321,400
  • Household income at the median: $81,419
  • Rent at the median: $1,252 a month
  • Permits issued for new building during 2025: 1,835

The county includes Statesville, Mooresville, Troutman, Davidson, Harmony and Love Valley, and each taxes at its own rate on top of the county's. Commuters average 25.1 minutes to work.

More questions about Iredell County, NC Property Tax Guide

What is the Iredell County property tax rate?

The county rate is .50 per $100 for 2026, and Statesville, Mooresville and other towns add their own rates. Check the county rates page for your town and fire district.

When must Iredell County taxes be paid?

Bills are due September 1 and are penalty free through January 5. Interest of 2 percent starts January 6, then 0.75 percent more each month.

Where do I file an appeal in Iredell County?

File first with the assessor at PO Box 1027, Statesville, NC 28687, within 30 days of your value notice. If that fails, a written appeal goes to the county review board, and the last stop is the state Property Tax Commission.

Who pays the property tax when I sell in Iredell County?

The seller is billed for the year of sale if the house sells after January 1, and proration with the buyer is settled in the contract or at closing. You can ask to pay the collector at closing.

Does Iredell County offer relief for older homeowners?

Yes. Owners aged 65 and over, or disabled, may qualify for the elderly or disabled exclusion when income is within the limit, and applications are taken through June 1. The county also halves the solid waste fee for those owners.

Johnston County by the numbers

Which Johnston County office handles my tax bill?

Tax Administration works out of the courthouse in Smithfield, 207 East Johnston Street, second floor. It keeps weekday hours from 8 to 5 and closes for county holidays.

Two phone numbers split the work, as the county contact page explains:

  • 919-989-5120 (Tax Collection): your bill, payment plans, wage garnishment, bank attachment and foreclosure policy. Write to P.O. Box 451, Smithfield, NC 27577.
  • 919-989-5130 (Tax Administration): listing property, valuation and relief programs. Write to P.O. Box 368, Smithfield, NC 27577.

An online portal shows bills, appraisal cards and sales. Sellers should also know about the downloads page, where the county posts a delinquent tax file and an accounts receivable file for lenders.

What is the Johnston County property tax rate?

The county rate is 0.510 per $100 of value for the 2026 tax year, down from 0.520 the year before, and the county fire protection service district adds 0.115. The county posts a chart that shows the 2026 and 2025 rates side by side.

Your parcel's taxing districts come from the county GIS, so call 919-989-5130 if the districts on your bill look wrong.

For fiscal year 2026-2027 the county reports how its budget splits: education 32 percent, public safety 23 percent, human services 18 percent, general government 12 percent, debt service 10 percent and physical development 5 percent. Those shares do not include town or district spending.

When does a Johnston County tax bill turn late?

The county mails statements in July, sets September 1 as the due date and treats January 5 as the last penalty-free day. Starting January 6 the balance gains 2 percent, then three-quarters of a percent for each month after that.

Billing follows the January 1 owner, but the paper statement goes to whoever the records show on June 30. If one arrives for a house you have sold, the county says to pass it to the buyer. Lenders pull their own data from the tax office and usually pay late in the year, so your copy is for your files only.

Owners who prefer installments can sign a payment agreement for the current year, accepted until the bill turns delinquent. Older unpaid years are not eligible. Ways to pay:

  • Phone: 888-327-7344, with the year and bill number
  • Web: the county pay taxes page
  • Post: Tax Collections, P.O. Box 451
  • In person: a locked drop box at the courthouse doors

Cars and trucks are handled apart from this. The state tag and tax system collects vehicle tax through the Division of Motor Vehicles.

What changed with the Johnston County revaluation?

Johnston County's last revaluation before the current one was in 2019, and the new values took effect January 1, 2025. They drive tax bills from the summer of 2025 until the next countywide revaluation, with exceptions such as new construction.

State law at G.S. 105-286 requires every county to reappraise at least every eight years. The county hired Pearson Appraisal Service for the work, and its own certified appraisers reviewed the results. Appraisers used aerial images, street-level images, sales data and the tax database, and they made field visits to more than 115,000 properties.

The county explains that appraised value and assessed value are the same as of the revaluation date. It also explains why an online estimate can differ from the tax office figure: automated models do not check whether a sale meets the statutory test, and the county screens sales by phone calls and visits. A foreclosure sale is analyzed carefully before it counts as market evidence, and your own purchase price may differ from market value.

You must report changes you make to a property, such as additions, demolished buildings, or fire and flood damage. Email taxoffice@johnstonnc.gov or call 919-989-5130, or note it on the January listing form.

Can I challenge a Johnston County value?

Yes, but only inside a window. For real property in the 2026 cycle the county accepted its valuation appeal form until 5:00 p.m. on April 28, 2026, and its appeals page says real property appeals open in February 2027.

Personal property follows a different clock: the form has to land at the tax office thirty days after the bill date. Individual and business personal property share one form, and both are on the county forms page.

After that review the next body is the equalization and review board, which G.S. 105-322 assigns to the commissioners by default. A last appeal to the state Property Tax Commission is possible under G.S. 105-290, filed with a copy to the assessor.

Listing carries a separate deadline. January is the listing month, and a late list adds a 10 percent penalty to the levy. Last year's improvements, untagged vehicles, boats, aircraft and business assets all go on the form, and a building permit does not count as listing.

Which relief programs apply in Johnston County?

The county applies the same three state homestead programs for 2026, and an owner picks one. File Form AV-9, available from the county forms page, and ask for the relief specialist at 919-989-5130.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: owner is 65, or permanently and totally disabled, and the owner plus spouse have combined income of $38,800 or less.
  • Circuit breaker deferment: same age or disability test, income cap of $58,200, and five years of owning and occupying the home.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: service-connected total and permanent disability, or a specially adapted housing benefit. A surviving spouse who has not remarried can also qualify.

The county wants applications in before June 1 of the tax year. Present use valuation for farm, forest and horticultural land runs separately, through Form AV-5 in the January listing month. A tract removed from that program owes the deferred tax for the current year plus three earlier years, with interest. Builders can also apply every January to exclude inventory value, for as long as three years on homes and five on commercial lots.

What happens to the tax when I sell my Johnston County house?

Nothing is divided for you. The county neither splits nor prorates between parties, so the buyer and seller settle it by contract, through the broker or the closing attorney.

The real property page repeats the point from another angle: a mid-year transfer leaves the seller responsible, and any credit at closing is a private deal. If you owe earlier years, ask collections for a payoff figure ahead of closing, because G.S. 105-355 attaches the lien to the parcel from the listing date.

An unpaid account can end in foreclosure, after notices and a pre-foreclosure letter, with the file handed to a private attorney. Sales take place on the courthouse steps, usually starting around ten in the morning. The bidder puts down 5 percent. Ten days must pass before the sale is final, and an upset bid has to top the last by 5 percent or $750, whichever is larger. The owner may redeem by paying taxes, interest and costs until the court confirms the sale.

How big is Johnston County?

Census QuickFacts estimates the mid-2025 population at 256,448, an increase of 18.7 percent over the 2020 base. Land covers 792.02 square miles, and the county counts about 99,408 housing units.

  • Owners occupy 76.1 percent of households (2020-2024)
  • Typical owner-held home value: $305,600
  • Middle household income: $83,384
  • Rent at the middle: $1,146 per month
  • New building permits in 2025: 3,002
  • Average trip to work: 32.2 minutes

The courthouse and tax office are in Smithfield. Clayton, Selma, Benson, Four Oaks and other towns each levy their own rate in addition to the county's.

More questions about Johnston County, NC Property Tax Guide

What is the 2026 tax rate for Johnston County?

The county levies 0.510 per $100 for 2026, down from 0.520 in 2025. The fire protection district adds 0.115, and each town adds its own rate.

When do Johnston County property taxes become delinquent?

They turn delinquent after January 5. Interest begins January 6 at 2 percent for the first month, then three-quarters of a percent per month.

Will Johnston County divide the tax between me and the buyer?

No. The county bills the January 1 owner and does not prorate, so your broker or closing attorney should settle the split on the closing statement.

Can I spread Johnston County taxes over installments?

Yes, for the current year only. Return a payment agreement to collections before the bill goes delinquent, since prior-year balances are not eligible.

Whom do I ask about Johnston County tax relief?

Call 919-989-5130 and ask for a property tax relief specialist. The application is Form AV-9, due before June 1.

Lenoir County by the numbers

Where does Lenoir County send its property tax bills from?

Bills come from the Lenoir County Tax Department in the administration building at 101 North Queen Street in Kinston, phone 252-527-7174. Plan a visit between 8:30 and 5:00 any weekday.

One office carries several jobs. It lists and appraises real estate, keeps ownership and transfer records, tracks exemptions, exclusions and deferrals, and mails the bills. It also bills the special districts layered over the county: fire districts, municipal service districts and drainage districts. Solid waste fees, privilege licenses and permits to move mobile homes run through the same counter.

The county website links to online bill viewing and payment, real property records, GIS maps, a scheduler for real property appeals, and listing forms for business and individual personal property. A seller checking a bill before closing can look there first and then phone for a payoff figure.

How does the tax calendar work for a Lenoir County bill?

A bill is due on September 1, yet it costs nothing extra until January 6. Past that day, 2 percent interest is charged through February 1, then 3/4 percent a month, counting part of a month as a whole one.

Calendar rules that shape a Lenoir County tax year, with the statute for each
StepWhat the law saysWhere to read it
ListingOpens the first business day of January, closes January 31G.S. 105-307
Payment dateSeptember 1 of the fiscal year for which the tax is leviedG.S. 105-360
Last interest-free dayThe day before January 6G.S. 105-360

Next appeal levelWritten notice of appeal to the state commission within a month of the mailed rulingG.S. 105-290

A mailed payment is dated by its postmark.

How do I appeal a Lenoir County property value?

Real estate appeals in this county are heard by its Board of Equalization and Review. The 2026 window ended on April 23, 2026, when the board adjourned. Per the county, the 2027 window opens on January 1, 2027.

This quasi-judicial board hears disputes over how real estate and personal property were listed and appraised, plus exemption applications, exclusion requests and present-use classifications, all under G.S. 105-322.

Timing is strict: ask for a hearing, by letter or in person, before the board adjourns. A written decision follows within 30 days of adjournment. Someone still unhappy can file notice with the state Property Tax Commission inside 30 days of the mailing date, stating the grounds and sending a copy to the assessor. The county site offers a form for scheduling a real property appeal.

When did Lenoir County last revalue property?

Lenoir County's own page says assessed values held steady after the reappraisal effective January 1, 2017, and it described the next one as effective January 1, 2025. North Carolina law sets the outside limit at eight years between reappraisals of real property.

In between, a value changes only when the property does, for example through new construction or a removed building. During a reappraisal, certified appraisers visit parcels, confirm characteristics and study sales and costs so every property is measured as of the same date.

Treat the assessed figure as a tax number and not a market price. Weigh it against recent sales when choosing an asking price, and request the current assessed value on your parcel from the office.

What property tax relief programs exist for Lenoir County owners?

Three homestead programs exist statewide, and the county takes the AV-9 application for them. One owner may claim just one of them. File during the listing period; the county must still accept an application up to June 1 before the tax year.

  • Age or disability: protects $25,000 or half the appraised value, whichever is the larger figure. Applicants must be 65 or older, or totally and permanently disabled, and report income no higher than the $38,800 figure NCDOR prints for 2026.
  • Disabled veterans: the program removes $45,000 of appraised value from the tax base. NCDOR's form says no age or income limit applies, and the owner submits Form NCDVA-9 through the assessor.
  • Circuit breaker: limits the bill to 4.0 percent of income at or below the cap, and to 5.0 percent between the cap and 150 percent of it (NCDOR prints $58,200 for 2026). The owner must have owned and lived in the house for five years, and a fresh application is filed yearly. Deferred tax becomes due on a sale.

Farm, horticulture and forest land may qualify for present-use value, which lowers the assessment. Lenoir County has an AV-7 form to request an estimate of deferred taxes, a useful step before selling qualifying land.

What does a Lenoir County landlord or business owner have to list?

Anyone holding personal property tied to a business or other income-producing use must file a Business Personal Property Listing Form during January. The county names machinery, equipment, computers, furniture, fixtures, farm machinery, airplanes, supplies and construction in progress as examples. Rental owners who keep appliances, tools or equipment for their Lenoir County units should read that list.

An account that listed last year receives its form in the mail automatically. If none arrives, the county says it is the owner's job to ask for one during regular office hours. Organizations seeking an exemption from personal property tax must file their application by January 31.

Before December ends, the tax office also mails abstract listings to every taxpayer who listed the year before. Listing real estate for the first time, such as a newly built house, is a call to the Tax Assessor's Office, which can explain what a new owner has to provide.

What happens to Lenoir County property tax when I sell?

State law fastens the lien to a parcel as of January 1, so an unpaid balance stays attached to the house until it is paid. At closing, the attorney or title company usually requests the figure from the Lenoir County Tax Department and pays it out of the seller's proceeds.

Personal property works differently. A lien for unpaid personal property tax can reach every parcel the taxpayer owns in that taxing unit, so an old boat or equipment bill may surface against a house. Boats, jet skis, aircraft, mobile homes and unlicensed vehicles are listed each January, with a 10 percent penalty for a late listing.

Real estate follows a permanent listing system in this county. A seller does not relist the house every year unless its value changed.

What happens if Lenoir County property tax goes unpaid?

To collect, the county can file a court action that mirrors a mortgage foreclosure, brought where the property is located. Owners of record, spouses and other lienholders receive notice.

The foreclosure sale is a public auction outside the courthouse. The steps after the bidding are short:

  • A bidder may be asked to put down as much as 20 percent.
  • The commissioner files a report on the sale within three days.
  • Ten days run from the report for anyone to object or raise the bid.
  • A fee of up to 5 percent of the price goes to the commissioner.
  • Before a judge confirms the sale, redemption is possible for whoever pays everything owed on the parcel.

The county tax page names a legal services contact for tax foreclosures. Anyone holding a notice should call the tax office and a legal aid provider promptly.

What are the housing and income figures for Lenoir County?

Lenoir County had an estimated 55,837 residents on July 1, 2025, down from 59,495 in the 2010 census, and it has 27,402 housing units across 399.09 square miles.

Survey data for 2020 to 2024 gives $120,500 as the middle value of a home that its owner occupies. Owner-occupancy stands at 59.2 percent. Rent in the county has a median of $861. Households earn a median $45,143. The poverty rate is 19.1 percent, and people 65 and over make up 22.4 percent of the county.

Monthly owner costs are a median $1,237 with a mortgage and $460 without one. At home values this modest, a tax bill is a real share of yearly housing cost, and back taxes can eat much of a house's equity. Only 131 building permits were issued in 2025, which leaves a resale competing mainly with other older houses.

More questions about Lenoir County, NC Property Tax Guide

Which phone number reaches Lenoir County tax staff?

The tax office answers at 252-527-7174, from its Kinston location at 101 North Queen Street, on weekdays from 8:30 until 5:00.

Is the Lenoir County real estate appeal period still open for 2026?

No. It closed April 23, 2026, when the Board of Equalization and Review adjourned. The county says the window for 2027 opens January 1, 2027.

Must a Lenoir County homeowner list the house each year?

No. The county runs a permanent listing system for real estate, so a house is relisted only after a change in value. Boats, aircraft and unlicensed vehicles need a January listing.

What does a late personal property listing cost in Lenoir County?

A 10 percent penalty. Listings made after the period ending January 31 are charged it, per the county tax page.

Can a house with unpaid Lenoir County tax be sold?

Yes. The balance is settled from the seller's proceeds when the sale closes. Ask the tax office for the figure ahead of signing, so it is printed on the settlement statement.

Lincoln County by the numbers

Who in Lincoln County runs the property tax system?

Everything starts at the Lincoln County Tax Department, third floor, 100 East Main Street, Lincolnton. Five divisions share the work: Land Records (maps and 9-1-1 addresses), GIS, Appraisal, Listing, and Collections.

The Tax Administrator carries responsibility for listing, appraising and assessing all real and personal property and for collecting what is owed. The same office processes exemption and exclusion requests. Appraisal staff take revaluation questions at (704) 736-8670.

The department's mission statement promises equal treatment of every owner, and its working yardstick is true market value: what a knowledgeable buyer and seller would settle on with no pressure on either side. The county measures that using the uniform appraisal standards in G.S. 105-283.

What is the Lincoln County property tax calendar from bill to penalty?

Each July the county mails bills to whoever held title on January 1. September 1 is the due date. Payment stays penalty-free through January 5, or through the next business day if January 5 is a Saturday or Sunday.

An account still open on January 6 gets a 2 percent penalty. From then on, each month adds three-fourths of one percent on its first day, and the county treats the balance as eligible for forced collection.

  • Pay between July 1 and August 31 and the county knocks 2 percent off.
  • Commissioners fix the rate by the end of June.
  • You may pay in pieces, and once this year's bill is closed you can start prepaying next year's.
  • Cash, checks, money orders, cards and e-checks all work, with a convenience fee on cards and e-checks.

Lenders with escrow accounts do not get mailed notices. Most pull what they need electronically, although the borrower still receives a paper notice for personal records.

What rates apply in Lincoln County for 2026/2027?

Every parcel carries the county rate of 0.499 per $100 of value, plus whatever its fire district or town levies. The county tax rate page prints a total for each district, so the right line depends on where the parcel sits.
