A separate availability fee of $140.00 applies per major structure, and $70.00 per major structure for OAE participants. Maiden levies its own town rate, so owners there should call town hall. The Denver, East Lincoln and North Brook fire districts print lower totals than the fire districts at High Shoals, so where a house sits changes the bill by more than the county rate alone.

Why does the 2027 revaluation matter to a Lincoln County seller?

Lincoln County chose by resolution to reappraise every four years, more often than the eight-year outer limit in G.S. 105-286. The last values date from January 1, 2023, and new ones arrive on January 1, 2027.

Before each cycle, appraisers study arm's-length sales, run statistical tests, and draft a Schedule of Values that the commissioners adopt. Transfers between relatives or related companies, foreclosure sales and gifts may be set aside, since they may not show open-market prices. The 2027 Schedule of Values, Standards, and Rules has been adopted and is posted for owners.

Notices of new value usually arrive in February. Under the county's own checklist, the figure is meant to track market value on that January 1, so pull your parcel record before choosing an asking price. Buyers will ask what it says.

How can a Lincoln County owner challenge an assessment?

Begin with an informal review, requested within 30 days of the notice date. Email revaluation@lincolncountync.gov, use the online form, phone (704) 736-8670, or mail the Appraisal Division at 100 East Main Street, Third Floor, Lincolnton, NC 28092.

When the informal answer stands, put a written request before the Board of Equalization and Review. A separate 30-day clock starts on the informal outcome. Five members and three alternates, named by the commissioners, sit on that board, and state law in G.S. 105-322 keeps its first session from falling before the first Monday of April. You hear the result in writing within a month.

After the board comes the Property Tax Commission, by written notice within 30 days, and then the Court of Appeals in the last stage. Keep in mind that any appeal can end with a value that is unchanged, lower or higher.

  • Helpful evidence: sales of comparable homes on or before the valuation date, similar parcels carrying lower values, photos of damage and repair bids.
  • Reasons the county lists as not grounds for appeal: high taxes, trouble paying, thin county services, or the size of the increase.
  • An outside appraisal helps only if it is dated before the valuation date, and the office does not advise buying one for this purpose.

Which relief programs can lower a Lincoln County tax bill?

State law gives three homestead options, and an owner can claim just one. File Form AV-9 with the county tax office; the state's instructions require the county to take it through June 1.

  • Age or disability: an exclusion equal to the larger of $25,000 or 50 percent of appraised value, open to owners 65 and up, or those permanently and totally disabled, earning no more than $38,800 for 2026.
  • Disabled veterans: the first $45,000 of appraised value is excluded, and NCDOR's form states there is no age or income limit.
  • Circuit breaker: a 4 percent of income ceiling when income is within the $38,800 limit, or 5 percent from there up to $58,200; the owner must have lived in the home five years, and any excess is deferred.

Landowners who farm or grow timber can ask the office about present-use value. It requires a 5-acre tract for horticulture, 10 for agriculture or 20 for forest, plus average gross income of $1,000 a year over three years for the first two uses.

What happens to Lincoln County taxes at closing?

County staff say the closing attorney ordinarily prorates the year's bill between the parties, so the seller bears the months of ownership. The settlement statement should show the proration, and your attorney can explain it.

Old balances do not disappear at closing. G.S. 105-355 treats the lien as attached on the listing date, and G.S. 105-374 allows a foreclosure action that works like a mortgage foreclosure and ends in a public sale at the courthouse. Redemption before confirmation costs the tax plus penalties, interest and court costs.

The 2020 to 2024 Census figures show 36,811 households of about 2.50 people each, and 90.3 percent of residents lived at the same address a year earlier. Stable ownership like that means some sellers carry an exclusion or deferral, so ask the Tax Department whether one is attached before you list. A circuit breaker deferral comes due for the previous three years when the owner sells.

More questions about Lincoln County, NC Property Tax Guide

What date does a Lincoln County tax bill become delinquent?

After January 5, with the penalty beginning January 6.

Is there a prepayment discount in Lincoln County?

Yes, 2 percent off for payments between July 1 and August 31. Bills usually reach mailboxes in early July.

When will Lincoln County values change next?

January 1, 2027 is the next reset, four years after the one dated January 1, 2023. Owners normally see new notices in February.

Where do I send a Lincoln County value appeal?

Write to revaluation@lincolncountync.gov or call the Appraisal Division at (704) 736-8670 within 30 days of the notice date. If that fails, take a formal appeal to the review board.

Who is responsible for Lincoln County taxes at closing?

The seller pays through the day of closing, since the attorney splits the year. Back taxes sit as a lien on the parcel and are cleared at the table.

Which Madison County office handles my tax bill?

Walk into Room 25 at 5707 Highway 25/70 in Marshall, or phone 828-649-0734, and you reach Madison County Tax Administration. Its posted weekday window is 8:00am to 5:00pm, with the office shut on Saturday and Sunday.

The county's assessor page splits the job into three parts. The assessor lists and values property, the county commissioners choose the rate, and a separate tax collector sends and collects the bills. Take a rate complaint to the commissioners and a value complaint to the assessor.

The county covers 449.62 land square miles with a 2020 density near 47 people per square mile. A Marshall town lot and a steep mountain tract sit on the same roll yet look nothing alike, so read your own parcel record before an offer arrives.

What rates did Madison County print for 2024-2025?

The county-wide rate on the posted sheet is 0.36 per $100 of value, with a fire district charge added for each parcel and a town charge where one applies. This sheet is headed 2024-2025, so request the one that matches your own bill.

How does the assessor arrive at a value in Madison County?

Three methods feed one number: cost, income and market. The assessor weighs what sellers and buyers have been doing and what construction costs, then settles on an assessed value for the parcel.

Land and buildings stay on the roll without re-listing. A homeowner reports only changes, such as an added garage or a demolished shed. Personal property gets listed each January, and the page names single-wide mobile homes, boats, farm machinery, unlicensed campers and unregistered vehicles.

  • The county contracts outside help for its periodic reappraisal.
  • Ownership changes and parcel maps are kept by the assessor.
  • A GIS system shows boundaries and aerial photography.
  • New structures need an E-911 address before a building permit issues.

Compare the record with what you actually own. An outbuilding missing from the card, or the wrong acreage, is simpler to correct now than in the middle of an inspection period.

What is the Madison County tax calendar?

Bills are payable from September 1, and face value is accepted into early January. After that a penalty clock runs.

  • January 1 to 31: listing window for personal property.
  • September 1: bills due.
  • January 6: a 2 percent charge is added.
  • February 1 onward: three-fourths of one percent more, monthly.

For mail, the postmark date is the payment date. Early-payer discounts are optional for counties and towns, so ask tax administration whether one is in force. The office's page also links to online payments.

How can a Madison County owner contest an assessment?

Complete the county's formal appeal form and send it to the Madison County Assessor's Office, 5707 US 25/70, Suite 3 Box 4, Marshall, NC 28753. The 2026 version asks for your value opinion as of January 1, 2024.

Expect questions on when you bought and for how much, the year built, fire insurance coverage, any inheritance or family sale, and improvements with their costs. Attach an independent appraisal if one exists. A house on the market needs the asking price and the broker's agreement attached, and rental property needs its latest three years of income and expense figures. Anyone filing for an owner submits an assessor-approved, notarized power of attorney.

The form is blunt that a bigger bill is no ground for appeal. Argue the value, using comparable sales and repair estimates.

Above the assessor sits the board of equalization and review, usually the commissioners themselves, which convenes in a window running from the first Monday in April to the first Monday in May. Request your hearing before it adjourns. Once its decision is mailed, the state Property Tax Commission is the next stop, with 30 days to file.

Which relief programs can reduce a Madison County bill?

The assessor's page names an elderly and disabled exclusion, an agricultural and forestry land use program and exemptions. An owner may draw on only one of the three state programs listed here.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: shields the larger of $25,000 or 50 percent of appraised value. Applicants are 65 or over, or permanently and totally disabled, with income at or under NCDOR's printed 2026 cap of $38,800.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: the first $45,000 of appraised value, with no age or income test on the form.
  • Circuit breaker: a 4 percent of income ceiling, rising to 5 percent when income falls between $38,800 and $58,200 (NCDOR's 2026 numbers). Owners must have lived there five years.

File Form AV-9 with the county assessor, who must take it through June 1. Circuit breaker applicants file again every year. See NCDOR Form AV-9.

What if a Madison County house sells with tax still owed?

The debt stays with the land. G.S. 105-355 attaches the lien at the listing date, penalties, interest and costs included, and the title agent will want it cleared when keys change hands.

Circuit breaker owners face one more item. Deferred tax from the previous three fiscal years comes due on a transfer, on the owner's death, or when the owner moves out. Madison County asks attorneys and paralegals for 10 days' notice so tax administration can produce deferred bills, which means a rushed closing can stall on paperwork.

Long-unpaid tax can end in a court foreclosure and a public auction, and tax administration's page links to those sales. Redeeming ahead of confirmation takes full payment of tax, penalties, interest and costs.

Who is selling a house in Madison County, and what do they face?

The Census Bureau's mid-2025 estimate is 22,553 people, 6.4 percent above the 2020 base. Seniors account for 25.3 percent of them, and 8,342 households average 2.50 persons. Median household income runs $58,531 in 2024 dollars.

Long-settled families produce plenty of back taxes, inherited mountain land and tired houses. These steps help in each case.

  • Request a statement for every parcel, with any deferred amount.
  • Check that the tax record and the deed show the same owner name.
  • Find out which relief or land use status the buyer would inherit.
  • Commission a survey first if the acreage is in doubt.

A cash buyer can settle the tax balance from the proceeds and skip the repair list, which fits owners who want out of an overdue parcel.

More questions about Madison County, NC Property Tax Guide

Who answers questions about Madison County property tax?

Call Madison County Tax Administration at 828-649-0734 or stop by Room 25, 5707 Highway 25/70, Marshall. It posts weekday hours, 8:00am to 5:00pm.

Which towns have their own rate in Madison County?

Marshall (0.355), Mars Hill (0.47) and Hot Springs (0.45) each add a charge on the 2024-2025 sheet. The 0.36 county rate covers every township.

Will a larger bill alone win an appeal in Madison County?

No. The 2026 form says a rising bill is not a valid reason. Your case must be about market value on the valuation date shown.

When does Madison County start charging interest on unpaid tax?

It begins on January 6 with a 2 percent charge. Beginning February 1, three-fourths of one percent more accrues monthly.

Can a Madison County owner close a sale with tax still due?

Yes. The lien gets paid from your proceeds at closing. Ask the tax office for a payoff early, and allow 10 days if deferred bills must be prepared.

With a typical home valued in six figures, even a small percentage error in the tax value repeats every year. Read your property record card against the house as you know it.

When does a Moore County tax bill turn late?

Bills fall due each September 1. State law sets the grace period in G.S. 105-360: a payment made before January 6 owes no interest, and a later one adds 2% through the end of January, then 0.75% a month.

January is also the listing season for personal property. Personal property, including business equipment, is listed each year, and real estate is listed permanently once it is on the books (G.S. 105-307). Statewide, owners list in January, with the window closing on the 31st unless an extension applies.

A fall sale does not cancel that year's bill. Ask the closing attorney whether the tax will be prorated or paid in full out of the proceeds.

How often is Moore County revalued?

Moore County revalues every four years. Its latest revaluation became effective January 1, 2023, and its FAQ schedules the next for 2027, then every fourth year, unless the market or state law calls for another timetable.

That beats the state floor of one reappraisal every eight years, and counties may shorten the cycle by resolution (G.S. 105-286).

Values come from mass appraisal using the cost, market and income approaches, fixed to January 1 of the revaluation year. They do not follow the market between revaluations. An appraiser may still visit after a building permit, a parcel map change, or a recorded sale priced well away from the assessment. Permit data flows in from the county plus Aberdeen, Pinebluff, Pinehurst and Southern Pines.

Added heated floor area is an improvement, as are decks, porches, patios, storage buildings, pools and barns, and the owner is expected to report them.

How does a Moore County value challenge work?

Send the Tax Department a signed written request or the county appeal form. For real estate the window opens each January 1 and shuts when the county's review board adjourns, a date the county advertises in the local newspaper.

Moore County appeal paths by property type
Property typeWhen to appealHow
Real propertyOpens January 1, ends at board adjournmentSigned request or appeal form, informal review first, then the board
Personal property, business or notThirty days counted from the bill dateSigned written request or personal property form
Registered motor vehicleThirty days counted from the bill dateSigned written request; pay the bill on time regardless

You must show that the value is higher than surrounding properties justify, or higher than fair market value, using cost, sales or income evidence from the run-up to the revaluation date.

If the board rules against you, the next stop is the state-level Property Tax Commission, which needs written notice filed within thirty days after the decision is mailed (G.S. 105-290).

What tax relief can Moore County homeowners claim?

Three state programs can reduce the bill on a permanent residence, and an owner can draw on only one. Moore County owners apply through the county tax office.

  • Elderly or disabled homestead exclusion: whichever is bigger, a flat $25,000 or one half of appraised value, comes off the taxable amount for an owner who has reached age 65, or who is totally and permanently disabled, within the income limit (G.S. 105-277.1).
  • Disabled veteran homestead exclusion: $45,000 of value is excluded, with nothing asked about age or income (G.S. 105-277.1C).
  • Circuit breaker: the bill is capped at 4% of income for owners at or under the limit, or 5% for incomes up to 150% of it, and the excess is deferred as a lien (G.S. 105-277.1B).

The state revenue department lists, for 2026, $38,800 as the income limit and $58,200 as the 150% mark. Form AV-9 goes to the county, ideally during listing, and the county must accept it up to June 1 before that tax year starts.

A sale or move triggers repayment of the circuit breaker deferral for the prior three fiscal years, so include it in the closing payoff.

Can I sell a Moore County house that still has tax due?

Yes, but the tax follows the parcel, so it is settled at closing. A lien for real property tax attaches on the listing date (G.S. 105-355), and the county can enforce it by foreclosure, which is described in G.S. 105-374.

A tax foreclosure runs like a mortgage foreclosure action in the county court. The house is sold at auction on the courthouse steps, and an owner may still redeem ahead of confirmation by paying the tax with its penalties and costs.

Selling before that point usually costs less. Ask the Tax Department for a payoff, look for any open town bill, and hand the figure to the closing attorney.

How does Moore County set the value of a particular house?

Every parcel is valued under the 2023 Schedule of Values adopted by the Board of Commissioners, using the features the house had on January 1 of the year in question. The appraiser records those features on a Field Review Document, and owners can pull that document or a shorter property record card from the county GIS site or from the Tax Department.

The land records team builds the ownership side from the paperwork that reaches the recorder's counter or the Clerk of Court, and it also keeps the parcel data that the GIS maps display. Mass appraisal means one set of standard methods is applied to a whole group of properties, then tested statistically. No single appraiser sets a price house by house.

  • Check the square footage, bedroom and bath counts and outbuildings on your card.
  • Look at what similar houses on your street are valued at.
  • Bring sales, cost or income evidence if you disagree, since the proof rests on you.
  • Remember that a recorded sale far from the assessment can trigger a visit.

For a seller, a clean card means fewer surprises when a buyer's agent compares your tax value to the contract price.

More questions about Moore County, NC Property Tax Guide

What are my payment options?

You can pay at the Carthage courthouse counter, through the mail, on the county website, or over the phone at 1-855-451-2620. The counter takes cash, checks and plastic, and card payments add a convenience fee.

What year did the last Moore County revaluation take effect?

January 1, 2023. The county has the next one scheduled for 2027, with four-year rounds after that.

How long can I contest a vehicle or personal property value?

The window is thirty days from the bill's date. Send a signed written request to the Tax Department, and pay a vehicle bill on time anyway so no late penalty builds.

Do Moore County values rise and fall with the market each year?

No. The county fixes value on the revaluation year's January 1 date and leaves it alone in between. New improvements can still draw an appraiser and change the figure.

Who accepts the elderly or disabled exclusion application?

With the county tax office, on Form AV-9. The state prefers it during January listing but takes it up to June 1 before the new tax year starts, and a household can use just one of the three programs.

Nash County by the numbers

Which Nash County office sends and collects the tax bill?

One combined office serves as both assessor and collector in Nash County. It lists and values real and personal property, assesses it and collects the resulting tax. Find it at 120 W. Washington St., Suite 2058, Nashville, NC 27856, and you can call 252-459-9824 during the business day, which starts at eight in the morning and ends at five

Relief applications under state law also go through this office. The Collections page explains that the collector handles money, while questions about listing, billing and assessed values belong with the assessor's staff.

The county commissioners adopt the rate in spring, by June 30 at the latest, and a bill multiplies that rate by each $100 of taxable value. Mailing happens in July or August. An owner with no statement by September 15 should call the collector.

How do Nash County's numbers compare on housing?

Federal estimates give Nash County about 99,365 residents in mid-2025, a 4.6% gain over 2020. Land area is 540.44 square miles, so the 2020 density was nearly 176 people on each one.

  • A typical owner-occupied house is valued at $191,000 in the 2020-2024 survey.
  • Households owning their home: 63.6%.
  • Typical monthly rent: $953.
  • Total homes and apartments by mid-2025: 45,068.
  • Average trip to a job: 23.7 minutes.
  • Veterans among residents (2020-2024): 5,784.

Since 63.6% of households own, a meaningful share of Nash County houses are rentals. A landlord should remember that the county bills the January 1 titleholder, whatever the tenant pays.

What dates and penalties apply to a Nash County tax bill?

The county sets September 1 as the due date and January 5 as the final day before interest starts. If January 5 is a Saturday or Sunday, payment is accepted through the following working day. A postmark dated by the cutoff counts, and the county advises mailing a full week early.

Unpaid realty and personal property accounts pick up 2% for January and then 0.75% for each later month, which tracks G.S. 105-360. Registered motor vehicles are handled separately, at 5% for the first month past due.

  • Delinquent real estate may be advertised in local papers between March 1 and June 30, with the advertising cost charged to the owner.
  • The county lists garnishment of wages, attachment of bank accounts or rents, foreclosure, and offsets against state income tax refunds.
  • Prepayments toward a coming bill are accepted, and staff can explain the terms.

Who pays the Nash County tax after a house changes hands?

A seller remains liable for the year's bill. Per the county, the legal obligation sits with whoever held title on January 1, and a later sale does not wipe it out.

Proration normally happens at closing, so confirm with your agent or closing attorney that it did. For certainty, you can direct the check to the Tax Collector's Office from the closing table, and if the current bill is not yet due, the collector takes a prepayment computed at last year's rate.

State lien law reinforces this: the lien reaches the parcel on the listing date, as G.S. 105-355, and no buyer or lender will want title with it still open. Once a closing date exists, ask the county tax office to put the amount owed in writing.

What steps does a Nash County assessment appeal follow?

An informal appeal comes first, and only if it fails does the dispute reach the county review board. No taxpayer may skip a step, says the county's revaluation page.

The informal step can be started four ways.

  • By appointment, face to face with an appraiser at the West Washington Street office in Nashville.
  • Over the phone, once an appraiser agrees to call you back.
  • By post: fill in the bottom of the appeal notice and send it with your documents to the Tax Office, marked for the Board of Equalization and Review.
  • On the web, using the county's online informal appeal form.

Once the informal answer arrives, you have a thirty-day window after the notice date to go formal, and you must prove the value is wrong. Under G.S. 105-322 the board's opening session comes in the spring window the statute sets, April into early May.

The board weighs fairness and accuracy of the value, and the county's FAQ says it ignores whether you can afford the tax. Neighbors' comparable properties with lower assessments make the strongest evidence. A denial can move on to the Property Tax Commission, with written notice due a month after the ruling is mailed (G.S. 105-290).

Which relief programs does Nash County offer?

The county's Tax page names four: the elderly and permanently disabled exclusion, the disabled veterans' exclusion, the circuit breaker deferment and the builder's inventory exclusion. Request an application at (252) 459-1222 or download one from the tax forms page.

Key filing dates on the Nash County Tax page
ItemDeadline or rule
Elderly or disabled, disabled veterans, circuit breakerApplication due June 1
Builders' inventory and other reliefFiling due June 1
Other exemptions for classified parcels (Form AV-10)Filing due January 31
Personal and business personal property listingForms in hand by January 31, or a 10% late penalty
Property tax dueSeptember 1

The state revenue department lists $38,800 as the 2026 income limit for the elderly or disabled exclusion and circuit breaker, with $58,200 as the ceiling for the higher circuit breaker tier. For the elderly or disabled exclusion, whichever is greater, a flat $25,000 or half the home's appraised value, comes off the assessment (G.S. 105-277.1), and a disabled veteran can exclude $45,000 of value, regardless of age or income.

How does a revaluation work in Nash County?

State law sets eight years as the longest gap between reappraisals, each effective January 1 of the scheduled year (G.S. 105-286). Nash County's own page describes the purpose as an accurate and equitable assessment of every parcel.

The county's revaluation page describes a project covering more than 53,000 parcels, carried out with an outside firm, Piner Appraisal, whose appraisers also take informal appeals. Each owner is mailed the new assessed value, and the thirty days run from the date on that notice.

The county defines market value as the price a willing, able buyer and seller would settle on with neither under pressure, and it excludes foreclosure and family sales. If your own sale was one of those, bring different comparables.

What else does the Nash County tax office handle besides real estate bills?

The collector's side of the office also deals with vehicles, business owners and utility customers, useful to know when you are closing out a household or a rental.

  • Bills for registered motor vehicles go out monthly instead of in the fall, and they have their own interest rule.
  • Business licenses are issued through the Tax Collector's Office.
  • Personal and business personal property forms must be in the office by the end of January, and a late listing carries a 10% penalty.
  • Check or cash payments for county water and sewer bills can be made at the Tax Collections Office in the administrative building in Nashville during regular business hours.

The county's Register of Deeds also sits in the same administrative building, on the third floor at 120 W. Washington Street, so a seller can record a deed and ask the tax office about a payoff in one trip.

More questions about Nash County, NC Property Tax Guide

What is the Nash County due date?

September 1 starts the payment period, and it runs through January 5 (extended past a weekend January 5). Interest of 2% then applies for January, followed by 0.75% each month.

If I sell partway through the year, do I still owe that year's tax?

Yes, unless it is settled at closing. The county treats the person who held title on January 1 as legally responsible, and a sale does not change that. Proration is typical, or you can pay the Tax Collector directly at the table.

How can I challenge my Nash County assessment?

Begin with an informal appeal, by phone, post, web form or in person. If the answer disappoints you, file a formal appeal with the Board of Equalization and Review thirty days after the date shown on the informal result.

When must Nash County relief applications arrive?

June 1 is the date for elderly or disabled, disabled veteran, circuit breaker and builders' inventory applications. Classified-parcel exemptions on Form AV-10 are due January 31.

How steep is the Nash County late listing penalty?

It is 10%. Personal and business personal property forms must reach the county by January 31, and late ones carry that penalty as the law requires.
